Metal Dragons.title: Slayer task/Metal dragons

infobox.otherReq: Partial completion of Dragon Slayer I

Metal Dragons.intro:
Metal dragons can be assigned by high-levelled slayer masters as a potential task.

Players have many options for killing these dragons:

• Bronze dragons - found in Brimhaven Dungeon and the Catacombs of Kourend. The lowest level option.
• Iron dragons - found in the same locations as bronze dragons. More plentiful. Can also be found in the Isle of Souls dungeon.
• Steel dragons - found in Brimhaven Dungeon and the Catacombs of Kourend.
• Mithril dragons - found in the Ancient Cavern, requiring completion of the first part of the Firemaking section of the Barbarian Training miniquest.
• Adamant dragons - found in Lithkren Vault, requiring completion of Dragon Slayer II in order to access.
• Rune dragons - same as above.

Of these dragons, only mithril dragons cannot be cannoned. All metal dragons are capable of using melee and long range dragonfire, which rolls differently compared to chromatic dragonfire. Unlike chromatic dragons, where Protect from Magic would block most of the damage, metal dragons aren't affected by it, thus making an anti-dragon shield mandatory if not using a super antifire potion. Mithril, adamant and rune dragons are also able to use both magic and ranged, with the latter two additionally having a special ranged attack that mimics ruby and onyx enchanted bolts respectively.

As with all dragons, metal dragons have the draconic attribute, making them susceptible to the dragon hunter lance, dragon hunter crossbow and dragon hunter wand. They are also weakest to stab and heavy ranged attacks, although the higher levelled metal dragons are more resistant to the latter. Additionally, all of these dragons have a 50% vulnerability to earth spells.

If players are seeking a fast task of dragons, they are recommended to kill bronze dragons at Brimhaven Dungeon's slayer-only area, where five of them can be found in a small area which is cannonable. Alternatively, iron dragons may be cannoned instead if seeking the draconic visage, as bronze dragons do not drop them and iron dragons are still fairly easy to kill. If seeking profit, kill rune dragons instead. It is not recommended to kill other dragons apart from collection log purposes. Metal dragons as a slayer task also have an incredibly high weight value (the most out of all potential tasks) so players should determine whether or not to block them depending on what tasks they are looking for.

Abyssal Demon.title: Slayer task/Abyssal demons

infobox.otherReq: Priest in Peril or Fairytale II - Cure a Queen

Abyssal Demon.intro:
At level 85 Slayer and Combat level, the player may be assigned Abyssal demons by mid and high levelled Slayer Masters and Krystilia. They can be found in the Abyssal Area, the Catacombs of Kourend, the Wilderness Slayer Cave, and in the Slayer Tower, where they are found on the third floor and in the task-only basement.

Abyssal demons use a fairly accurate melee stab attack, but with a relatively low max hit of 8. With Bigger and badder unlocked, the Greater abyssal demon has a chance to spawn as a Superior slayer monster. The greater abyssal demon is much more powerful and accurate with a max hit of 27. Protect from Melee will neutralise all damage taken from either variation.

Players on abyssal demon tasks may also opt to kill the Abyssal Sire boss instead, which can be very profitable as compensation for significantly lower experience rates compared to Abyssal demons.

Abyssal demons have a unique mechanic in which they frequently teleport around the area they're being attacked in. They also have a high chance to teleport the player up to 20 tiles away. It is highly recommended to acquire and read a Teleport anchoring scroll before fighting Abyssal demons for the first time, as this will eliminate the chance for the player to be teleported. If the player doesn't have access to the anchoring scroll, it is recommended to enable Auto Retaliate to continue attacking after being teleported. The greater abyssal demon also teleports around the player, and afterward will always land a successful hit if its attack is not prayed against. By having only two open sides through backing yourself into a corner, you can maximize multi-target ice spells since they will no longer be able to teleport behind you. This is best combined with either goading potions in the Catacombs of Kourend or a dwarf multicannon in the Wilderness Slayer Cave.

Abyssal demons are Demons, meaning they are subject to the various accuracy and damage bonuses of Demonbane Weaponry including Arclight, Emberlight, the Scorching bow, and Demonbane spells, although generally, these are not used in favour of damage dealt through area of effect damage.

Because they potentially offer high rates of Slayer experience, players should extend Abyssal demons as soon as possible.

The drop table for Abyssal demons is generally unremarkable with a few exceptions. They drop the Abyssal whip at a 1/512 rate, and therefore will drop an average of one whip every other extended task. They are also one of the only sources of the Abyssal dagger, but this is an extremely rare drop. Ensouled abyssal heads will appear several times in a task, making a Soul bearer useful. The Herb sack will also allow the player to profit further, and an Explorer's ring 4 may be used for the few alchable items among their drops. Abyssal demons in the Catacombs of Kourend also have access to that location's drop table which includes pieces of the Dark totem. Greater abyssal demons in the Catacombs will always drop a piece of the Dark totem.
Abyssal Demon.strategy:
The Wilderness Slayer Cave is the only location in which a Cannon can be used against Abyssal demons, although as part of the Wilderness, it is also a Player killing hotspot. The Wilderness Slayer Cave also allows taking advantage of cheaper Blighted supplies and the passive effects of the Accursed sceptre (a) and other weapons charged with Revenant ether.

With their 1x1 size, Abyssal demons are ideal for use with area of effect weapons including the Venator bow and Ancient Magicks. The Catacombs and Wilderness Slayer Cave are the only two Multicombat areas with Abyssal demons. As Abyssal demons are not aggressive, a method to cause them to attack the player, such as Dinh's bulwark or a Goading potion, is recommended.

Because of the teleportation mechanic, Smoke Barrage or Smoke Burst are favoured over their Ice equivalents. After teleporting away, frozen abyssal demons will not move back toward the player until they're unfrozen. Blood spells are significantly more expensive than Smoke and are not recommended.

Killing Abyssal demons outside multicombat areas, usually done only on a Konar task, will result in a slower task requiring more attention. If required to kill Abyssal demons in a single combat zone, it's recommended to use an Expeditious bracelet with a melee setup.

If the player is comfortable with the risk, Abyssal demons in the Wilderness Slayer Cave will provide some of the best rates of Slayer experience in the game. Abyssal demons in the Catacombs are still an outstanding source of experience.

By having only two open sides through backing yourself into a corner, you can maximize multi-target ice spells since they will no longer be able to teleport behind you. This is best combined with either goading potions in the Catacombs of Kourend or a dwarf multicannon in the Wilderness Slayer Cave.

equipment.name: Catacombs magic
equipment.text:
This is the recommended equipment for barraging or bursting abyssal demons in the Catacombs of Kourend.

Abyssal demons in the Catacombs are excellent experience due to the AoE effect of ancients; The chambers contain plenty of spawns that can be grouped together for barraging or bursting, making them highly suited for multitarget strategies. This means they're some of the highest slayer experience in the game, and therefore the bracelet of slaughter is preferable over a tormented bracelet or confliction gauntlet as it will increase task length. This is especially true for player looking to train their slayer and magic levels.

Because abyssal demons have low magic defence, magic damage and prayer bonus should be prioritised over magic accuracy. Magic attack bonuses are far less important than damage multipliers.

equipment.name: Wilderness slayer cave
equipment.text:
The cannon will not be lost if you die while it is placed on the ground.

The accursed sceptre (a) is notable here, as it provides a 50% boost to both Magic accuracy and damage against any NPC in the Wilderness, making it a powerful option. This effect stacks with the slayer helmet (i). Players should 3-item, or 4-item if using Protect Item, keeping only their sceptre and a few key magic strength pieces as their core items that are kept on death. The rest of the setup can consist of inexpensive equipment, such as monk's robes, bracelet of slaughter, and free items like the completed book of darkness.

Blighted supplies are recommended for food and prayer restoration as well as blighted ice sacks. This is because they are inexpensive and top tier, but can only be used in the wilderness.

equipment.name: Melee
equipment.text:
Meleeing abyssal demons offers good experience and easily allows the player access to the Arceuus spellbook for offering spells, thralls, and death charge. If in the Slayer tower bonus experience will also be awarded, scaling with completion of the Morytania Diary.

Use of demonbane weaponry like Arclight or Emberlight is strongly recommended for highest damage output.

Dark Beast.title: Slayer task/Dark beast
Dark Beast.intro:
Dark beasts can be killed with Melee, Magic or Ranged. Melee is the most effective against them and should be used in conjunction with high prayer bonus armour, such as Proselyte armour, for Protect from Melee. To maximise profit, players should bring a herb sack and a gem bag so that they can loot all herbs and gems they receive.

Dark beasts are good point-gaining tasks as they are not assigned in large numbers; even the extension doesn't give as much as other monsters, though this is balanced by their large health pool.

Dark beasts are a unique monster in that they are permanently aggressive towards the player no matter how long they stay there for. They will only use Magic as their first attack if they are attacked by the player first, or if they cannot attack the player with Melee. As such, while they can be hit with a dwarf multicannon, it is not recommended to bring one. Not much attention is required for killing them, apart from restoring prayer, though players who have unlocked Superior slayer monsters will need to pay attention for any night beasts that spawn. Unlike their normal brethren, they are not aggressive and will always initiate with a magic attack even if forced to be made aggressive.

Araxyte.title: Slayer task/Araxytes
Araxyte.intro:
Araxytes are a potential slayer assignment from Nieve/Steve, Duradel/Kuradal, and Mortimer, after completion of Priest in Peril. Turael/Aya and Spria can also assign them, albeit indirectly as a spiders task. They require 92 Slayer in order to be harmed and are found exclusively in the Morytania Spider Cave.

Araxytes attack with melee, and are also able to inflict venom starting at 6 damage, therefore, it is recommended to bring venom immunity to all encounters, preferably extended anti-venom+ for long trips. They are fairly far from a bank, though a spider cave teleport will bring players to the entrance of the cave.

Hellhound.title: Slayer task/Hellhounds
Hellhound.intro:
Hellhounds can be assigned as a slayer task at 65 combat level by various Slayer masters. They can be found in a variety of locations around Gielinor. The task is very straightforward as regular hellhounds only attack with their fairly accurate melee bites; it is recommended to either safespot them or keep Protect from Melee on at all times. Hellhounds are primarily known for their high drop rate of hard clue scrolls, at a rate of 1/64, or 1/32 if killing in the Wilderness with a imbued ring of wealth. They also drop ensouled hellhound heads and the smouldering stone.

Outside of the Wilderness, hellhounds are primarily killed in the Stronghold Slayer Cave for general slayer, as there are four rooms of three or four hellhounds in each one, and a dwarf multicannon can be set up in their caves. They may also be killed in the Catacombs of Kourend for ancient shards and dark totem pieces. The catacombs do not allow for a cannon, but is a Multicombat area and allows for relative AFK training, especially with a Venator bow, and is also quite close to the entrance. Once the aggression timer expires, the player can simply run south and up the vine to the Giants' Den to reset aggression. Some players opt to restore prayer at an altar and teleport back to this location using Xeric's talisman's Xeric's Heart option or the Kourend Castle Teleport spell (requires 48 Magic and completion of Client of Kourend to unlock the spell).

In the Wilderness, hellhounds are primarily killed in the Wilderness Slayer Cave, with a group of five slightly stronger hellhounds in a multicombat area. The drop rate of the smouldering stone from these hellhounds is increased by 50%, and they have access to the Wilderness Slayer Cave drop table, which can help offset some supply costs. However, the cave itself is a very popular player killing hotspot despite the hellhounds being below level 20 Wilderness, and players killing them here should not bring any items they are unwilling to lose. These hellhounds are generally killed if assigned by Krystilia.

Revenant hellhounds do not count towards a normal hellhound task, despite being ghostly hellhounds.

Alternatives for normal hellhounds include the skeleton hellhounds summoned by Calvar'ion/Vet'ion respectively. While the main boss itself is obviously not a hellhound, players can progress through the task with the boss' spawns and make reasonable profit at the same time. Every boss kill will spawn four hellhounds in total, two pre-enrage and another two post-enrage. However, the bosses are also popular player killing hotspots and players should not bring any items they are unwilling to lose.

A final alternative is Cerberus for players who have 91 Slayer or higher, with a minimum of 86 with a wild pie boost. Cerberus is much stronger than other hellhounds, with additional mechanics, and a chance at valuable unique drops. It is recommended that a player has access to the Ward of Arceuus spell and either an Arclight, Emberlight, or Scythe of Vitur to kill Cerberus, as worse setups may offer considerably less (or even negative) profit. This is due to her summoned souls attack (which drains up to 90 prayer, reduced to 60 with Ward of Arceuus, if successfully prayed against) resulting in higher than expected usage of prayer potions.

Ensouled hellhound heads can be sent to the bank with a charged Soul bearer, or resummoned on the spot for additional prayer experience.

Lizardmen.title: Slayer task/Lizardmen
Lizardmen.intro:
Lizardman can be assigned as a Slayer task after being unlocked at a cost of 75 Slayer reward points via the Reptile got ripped ability.

Normal lizardmen come in three forms; a plain level 53 and 62 variant, and the level 75 lizardman brute. These are simple enemies and have a weak poison that starts at 3 damage. They have very few lucrative drops, so these variants are primarily killed for the sake of speeding through a task with a cannon, often at the Lizardman Canyon due to it being a multicombat area.

The stronger shamans can be found in more sparse locations, and are more commonly killed as they drop the valuable dragon warhammer, which is popular for players who cannot acquire an elder maul. Lizardmen shamans require the use of Shayzien armour in order to kill them, as they have a unique poison spit that can deal up to 30 damage, which is fully blocked while wearing a full set of tier 5 shayzien armour. They also have various mechanics that make them harder to kill, though they are still easily dealt with using a ranged weapon and Protect from Missiles.

When killing shamans it is highly recommended to do so at the Lizardman Temple as the AoE explosion from their spawns are reduced from 5x5 to 3x3 due to the small size of the temple chambers. It is also recommended that players complete the Hard Kourend & Kebos Diary to unlock a toggle from Captain Cleive that allows the Slayer helmet to act as a variant of the Shayzien helmet (Note: this requires having access to a Shayzien helm (5) first.), allowing the bonuses from the Slayer helmet to apply onto the shamans.

Killing any variant of lizardmen while on a normal Lizard task will NOT progress the task.

TzHaar.title: Slayer task/TzHaar
TzHaar.intro:
TzHaar are an ancient race dwelling underneath the Karamja Volcano in Mor Ul Rek that can be assigned as a Slayer task if the player has unlocked the perk Hot Stuff for 100 slayer points.

TzHaar come in four varieties: the artisans TzHaar-Hur, the sages TzHaar-Mej, hunters TzHaar-Xil, and guards TzHaar-Kets. Killing any of these while wearing a ring of wealth increases their chances of dropping gems (and Onyx bolt tips for level 221 TzHaar-Kets).

The Hur and Ket primarily attack with melee, while the Xil can use either melee or ranged, depending on the weapon they are using; those wielding Toktz-xil-ul (resembling a throwing disc) will be able to use both styles, while those wielding Toktz-xil-ak or Toktz-xil-eks use only melee. TzHaar-Mej attack with magic.

Players killing TzHaar are recommended to kill the Ket or melee-using Xil, as they are easily safespotted through the many vents littering Mor Ul Rek. Attacking a Hur will cause all nearby TzHaar to attack the player, while attacking a Mej will cause nearby Xil and Ket to attack the player. When facing Ket, the player can also choose to kill the stronger level 221 variants in the inner area of the city, who can also drop pieces of obsidian armour. Accessing this inner area requires the player to show a fire cape to the Ket guards standing by the gates leading inside.

When offered an assignment of TzHaar, the Slayer master may instead allow the player to kill TzTok-Jad or TzKal-Zuk, with the latter requiring that the player has at least one TzKal-Zuk kill count. This can be further increased to two and three kills per task with the completion of the master and grandmaster combat achievement tiers respectively. While completing these tasks, the player will obtain slayer experience from every volcanic creature killed in their respective area and benefits from the slayer helmet's bonus for the entire run. If the player dies or leaves, the task is cancelled and no points are used.

A single kill of TzTok-Jad awards 37,010 slayer experience (25,250 from Jad and 11,760 from the pre-wave monsters, including the four healers), while a single kill of TzKal-Zuk yields ~125,000 experience (depending on how many cycles of monsters spawn while fighting Zuk, and the amount of both Jad and Zuk healers killed); 101,890 experience comes from Zuk, and the remaining from pre-wave monsters. Killing them on a slayer task not only speeds up kill times, but also increases the drop rate of their respective pets by 50% and 25%, making them much more rewarding for pet hunters.

Black Dragon.title: Slayer task/Black dragons

infobox.otherReq: Partial completion of Dragon Slayer I

Black Dragon.intro:
Black dragons can be assigned as a slayer task at level 80 combat by various Slayer masters (or at any combat level by Krystilia) after partial completion of Dragon Slayer I.

Black dragons are the rarest of chromatic dragons. As with all other chromatic dragons, they use melee and short-ranged dragonfire. When killing the standard variant of Black dragons, its recommended to use Protect from Melee and basic dragonfire protection (such as an anti-dragon shield and extended antifire potion), as the dragons are quite accurate and hit relatively hard.

Players can additionally kill baby black dragons, brutal black dragons, or the King Black Dragon as alternatives for a black dragon task.

While most variants of black dragons can be very profitable to kill, optimal strategies involve either quickly killing baby black dragons (as they are easily accessible in Taverley Dungeon with the task-only area) or brutal black dragons (which require 77 Slayer).

Cave Kraken.title: Slayer task/Cave krakens
Cave Kraken.intro:
Cave kraken can be assigned from level 87 Slayer. They are exclusively found within Kraken Cove.

Cave krakens have low value drops and are generally only killed for their uncharged trident which has a 1/200 drop rate. The Noxious Halberd can reach them, however it will deal no damage. They also take reduced damage from ranged attacks, so they should be fought with Magic using earth spells due to their elemental weakness. Damage can be protected against with Protect from Magic.

Alternatively, the Kraken boss can be fought. Magic is also used, but Kraken's typeless attacks means that the damage cannot be prayed against. The fight is very simple and it has a fairly generous drop table. Fishing explosives are recommended to initiate the fight quickly, and can be easily obtained from any Slayer Master.

For more information on killing Kraken, see Kraken/Strategies.

Dagannoth.title: Slayer task/Dagannoth
Dagannoth.intro:
Dagannoth are a slayer task assigned by the advanced Slayer masters. Requiring completion of Horror from the Deep to be assigned, dagannoth are known for their high slayer experience rates and easy task completions. For players who are seeking a more difficult challenge, the Dagannoth Kings are a viable alternative for players of moderate to experienced combat ability.

The weaker variant of dagannoth can be found within the Lighthouse basement, Jormungand's Prison, and the Catacombs of Kourend. In the first two locations, a dwarf cannon can be used very effectively as the area is multicombat. For players who wish to maximise AFK time without relying on prayer, the lighthouse is a good choice. Otherwise, it is best to kill them in the prison or catacombs, as these two locations only house melee-using dagannoth. When killing the dagannoth in the Lighthouse, players can sell noted food to Jossik in the Lighthouse and buy it back in unnoted form for a small amount of money.

Players with prayer-boosting melee gear and a decent amount of prayer potions are able to AFK dagannoth within the Catacombs of Kourend with Auto Retaliate turned on. The only actions that require attention are restoring prayer points and walking away and back into the area should dagannoth become tolerant towards the player. While players cannot use a dwarf cannon in the Catacombs of Kourend, players can also use a Dinh's Bulwark special attack in conjunction with the 50% special attack regeneration from an equipped Lightbearer ring. Using the special attack from Dinh's Bulwark will help maintain enemy aggression without needing to leave the area to reset the aggression timer.

If players are assigned to kill dagannoth at Waterbirth Island, the only ideal spot would be the main area in the first floor, as the other areas have far too little dagannoth despite being in a multicombat area. The dagannoth here are much stronger compared to other locations, though the player can speed up the task once every few minutes by triggering dagannoth spawn to emerge from the nearby eggs. This will only work while the dagannoth are aggressive, since the eggs will not hatch otherwise.

For players seeking a more rewarding experience, the player can choose to kill the Dagannoth Kings, assuming that the player is on a normal dagannoth task or assigned by Konar quo Maten to slay dagannoth at the dungeon. It is highly recommended that players have 80 Agility and have completed the Elite Fremennik Diary, as both of these will make the trek to the Kings significantly easier; a level 85 shortcut (boostable) that bypasses the need for a pet rock and rune thrownaxe, and a level 81 shortcut farther ahead, both of which cut the run time by ~85%. It is not recommended to kill the Kings on a task without completion of the Elite Fremennik Diary, as this will note their unique bone drop which accounts for the majority of profit.

Finally, players can use a dagannoth task as an opportunity to train Prayer through use of the Expert Reanimation Arceuus spell, if not killing them as part of Konar's task (though heads dropped by dagannoth in the assigned location will still count). Casting this spell on an ensouled dagannoth head within range of the Dark Altar will summon a reanimated dagannoth, which gives a good amount of prayer experience, though combat and slayer experience will suffer as a result.

Dagannoth frequently drop herb seeds. The use of a seed box is recommended.

Greater Demon.title: Slayer task/Greater demons
Greater Demon.intro:
Greater demons can be assigned by Krystilia, Chaeldar, Konar, Nieve/Steve, and Duradel/Kuradal. Despite their "greater" status, they possess a somewhat lackluster drop table, with their two most valuable drops being the rune full helm and the hard clue scroll. There are many different types of greater demons residing around Gielinor; however, with the exception of the Wilderness Slayer Cave, all have the same drop table.

When not killing greater demons as part of Konar or Krystilia's tasks, players have many spots to choose from. The most common spots are the Chasm of Fire and Catacombs of Kourend. The Chasm of Fire is a cannonable area in a small space, allowing for plenty of AFK and fast kill times, along with contracts for challenging a stronger version of Yama. Catering to the increased drop rates will require more banking and less AFK time, however. The Catacombs of Kourend has access to the ancient shard and dark totem piece drops. It is also a Multicombat area, allowing for players to AFK until the aggression timer expires, which can be easily reset.

In the Wilderness, players have several spots to kill greater demons from. The most common would be the Wilderness Slayer Cave due to the enhanced drops, multiway area and allowing a cannon, but this spot is frequented often by player killers, so players should not bring items they are not willing to lose. The Demonic Ruins is a much worse spot, due to being a far deeper multiway area and players tend to teleport in via Annakarl Teleports. A more secluded spot is the Lava Maze Dungeon, but accessing it requires a long trek around the maze, or 82 Agility (boostable at 77) for a shortcut that cuts a significant amount of time.

Players who have completed While Guthix Sleeps may also kill Tormented Demons for the progression of a greater demon task. These are a significant step up compared to normal greater demons and require a minimum of two combat styles in order to be fought. They provide extremely good experience rates (with each kill being 1,065 slayer experience) and can drop the valuable tormented synapse, which is used to create high tier, best-in-slot demonbane weaponry, which makes them worth it for ironmen that frequently kill demonic creatures. See their strategy page on more information on how to fight them.

The bosses Skotizo (guide) and K'ril Tsutsaroth (guide) also count towards greater demons for the purpose of a slayer task. Skotizo requires a dark totem in order to access. He drops clue scrolls, making it a great option for players that want to complete some Treasure Trails. K'ril requires a minimum of level 70 Hitpoints and partial completion of Troll Stronghold in order to access. His bodyguard Tstanon Karlak also counts as a greater demon.

Kalphite.title: Slayer task/Kalphites
Kalphite.intro:
Kalphites can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 15 combat by all Slayer masters, with the exception of Mortimer and the Wilderness Slayer master Krystilia. Kalphites come in a wide variety of levels, which is why they are possible tasks from nearly all Slayer masters. They can be found in the Kalphite Lair in the north-west Kharidian Desert, as well as in a Slayer task-exclusive area, the Kalphite Cave, just east of Shantay Pass.

Kalphites comes in four varieties: workers, soldiers, and guardians, as well as the boss monster the Kalphite Queen. With the exception of the Queen, all Kalphites use melee attacks. Additionally the soldiers and guardians can induce poison starting at 4 and 6 Hitpoints damage respectively. This poison bypasses protection prayers. Protect from Melee and some type of poison immunity will completely negate damage from the workers, soldiers and guardians.

Nechryael.title: Slayer task/Nechryael
Nechryael.intro:
Nechryael are a type of demon that can be assigned as a slayer task at level 80 Slayer and 85 combat by various Slayer masters. They are notable for their frequent drops of herbs, seeds, and alchable items, making them an extremely good slayer task.

Nechryael attack with melee, and can periodically summon up to two death spawns to assist them in battle. These death spawns are fairly inaccurate with a max hit of 2, but as they attack with typeless melee, Protect from Melee has no effect on them. Uniquely, they are able to attack you in single-combat areas regardless of if you are already in combat. It is recommended to bring food if using Melee or to have runes to cast blood spells if using Magic to kill nechryaels. It is also possible to leave the area and return to lose aggression, but this is impractical in most situations.

A stronger variant of the Nechryael, the Greater Nechryael, can be found in the Catacombs of Kourend, Iorwerth Dungeon and Wilderness Slayer Cave. These are mechanically the same as their standard counterparts, barring higher stats. It is highly recommended to kill these whenever possible, as they have a more lucrative drop table. Both variants share the same superior, the Nechryarch, though the common drop table takes from whichever variant they came from. Nechryarch attack with melee, but will periodically summon a trio of chaotic death spawn; one each in melee, magic and ranged. They hit significantly harder, but their attacks can be blocked with prayer. These spawns will only appear if the Nechryarch is allowed to attack the player, so using safespots or farcasting will prevent this from happening.

Players who seek a fast task are encouraged to kill them in the Catacombs of Kourend, as fourteen greater nechryael are found in two chambers of seven each. With a goading potion to draw aggression, players will find themselves gaining very high experience rates with minimal downtime.

If not intending to mage greater nechryael, players are recommended to melee them in the Iorwerth Dungeon, as it is very likely to be crashed by another player if using melee in the catacombs. The nechryael in the dungeon are able to drop crystal shards to increase overall profit per task.

If killing nechryael under an assignment from Krystilia, players must head to the Wilderness Slayer Cave. A goading potion is recommended, along with a one-click teleport such as a royal seed pod. The player can easily teleport out of the dungeon, but the caves themselves are a very popular player killing spot and players are likely to die if they do not pay attention in the caves.

Normal nechryael yield lower Slayer experience rates, although for ironman players in particular, their more plentiful seed drops are a very efficient source for Herblore training and general potions. In addition, as they are roughly twice as fast to kill, their malicious ashes can be offered more frequently for higher Prayer experience rates. Nechryael are found in the Slayer Tower and the Charred Dungeon, which is a multicombat area. It is highly encouraged to kill the normal nechryael in the Charred Dungeon, as despite there only being 6 spawns, the significantly faster kill times and better seed drop rates make them a lucrative task as well as a good task for hunting the imbued heart. This dungeon requires 60 Sailing to access the island and is very close to Wyrmscraig, allowing for reasonably quick access with a necklace of passage should the player not have a boat docked at Charred Island with a greater teleport focus.

Smoke Devil.title: Slayer task/Smoke devils
Smoke Devil.intro:
Smoke devils can be assigned as a slayer task at level 93 Slayer and level 85 combat by high-end Slayer masters. They are only found in the Smoke Devil Dungeon south of Castle Wars and can only be fought if on a task. They attack with magical ranged. As with dust devils, players must wear a facemask or slayer helm when fighting smoke devils, or their attacks will always deal moderate damage that also drains stats.

Players may choose between killing smoke devils or their boss variant, the thermonuclear smoke devil.

When killing normal smoke devils, players are highly encouraged to use barrage spells, as smoke devils have a high defence level. Although they have very high magic defence, they have a low magic level, which means most spells will still be reasonably accurate. A cannon is strongly recommended to lure the smoke devils, as their cave is extremely large and trying to stack them without one is significantly slower. Players who have obtained rewards from the elite tier of Combat Achievements should have enough cannonballs for one rotation to lure all the smoke devils, while those without may need to reload their cannon once to do so. Place the cannon in the centre of the dungeon and stack the smoke devils as they aggro, using the remains to the sides to stack them. Restore the stack when three or fewer smoke devils are left.

When killing the boss, players can opt between melee or magic. Magic is faster but more expensive, while melee is less cost but requires more attention.

If players wish to maximise profit from the task, killing the boss is recommended. If seeking to quickly clear the task or obtain the imbued heart/eternal gem, kill normal smoke devils instead. Their superior, the nuclear smoke devil, has a fairly high chance of rolling the table, second only to the Colossal Hydra.
Smoke Devil.strategy:
Attack styles:
The smoke devils attack only with a ranged attack. Protect from Missiles will prevent all damage.

Smoke:
The smoke devils are located in a smoky environment. Players not wearing a facemask or slayer helmet will take 10 damage occasionally while in the dungeon, and attacks from the smoke devils will deal very rapid damage that also drain stats. When using the slayer helmet to check how many kills you have left on the task, take care not to misclick on unequipping the helmet; this can quickly lead to a death with smoke devils attacking you. This also applies on not misclicking rune full helms in the inventory that smoke devils drop as loot.

Aviansie.title: Slayer task/Aviansie
Aviansie.intro:
Aviansie can be assigned as a slayer task provided that players have access to the God Wars Dungeon (requiring completion of Death Plateau) and has unlocked Watch the birdie slayer perk for 80 Slayer reward points.

Aviansie can be found in the normal and Wilderness God Wars Dungeon; as followers of Armadyl, Armadylean God-aligned items are required to make them tolerant. Aviansie have an increased sense of danger and will attack players if they are attacked, even if they're in combat with another monster. Their flying height means that they can only be harmed with ranged and magic, although salamanders and halberds are an exception as a direct target.

Aviansie have a somewhat generous drop table that mostly revolves around adamantite bars, runite limbs, ensouled aviansie heads and poisoned rune daggers, the limbs and daggers having reasonable high alchemy price. Aviansies in the God Wars Dungeon will only drop the bars noted if the player has completed the Hard Fremennik Diary, whereas those in the Wilderness drop them noted regardless of diary completion. Though unlikely, it is possible to be killed by other players in the Wilderness, and its dangers force players to bring less than optimal gear if minimising risk.

Kree'arra and his bodyguards can be killed as alternatives for an aviansie task, but not the Armadylean-aligned spiritual warriors, rangers and mages. Due to the general lack of popularity with aviansie, they are usually toggled off unless killing Kree'arra.

While an emergency teleport is required as usual at Kree'arra, players can bank at Nex; get the Zarosian kills prior to starting the trip to start off with an optimal inventory, and use an ecumenical key to avoid wasting time on kill count. Accessing Kree'arra will require two additional inventory slots to cover a crossbow that can fire a mith grapple. Banking at the prison will require a Zarosian item to avoid getting killed, and it is recommended to gather the necessary Zarosian killcount to avoid having to kill them while returning from a trip. With max mage gear, an Eldritch Nightmare staff and optional lightbearer, the player can often complete entire tasks at Kree'arra without having to bank, limited to the charges and runes in their possession.

Alternatively, players could kill reanimated aviansie, though it could be troublesome to obtain ensouled heads as they are not killed as often.

Black Demon.title: Slayer task/Black demons
Black Demon.intro:
Black demons can be assigned as a Slayer task at 80 combat level by various Slayer masters. They can be found in a variety of dungeons around Gielinor. Black demons can be easily killed using safespots when attacking with Ranged or Magic, or by using melee with the Protect from Melee prayer. They are weak to demonbane weapons, as well as water spells.

For lower-levelled players, black demon tasks can be very daunting, as their high stats requires safespotting, which will significantly lower kill rates. Higher-levelled players will not have this problem, but the demons have a near non-existent drop table which makes killing them generally not worth the time or experience.

The two best spots for killing black demons would be Taverley Dungeon or the Chasm of Fire. The former has many demons packed together while the latter has more safespots, and both are cannonable. The advantage of the latter is that those who have completed A Kingdom Divided and signed a contract with Yama will be able to get contracts from killing the demons. The drop rate is increased when killing them according to preference, but catering to this will prolong tasks and reduce AFK time. While black demons are also found in the Catacombs of Kourend, which is a multicombat area and have access to the catacombs table, it is generally not worth killing them there as they have unusually higher Defence compared to the other variants and it is not possible to utilise all four spawns.

In the Wilderness, black demons are only found in two locations; Edgeville Dungeon and the Wilderness Slayer Cave. Both spots are under 30 Wilderness, though the latter is a multicombat area. Each location has their advantages; Edgeville Dungeon is easier to escape from, while the Wilderness Slayer Cave is multicombat, has a different drop table, and has one entrance, with hopping inside being slightly difficult due to the demons' aggression.

If the player is killing black demons that were assigned to them by any Slayer master other than Krystilia or Konar, they may choose to kill demonic gorillas instead. This requires completion of Monkey Madness II and two combat styles. Killing demonic gorillas is slower, though they are quite profitable.

Bloodveld.title: Slayer task/Bloodveld
Bloodveld.intro:
Bloodvelds are a type of demon that use their long tongues to attack their victims. Being a Slayer monster, bloodvelds require a Slayer level of 50 to be damaged by players. As a demon, it is affected by demonbane weapons. An ash sanctifier may be brought to receive Prayer experience. Bloodvelds are popular among many players for their high Hitpoints and low Defence, thus making them good sources of experience.

Bloodvelds are one of few monsters that attack with magic-based melee, meaning that despite it using melee attacks against the player, it is the player's magic defence (rather than their melee defence) that is used to determine the accuracy of the bloodveld's attack. As such, it is recommended for players killing bloodvelds to equip armour with decent magic defence, such as dragonhide or blood moon armour, as they are relatively accurate in combat. Players using Prayer should still pray Protect from Melee instead of magic to nullify damage.

There are many locations to kill bloodvelds, though the most common one is the Stronghold Slayer Cave, due to its close proximity to a bank. The bloodvelds can also be killed here with a dwarf multicannon, requiring relatively low attention. The Meiyerditch Laboratories are notably multi-combat and cannonable. It is not recommended to kill bloodvelds elsewhere, as they take longer to access and/or are not cannonable. Bloodvelds have a superior variant, the insatiable bloodveld, if the perk Bigger and Badder is active.

Players can also kill Mutated Bloodvelds in place of normal bloodvelds. These bloodvelds have even more hitpoints than their non-mutated counterparts and a vastly improved drop table to make up for their difficulty. Mutated bloodvelds are found in four locations: the Catacombs of Kourend, Meiyerditch Laboratories, Buccaneers' Laboratory, and Iorwerth Dungeon. Each location has their own advantages and disadvantages. Under most circumstances, players are recommended to kill them in the Meiyerditch Laboratories, as a cluster of seven mutated bloodvelds can be found. Coupled with its multicombat nature and the ability to place a cannon, bloodveld tasks here provide the most experience per hour and even more AFK time. Players with 76 Sailing may instead kill them at Buccaneers' Laboratory, which is also multicombat but has no obstacles blocking bloodvelds. Building the rowboat and bank chest makes accessing and banking here much faster than other locations.

The other two locations are only recommended when assigned there by Konar.

If assigned by Konar quo Maten, it is reasonable to kill bloodvelds if sent to the Slayer Tower, but tasks sending the player to the God Wars Dungeon should be skipped, as they do not allow for the insatiable bloodveld to spawn, and AFK'ing is not possible without drawing aggression from other monsters.

It is not recommended to kill them if assigned by Krystilia, as the only location they can be found is the Wilderness God Wars Dungeon, which is a dangerous multiway area where players run the risk of being killed by other players (along with incredibly sparse spawns) forcing them to bring minimal risk and thus lowering overall rates.

Players who are not assigned bloodvelds by Konar can alternatively use Expert Reanimation on ensouled bloodveld heads, as reanimated bloodveld count towards the task. While overall Slayer and combat experience is much less, this is a viable alternative for players who are training Prayer.

variants.notes: For each tier of the Morytania Diary completed, players receive an additional Slayer 2.5% experience for bloodvelds slain at the Slayer Tower. Each tier completed results in an additional 3 Slayer experience per kill.
The slightly-stronger God Wars bloodveld variant are followers of Zamorak and will be aggressive to the player unless the player has a Zamorak item equipped.

Superior slayer monster variant, which has a chance of spawning on a bloodveld's death after purchasing the Bigger and Badder unlock for 50 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master.
Cannot spawn from the Zamorak-aligned bloodvelds in the God Wars Dungeons.

Mutated bloodvelds in the Catacombs of Kourend can drop ancient shards and dark totem pieces. They can be killed in multicombat.
In the Iorwerth Dungeon, mutated bloodveld can drop crystal shards. This location can only be accessed after completion of Song of the Elves.
The Meiyerditch Laboratories location is a multi-combat area where a dwarf multicannon can be used to kill mutated bloodveld. The area is only accessible with partial completion of Sins of the Father (after killing the mutated bloodveld during the quest). However, the run to the Meiyerditch Laboratories is fairly long, so it is recommended to use Prayer there instead of food. A shortcut through the abyss to the blood altar may be worth considering if you don't have the agility or mining level for the fairy ring shortcut, though it carries very significant risk going through the wilderness.
The Buccaneers' Laboratory location is also a multi-combat area where a dwarf multicannon can be used to kill mutated bloodveld. 76 Sailing is required to access this area. Players are recommended to build a rowboat on the island, which allows easy access through Pirates' Cove.
Superior slayer monster variant, which has a chance of spawning on a mutated bloodveld's death after purchasing the Bigger and Badder unlock for 50 Slayer reward points from any Slayer master.

Using the Expert Reanimation spell on an ensouled bloodveld head, players can reanimate a bloodveld for greatly reduced slayer experience. However, the player also receives 1,040 Prayer experience for each kill.
If the spell is not cast within a reasonable amount of time of picking up the head, or if the player trades the head or teleports away, then the user will need to reanimate the heads at the Dark Altar in Kourend.

Drake.title: Slayer task/Drakes
Drake.intro:
Drakes are high level Slayer monsters found in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. They can drop their claws and teeth, which are used to upgrade the boots of stone and holy sandals into boots of brimstone and devout boots, respectively. These items are five times more common when killed on a Slayer task.

Drakes use both ranged and ranged melee, so melee armour is recommended against their attacks. Additionally, they will launch a fireball at the player's position, which deals 6-8 damage per hit for four hits if dragonfire protection is not used. It functions the same as chromatic dragonfire, although it can also be avoided by stepping away from the target tile.

Prior to completion of the elite Kourend & Kebos diary, boots of stone, boots of brimstone or granite boots must be worn within the dungeon to avoid taking constant damage.

Drakes are considered draconic and as such dragonbane weapons are very effective. They take 50% more damage from water spells.

A superior version of the drake, the guardian drake, can occasionally appear if superiors are enabled. Guardian drakes additionally have a special attack that will deal heavy damage and stun the player if they do not move out of melee distance in time, so flinching or using ranged weapons are recommended when killing them.

Most players tend to block drakes despite them being cannonable; they have a very high weight, somewhat lackluster drops and high stats for their level, in addition to their two flat armour value. It is recommended to kill drakes in the task-only area, as while both rooms are still large, the task-only area is smaller for a cannon to make the most out of.
Drake.strategy:
• Level 84 Slayer to deal damage or receive a task.
• Access to Mount Karuulm.

Drakes' normal ranged attacks can be fully blocked by protect from missiles.

Drakes do not require a fire protection shield or potion to be slain, unlike most other dragons. However, after seven auto-attacks, drakes will launch a volcanic breath towards the player's current position, which deals 6-8 damage for four hits if the player is struck by the projectile.

• The levels of dragonfire protection apply to this special attack.
• Having a form of dragonfire protection will reduce this to 3-4 damage.
• Wielding a dragonfire shield, dragonfire ward, or anti-dragon shield alongside drinking an antifire will negate the damage.
• Using a Super antifire potion or its extended version will negate the damage, allowing you to wear a defender or use a blowpipe.

Alternatively, moving one tile elsewhere when the projectile is launched allows complete avoidance.

Together, a player can take no damage when using protect from missiles and dragonfire protection, if attacking from at least 1 tile away.

Gargoyle.title: Slayer task/Gargoyles

infobox.otherReq: Completion of Quest Priest in Peril

Gargoyle.intro:
Gargoyles can be assigned as a Slayer task by various Slayer masters at level 75 Slayer, level 80 combat, and with completion of the Priest in Peril quest. They are only found in the Slayer Tower, either on the top floor or in the basement. The gargoyles in the basement of the Slayer Tower can only be killed while on a Slayer task, as Raulyn will stop the player if they attempt to fight them off-task. Gargoyles have a Superior slayer monster variant, the level 349 marble gargoyle. Unlike regular gargoyles, the marble gargoyle also utilises ranged attacks. It also has a special attack, launching a white-red orb that deals heavy damage and entraps the player if not dodged; this attack has a 1x1 AoE (in other words, it affects only the single tile where the player was standing).

Gargoyles are weak to both magic and crush attacks, but melee is commonly used due to the lack of safespots, less defence against their attacks and expenses for casting spells. They have -2 flat armour, so weapons such as Dual macuahuitl are recommended to make use of the extra damage. Even then, they are still easily fought with most standard weapons one might have available.

To kill a gargoyle, a rock hammer, a rock thrownhammer, or a granite hammer must be used when they reach 9 or lower Hitpoints. Normally, the item must be used on the gargoyle, but players can buy the "Gargoyle Smasher" perk from Slayer masters for 120 Slayer points, which will automatically smash the gargoyle when it falls to 9 or lower Hitpoints, provided that the player has a rock hammer (or equivalent) in their inventory. The granite hammer will automatically smash gargoyles even without the perk if it is equipped. The rock hammer is faster than the rock thrownhammer as it does not have travel time. If both are in the inventory, the rock hammer is used in melee distance, while thrownhammers are used outside of melee distance.

Gargoyles also have a boss variant, the Grotesque Guardians. In order to access them, the player must kill gargoyles on-task to obtain the brittle key, which unlocks the boss arena. The boss fight consists of two gargoyles; Dusk and Dawn. Players can choose between melee and a melee/range hybrid; the former requires a polearm weapon, while the latter has easier accessibility.

When considering whether to kill regular gargoyles or the Grotesque Guardians, it is worth noting that the normal gargoyles are much faster to kill and require less supplies and effort, whereas the Grotesque Guardians are more time-consuming, and require more effort and supplies to kill. The requirements for killing the Guardians are also substantially higher in terms of stats and gear. The drop table of the Guardians is not significantly better than gargoyles, especially considering that regular gargoyles have very decent drops as well. However, the Guardians are one of only two sources of granite dust, which is untradeable. The dust strengthens steel cannonballs, turning them into granite cannonballs with a max hit of 35 instead of 30.

It is recommended to kill gargoyles in the basement during a task, as there are many gargoyles in a fairly small area compared to the top floor. The basement is also large enough that the player can reset the aggression timer easily without leaving the area.

If killing the Grotesque Guardians, it is strongly recommended the player avoid purchasing Double Trouble, as this causes the boss to be counted as two kills per task rather than one, drastically reducing the amount of kills per task.

Red dragons can be assigned as a Slayer task after unlocking Seeing red for 50 Slayer reward points and requiring partial completion of Dragon Slayer I to receive the Anti-dragon shield.

Adult and brutal variants use melee and dragonfire, so sufficient dragonfire protection is needed to avoid taking heavy damage. Alternatively, using Protect from Magic will suffice.

Normal dragons are found in Brimhaven Dungeon and Forthos Dungeon. Completion of the Elite Karamja Diary will result in the dragons dropping noted red dragonhide on death for the dragons in the former.

Once Dragon Slayer II is completed, a group of three dragons can be found in the Corsair Cove Dungeon and is very close to a bank, along with two baby dragons.

Brutal red dragons can be found in the Catacombs of Kourend. These are a stronger alternative, and unlike their normal variants, also have a chance at the draconic visage. They are generally not worth killing, since a task of brutal red dragons is very slow compared to normal or baby red dragons.

Suqah.intro:
Suqah can be a good Slayer task, due to the relatively high amount of experience per hour that can be gained from killing them with the help of a dwarf multicannon. However, the use of a dwarf multicannon and toxic blowpipe will also result in a loss of coins due to their lack of valuable drops.

If using the northern area on Lunar Isle, players should pray Protect from Magic and wear armour with high Melee defence, as these Suqah attack with both a melee attack and a magic attack.

Players wishing to avoid the magic damage should fight the suqah on the southern part of the island, such as near the Astral Altar, as these attack with only melee. There are also three melee-only suqah on the south-west part of the island, over the bridge (abutting the city wall); specifically, a cannon can be placed directly north-west of the dead tree to target the melee-only suqah while avoiding the single mage-dealing suqah in the vicinity.

Vampyre.title: Slayer task/Vampyres
Vampyre.intro:
Vampyres can be assigned as a Slayer task by various Slayer masters once the player has completed Priest in Peril and achieved at least level 35 combat. Mostly confined to the Morytania region, access to different variants of vampyres is usually tied to progression within the Myreque questline.

Prior to the Actual Vampyre Slayer unlock, vampyre tasks can only be assigned by Slayer masters Mazchna and Vannaka and only 10 to 20 will be assigned at a time.

Vampyres come in three different attribute tiers which determines their weaknesses to various vampyrebane weapons:

• Tier 1 vampyres, such as feral vampyres and Vampyre Juveniles, can be hurt with any weapon.
• Tier 2 vampyres, such as Vampyre Juvinates, must be harmed with silver weapons at minimum. Alternatively, wearing efaritay's aid will allow any weapon to hurt them, but their damage is reduced by 50%.
• Tier 3 vampyres, such as vyrewatch, Vyrewatch Sentinels and venators, require the Ivandis flail as a minimum. Other superior weapons, such as blisterwood, the hallowed flail and sunspear will also work. Efaritay's aid does not allow normal weapons to damage them.

High-levelled players should not toggle vyre tasks on until they have completed Sins of the Father, where they may kill vyrewatch sentinels for their lucrative blood shard drop. Sentinels are permanently aggressive unless the player has worn a full set of vyre noble clothing, meaning they can be easily AFK'ed with little input by the player as they only use melee.

After the third fight against Lowerniel Drakan in The Blood Moon Rises, all vyres will become tolerant of the player. In order to toggle the sentinels' aggression back, they player must complete the quest and speak to the werewolf hired by Lord Mischa Myrmel (south of the Darkmeyer teleport on Drakan's medallion) to buy a garlic cocktail from him for 20 coins. Additionally, completion of the quest will unlock venators. They are harder than sentinels but have a superior along with a vastly improved drop rate on the blood shard.

Efaritay's aid is recommended for players who are willing to put some extra cost/time in, as the bonuses of the ring will stack alongside task bonuses. These will generally provide superior damage over other rings such as the ultor ring.

Warped Creatures.title: Slayer task/Warped creatures
Warped Creatures.intro:
Warped creatures can be assigned as a Slayer task starting at level 56 Slayer by Chaeldar, Konar, Nieve, Duradel, and Mortimer. They will only be assigned if the option Warped Reality is purchased, barring Mortimer who will assign them regardless. Warped creatures are found exclusively in the Poison Waste Dungeon, requiring completion of The Path of Glouphrie.

Players must have the crystal chime in their inventory to fight them, otherwise they will be invulnerable.

Warped Tortoises are relatively simple to fight, as they only deal melee damage, which is fully negated by Protect from Melee, although they are weak enough that high crush defence is sufficient to slay them as well. They are available directly at the entrance of the dungeon, making shorter trips viable as banking with the spirit tree is easy. They can be safespotted by traversing to one of the rooms further in the dungeon, where there are two tortoises surrounded by four pillars in the centre of the room, as well as pillars along the walls. By standing on the east or west of these four pillars in the centre, the player can attack the tortoises using ranged or magic without being attacked. Using a halberd also will work in the safespot. There is another safespot in the second room with the one Warped Tortoise, if hit from the angle shown in the image below.

For Warped Terrorbirds, it is recommended to wear earmuffs or a slayer helmet to halve their max hit and reduce chip damage through Protect from Missiles from their ranging attacks. They can attack with both melee and ranged, and will react to players' protection prayers and will switch the style they attack with after an attack is blocked with the correct prayer. This can be exploited where if only one is able to reach the player at melee distance and others are attacking at a range then players can use Protect from Missiles for a few seconds which will make all attacking terrorbirds switch to melee attacks and attempt to move into melee distance. If they are unable to reach the player doing this they will not switch back to using ranged attacks and instead stop attacking. This can be set up relatively easily by standing in corners so that only one or two of them can reach you with melee while the rest are stuck behind them.

While the warped tortoises are not aggressive, the warped terrorbirds are, and can quickly defeat an unprepared player. The terrorbirds also never lose aggression, making most parts of the dungeon with them unable to be used for safespots.

For players who don't mind killing either monster (as both have different drop tables), the most ideal spot to kill them is in the second large chamber in the dungeon. Place the cannon on top of the north-western tortoise spawn and have Protect from Missiles active. Telekinetic Grab is useful to grab drops from across the pit.

equipment.name: Prayer Melee (Tortoise)
equipment.text:
This setup is used if planning to fight the warped tortoises with use of Protect from Melee, to negate all damage and increase AFK time. Prayer equipment should be prioritised in order to make AFK times longer. The Sarachnis cudgel can be substituted for any melee weapon, although the tortoises are weak to Crush, so they are the preferred choice. Maces also possess a Prayer bonus of their own, making them extra beneficial for this setup.
• Before obtaining a black mask, replace with the best melee strength or prayer headgear item available, such as the helm of Neitiznot.
• Runes are brought for casting High Level Alchemy to avoid needing to return to the bank to store valuable item drops.
• Earmuffs should be worn on the run past the terrorbirds to reach the desired area for fighting tortoises (assuming you do not wish to fight the ones at the entrance), and may be dropped after reaching them if you have a teleport out.
• Grand seed pod can be replaced with a charged (and worn) ring of wealth, as it will also transport a player near both a bank and a spirit tree with its teleport to the Grand Exchange.
• Prayer potions can be substituted for moonlight moth mixes to save on costs, at the cost of trip length.
• Black warlock mixes and ruby harvest mixes may also be used to the same effect; although these typically have a very low volume on the Grand Exchange so you would need to create them yourself.

equipment.name: Ranged safespot
equipment.text:
This setup is used for safespotting the warped tortoises, using this . Any fast ranged weapon will prove effective, and no resources are needed as the player cannot be reached by the tortoises to be attacked. The hunters' sunlight crossbow can be substituted for any ranged weapon, and although the tortoises are weak to heavy ranged weapons, such as crossbows, faster weapons like shortbows, throwing knives, or the toxic blowpipe will more often perform better. If your Strength stat is at least roughly equal to or higher than your Ranged stat, the eclipse atlatl can be the best option for them, especially if using high strength bonus items like an amulet of strength, barrows gloves, and berserker ring (i). If using the atlatl, remember to bring both ranging potions and super strength potions.
• Proselyte armour can be worn instead to save on prayer potions, for only a small loss in dps.
• Prayer potions are not needed if not intending to use Eagle Eye.
• Runes are brought for casting High Level Alchemy to avoid needing to return to the bank to store valuable item drops.
• Before obtaining or imbuing a black mask, replace with the best ranged or prayer headgear item available, such as a mitre or Shayzien helm 5.
• Earmuffs should be worn on the run past the terrorbirds to reach the safespot area, and may be dropped after reaching them if you have a teleport out.
• Grand seed pod can be replaced with a charged (and worn) ring of wealth, as it will also transport a player near both a bank and a spirit tree.
• Prayer potions can be substituted for moonlight moth mixes to save on costs, at the cost of trip length.

=== Terrorbirds safespotting ===
• Must bring a weapon with at least 9 tile of range, such as the crystal bow or Craw's bow. crossbows and shortbows can also reach while using the "Longrange" attack style, however this results in much less DPS than the previously mentioned weapons.
• If lacking a naturally longrange Ranged weapon like the crystal bow, Craw's bow, or ballista, maging will typically be better damage.
• See images below on how to safespot them using the doors near the entrance.

equipment.name: Magic safespot
equipment.text:
This setup is used for safespotting the warped tortoises, using this . While generally less damage than using Ranged, it is an alternative option that is still reasonably effective. The twinflame staff casting Earth spells is one of the better options for this, although at higher Magic levels some powered staves like the trident of the seas can outperform it, especially if using boosts.

• Monk robes can be worn instead to save on prayer potions, for only a small loss in dps, assuming no max hits are lost, such as if you have robes with magic damage like Ahrim's robes.
• Prayer potions are not needed if not intending to use Mystic Might.
• Runes are brought for casting the highest level Earth spell available, and for High Level Alchemy to avoid needing to return to the bank to store valuable item drops. Using a dust battlestaff or the twinflame staff will provide the elemental runes for each spell, respectively.
• Before obtaining or imbuing a black mask, replace with the best magic or prayer headgear item available, such as a mitre or bloodbark helm.
• For Ironmen, the occult necklace should be replaced with either a stole, unholy symbol, or amulet of magic, as it cannot be obtained until a much higher Slayer level.
• Earmuffs should be worn on the run past the terrorbirds to reach the safespot area, and may be dropped after reaching them if you have a teleport out.
• Grand seed pod can be replaced with a charged (and worn) ring of wealth, as it will also transport a player near both a bank and a spirit tree.
• Prayer potions can be substituted for moonlight moth mixes to save on costs, at the cost of trip length.
• Magic potions or forgotten brews may be optionally brought if using a powered staff, as they will often gain substantial DPS when boosted.

=== Terrorbirds safespotting ===
• All magic weapons and cast spells are able to reach the terrorbirds for the safespot, except for the Eye of Ayak. As warped terrorbirds lack an elemental weakness, a powered staff on the "Longrange" attack style will be better on average.
• If lacking a naturally longrange Ranged weapon like the crystal bow, Craw's bow, or ballista, maging will typically be better damage.
• See images below on how to safespot them using the doors near the entrance.

Aberrant Spectre.title: Slayer task/Aberrant spectres
Aberrant Spectre.intro:
Aberrant spectres can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 60 Slayer and level 65 combat by various Slayer masters. They can be found in the Stronghold Slayer Cave, the second floor of the Slayer Tower, and in Deepfin Mine.

A nose peg or Slayer helmet is required when fighting aberrant spectres. Without either of those equipped, they will use a special attack which hits through protection prayers and drain the player's stats very quickly.

Aberrant spectres have a normal magic attack that has a max hit of 8. Protect from Magic will completely neutralize it. With Bigger and badder unlocked, the Superior variation, the Abhorrent spectre may spawn. The Abhorrent has a max hit of 33, and Protect from Magic will still prevent its normal damage.

Players assigned aberrant spectres may also choose to kill Deviant spectres in the Catacombs of Kourend. Deviant spectres are generally not preferred as they have have significantly higher defence, which yields lower Slayer experience rates while also having only marginally better drops. They do have access to the Catacombs droptable which includes pieces of the Dark totem, and also have their own superior variant, the Repugnant spectre, which will always drop a piece of the Dark totem. Deviant and Repugnant spectres share the requirement of a nose peg or Slayer helmet and Protect from Magic will negate all their damage.

Directly east of the fairy ring DJR fairy ring, there is a mysterious hole for quick access to deviant spectres (it must have been accessed earlier from below - ‘Climb-up Vine’ - if not, there is a boulder instead of a hole). The closest bank to this location is the Shayzien bank, which is south-east of the mysterious hole.

As Undead monsters, the Salve amulet(ei) and its appropriate variations give a bonus to damage and accuracy against Aberrant spectres. However, this effect does not stack with the Slayer helmet. Since its 20% boost to all three combat styles is higher than the Slayer helmet's maximum of 16.67%, the amulet is generally preferred.

Aberrant spectres are a popular task for their very frequent herb drops. They have an over 60% chance to drop at least one herb and may drop up to three, so bringing a herb sack is highly recommended. They also commonly drop seeds, so a Seed box is also helpful. Beyond that, they have a few alchable drops.

A Cannon can be used in the Stronghold Slayer Cave and the Deepfin Mine, although these are not Multicombat areas and will require safespotting to cannon more than one at a time. Aberrant spectres killed in the Slayer Tower benefit from the experience bonus granted by completing tiers of the Morytania Diary. The Stronghold Slayer cave is near multiple teleportation methods, has Nieve or Steve directly outside, and has a bank very close. A bank chest can be built in a hotspot within the Deepfin Mine and accessed quickly via a shortcut requiring 84 Agility.

Aberrant spectres also have the Spectral attribute, so the Ectoplasmator can be carried to yield a small amount of Prayer experience with each kill.

Basilisk.title: Slayer task/Basilisks
Basilisk.intro:
Basilisks can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 40 Slayer, level 40 combat, and level 20 Defence by medium level Slayer Masters. The high level masters will not assign them until players unlock Basilocked using Slayer reward points. Ordinary basilisks, which can be found in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon and Jormungand's Prison, attack only using an extremely inaccurate melee attack with a max hit of 5. Their thin drop table and high defence level generally make them worthwhile to skip, although their low weighting doesn't make them worth blocking.

However, after completion of The Fremennik Exiles quest, the player gains access to the Basilisk Knight in Jormungand's Prison, and basilisk tasks gain a new purpose for obtaining the powerful Neitiznot faceguard.

When fighting any basilisk, the player must equip a mirror shield or V's shield, or the basilisk's gaze will deal immense damage and massively drain the player's stats.

The knights have both a melee attack which can hit up to 20 and a magic attack with the same max hit. They also have a unique mechanic where they will match the player's Attack speed with a max frequency of four ticks. Knights will exclusively use their magic attack at distance while attempting to move into melee range. Protection prayers can block each kind of attack, although not simultaneously.

While not on a basilisk task, Basilisk knights drop the Basilisk jaw, which is combined with the Helm of Neitiznot to create the Neitiznot faceguard, at a rate of only 1/5000. While on task, however, this increases to 1/1000. Therefore, on average, Basilisk knights will deliver a drop worth every four to five Extended tasks. Due to their high defence these tasks can be relatively slow, with a maximum possible kill rate of only 100 per hour. For more information on strategies to kill Basilisk knights, including safespots, see Basilisk Knight/Strategies.

The task unlock for Konar, Nieve, and Duradel to assign basilisks can be toggled off once the player receives their jaw, but requires paying Slayer points to activate again.

Both variations of basilisk have their own Superior slayer monster variation. Ordinary basilisks may spawn the slightly stronger Monstrous basilisk, while knights may spawn the highly dangerous Basilisk Sentinel. The sentinels also have a special attack which launches a slow-moving projectile at the player. The player must either move one tile to avoid it, or be encased in stone. If encased in stone, the player must click rapidly to escape or else receive massive damage.

Knights have a reasonable drop table when including the jaw, but a poor one without. Still, they frequently drop alchable equipment, dozens of mid to high level Catalytic runes, and occasional high level herbs.

Cannons cannot be placed anywhere with any kind of basilisk.

Fire Giant.title: Slayer task/Fire giants
Fire Giant.intro:
Fire giants can be assigned as a slayer task at level 65 combat by various Slayer masters. They are the strongest generic giants for their category and are mostly known for their rune scimitar drops.

Fire giants can be found in an array of locations, most of which allow for the use of a dwarf multicannon. The lone exception is the Catacombs of Kourend, which does not allow a cannon but is a multicombat area.

In most cases, players are recommended to kill fire giants at the Catacombs of Kourend, due to the multicombat area of the dungeon allowing for relative AFK and having access to the catacombs drop table. The Giants' Den is a second alternative, as while it is not multicombat, it allows for a cannon and the giants are the same as those in the catacombs, along with sharing its drop-table including i.e. dark totem pieces. The level 109 Fire giants should be prioritised for maximum xp as they have more HP, yet significantly lower Defence levels compared to the level 104's.

If assigned by Konar quo Maten, most assigned areas are good locations for completing a fire giant task. The main exception is Brimhaven Dungeon, where the spawns are too spread out between floors, making it inefficient. She won’t assign them in the Smoke Dungeon, but even if you go there, it’s not recommended — there are too few giants scattered around to make it worthwhile.

If killing them as part of a task from Krystilia, the only location they can be found is the Deep Wilderness Dungeon, located around level 53 Wilderness. While somewhat close to the Mage Arena, its deep location makes it a prime hotspot for player killing, and it is highly recommended that players killing giants here have completed the Wilderness Medium Diary to unlock a shortcut (requires 46 Agility) between the fire and hill giant chamber, saving significant time and avoiding shadow spiders on the way.

Players who are not assigned fire giants from Konar or Krystilia can also choose to kill Branda the Fire Queen, who is one of the two bosses making up the Royal Titans encounter. The helmet boost will work for her, but not against her counterpart, Eldric the Ice King.

Gryphons.title: Slayer task/Gryphons
Gryphons.intro:
Gryphons can be assigned as a slayer task by Vannaka, Chaeldar and Mortimer after completion of the Troubled Tortugans quest. Additionally, both Nieve and Duradel may assign gryphons after the perk Wings Spread has been purchased.

Gryphons are found exclusively on The Great Conch (Fairy Ring CJQ). There are three lairs for gryphons; a western cavern, an eastern cavern (Slayer task only) and a lair in the centre of the island which leads to the Shellbane gryphon. Both the eastern and western caverns have a southern room that is multi-combat and cannon-able.

Gryphons attack with melee and have a special attack which causes knockback and moderate damage if the player's weight of their worn equipment is too low; this is 30 for normal gryphons and 40 for the boss. They are weakest to melee, ideally from stabbing attacks. While being a bit more resistant to magic, they have a 50% weakness to air spells.

Bringing the tortugan shield is not necessary for normal gryphons, but those who are fighting their superior, the dire gryphon, or the boss are required to use it, or their attacks will deal frequent and moderate damage, even through prayer. Dire gryphons are similar to the boss variant in mechanics.

A boss variant, the Shellbane gryphon, can be found in the centre lair and is only attackable on-task. It is a solo instanced boss and alongside melee, makes use of ranged attacks and also two additional special attacks, both of which are easily avoidable.

Gryphons have relatively poor drops (except Horn of Plenty), and players who are not planning to kill the boss should otherwise avoid toggling them on for Nieve/Duradel. The boss itself has somewhat lacklustre drops too, but is slightly better compared to normal gryphons and has several unique items to collect.

For players seeking gryphon tasks, they are recommended to use Vannaka; while the overall amount is lower than Duradel, gryphons are Vannaka's highest weighted task.

equipment.name: Recommended
equipment.text:
Players who are not safespotting gryphons are recommended to use melee equipment. A minimum of 30 kg is required for normal gryphons and 40 for the shellbane gryphon to avoid taking damage from their special attack.

They are best killed in the south-western multicombat room of the eastern task-only cave using a venator bow and a dwarf multicannon. 30 kg can be reached in a maxed range setup by using a black mask (i) rather than a slayer helmet (i), using a granite ring, or by substituting avernic treads (max) for echo boots. Bring a tortugan shield for the superior, and a cannon.

Skeletal Wyvern.title: Skeletal Wyvern/Strategies
Skeletal Wyvern.intro: Skeletal Wyverns are level 72 Slayer monsters found in the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon.
Skeletal Wyvern.strategy:
• Level 72 Slayer to damage skeletal wyverns. This can be boosted.
• Completion of QuestElemental Workshop I or II for access to the elemental or mind shields respectively. These shields offer protection from the wyverns' powerful icy breath attack.
• Alternatively, the dragonfire shield, ancient wyvern shield and dragonfire ward also offer the same protection, all requiring having started Dragon Slayer I.

Attack styles:
Skeletal wyverns attack with Melee, Ranged and their unique ice breath attack.
• The Melee attack is only used when the player is standing in Melee distance and can hit up to 13. Skeletal wyverns roll their slash accuracy against the player's stab defence when performing a bite or tail swipe attack.
• The Ranged attack has an attack range of 6 tiles and can hit up to 13.
• The ice-breath attack has an attack range of 5 tiles and can hit 50+, although this damage can be drastically reduced to a maximum hit of 10 by the following shields: elemental shield, mind shield, dragonfire shield, ancient wyvern shield, and dragonfire ward.
• This attack may also freeze the player's character for a few seconds. During this period, the character is not able to move or attack.
• There is a 1/7 chance to be frozen while wielding one of the shields listed above.
• The ancient wyvern shield will grant an immunity against this freezing effect.
• Without an appropriate shield, the chance to be frozen by a skeletal wyvern is determined by one's Magic defensive bonuses.
• Antifire potions have no effect.

During the first period, while the wyverns are still aggressive, it is necessary to wield a shield that protects the player from the icy breath attacks. However, after they become tolerant of the player, it is advisable to switch to a shield that provides ranged attack bonuses. Always keep the other shield in the inventory, as the wyverns are not always lured correctly behind the obstacles, making them not safespottable and thus able to use their icy breath attacks again.

This gear assumes the player is using the safespot method to attack the skeletal wyverns. Wyverns will be aggressive for the first 10 minutes, so it's necessary to bring an icy breath protection shield. Once they become tolerant of the player, players should switch to a shield with more useful stats. Wyverns can be lured incorrectly, which allows them to use their icy breath attack again, so keep the other shield in the inventory.

This equipment is recommended when the player has level 92 Ranged or higher, while not having access to Armadyl equipment, as at this Ranged level it is more effective than (blessed) dragonhide armour.
