Spiritual Creatures.title: Slayer task/Spiritual creatures
Spiritual Creatures.intro:
Spiritual creatures are a potential Slayer assignment given by medium and high-levelled Slayer Masters after completion of Death Plateau, a combat level of 60 and either 60 Strength or Agility with a minimum Slayer level of 63 in order to be assigned them.

There are three types of spiritual creatures players can kill as part of a task: spiritual rangers, the weakest at 63 Slayer, warriors at 68 Slayer, and mages, the only NPCs that drop dragon boots, at 83 Slayer.

These creatures are only found in the God Wars Dungeon and the Wilderness God Wars Dungeon. As followers of their respective gods, they are aggressive to anyone that is not wearing an item aligned to their god, but will be tolerant otherwise. This is essentially required, as the dungeons are multicombat areas with many monsters, likely resulting in a swift death if this is not met.

In the God Wars Dungeon, players are encouraged to wear at least one Zamorak-affiliated item, as Zamorak's followers are found in all corners of the main section of the dungeon. Depending on the god that the player is focusing on, they should also bring one of that item to ensure tolerance. This is usually a Saradomin item, since Bandos and Armadyl-affiliated spiritual creatures are rarely killed.

In the Ancient Prison, only a Zaros-affiliated item is required, as none of the other gods' followers are found inside. It is still recommended to bring one Saradomin- and Zamorak-affiliated item, as the player will have to run past Saradomin and Zamorak followers to reach the Ancient Prison's entrance.

In the Wilderness God Wars Dungeon, it is recommended to bring three god-affiliated items: one of either Armadyl or Bandos (depending on the entrance entering from), one Saradomin, and one Zamorak. Zamorak's followers are essentially everywhere in the dungeon.

The stats of spiritual creatures are generally similar, with minor variations.

• Armadyl's spiritual creatures - An additional requirement of 70 Ranged, along with a crossbow that can fire a mithril grapple. The rangers are the strongest, the warriors are the second strongest, and the mages are the weakest. Unlike Aviansie, they can be attacked with all melee weapons.
• Bandos' spiritual creatures - An additional requirement of 70 Strength and a hammer. The warriors are the strongest, the mages are second strongest, and rangers are the weakest. Barring the mages, the rangers and warriors have the most health of monsters in this category.
• Saradomin's spiritual creatures - No additional requirements are needed, as these are found in the main dungeon. The mages are the strongest, the rangers the second strongest, and warriors the weakest.
• Zamorak's spiritual creatures - An additional requirement of 70 Hitpoints, and the player will lose all prayer points upon entering Zamorak's Fortress. The mages are the strongest and cast Flames of Zamorak, which drains Magic if not protected against, the rangers are second strongest, and warriors the weakest.
• Zaros' spiritual creatures - The player must complete the miniquest The Frozen Door, which has a requirement of 70 Strength, Hitpoints, Ranged, and Agility. The mages are the strongest, the warriors second strongest, and rangers the weakest. They are significantly stronger than the other gods' spiritual creatures.

In the Wilderness dungeon, only one requirement of either 60 Agility or Strength is required.

Many players tend to block spiritual creatures, since they are neither cannonable nor AFK'able, have low experience rates, and have poor drops compared to other similarly levelled monsters. Ironman players may wish to unblock the task once they have 83 slayer in order to get dragon boots.

When killing spiritual creatures, players are recommended to:

• Spiritual rangers - skip or block
• Spiritual warriors - if killing, Zamorak's Fortress
• Spiritual mages - if killing, Armadyl's Eyrie or Ancient Prison

variants.notes: The Zarosian variant can occasionally launch an arrow into the air, which if hit by, will deal heavy damage, disable overhead protection prayers and bind the player for a few seconds.

The Zarosian variant periodically unleashes smoke clouds in an X formation surrounding the player, descending onto their location when the attack was used in 5 ticks. Failing to move away deals up to 40 damage.

The Zamorakian variant's Flames of Zamorak will drain Magic levels if it successfully hits and damages the player.
The Zarosian variant uses the Ancient Magicks - smoke will poison the player, shadow drains the player's Attack level, blood heals the mage and ice freezes the player. These secondary effects will occur on successful hits, even if the damage would be blocked by prayer.

Troll.title: Slayer task/Trolls
Troll.intro:
Trolls can be assigned as a Slayer task at 60 combat level by various Slayer masters. Trolls are, for the most part, found in the Fremennik Province and north of Burthorpe.

Trolls fought in quests all count towards the Slayer task, with the exception of sea trolls. The bosses can be fought again in the Nightmare Zone.

Players who have completed the hard Morytania Diary might want to bring the bonecrusher to gain passive Prayer experience from the big bones drops. Players with 92 Magic and the Arceuus spellbook may opt to use the Sinister Offering spell instead.

There are two types of trolls that players can fight for a troll task: mountain trolls and ice trolls.

Mountain trolls are found in many locations, primarily around the Fremennik Province, though a group of fourteen trolls are also found in Mount Quidamortem. The Mount Quidamortem trolls can be easily accessed with the Xeric's talisman if players have received an ancient tablet from the Chambers of Xeric unlocking the Xeric's Honour teleport, although using the Lovakengj Minecart Network teleport or nearby fairy ring are also suitable.

Other variants include thrower trolls and troll generals, however these are scarce, far, and have nonexistent drops.

The other trolls, ice trolls, can be found in the Ice Path, Trollweiss Dungeon, and the isles north of Neitiznot and Jatizso.

The trolls in the Ice Path are not worth killing, as these are far stronger than other trolls and have incredibly poor drops for their level. Instead, players are advised to kill the trolls on the isles, as they are weaker, have a slightly better drop table, and are found in larger quantities in an open multicombat area. If killing trolls here, prayer and a Neitiznot shield are required in order to reduce damage taken from the ice troll females, who are much more accurate and damaging if not using a Neitiznot shield. Out of the two isles, it may be preferable to kill the trolls north of Jatizso, as the trolls there will often focus on the guards fighting them, which will lower the damage the player receives. Additionally, the bank on Jatizso is slightly closer to the troll area than it is on Neitiznot.

Regardless of the troll being killed, a dwarf multicannon is highly recommended as trolls have low aggression range.

One quick way to complete a trolls task for players not using a dwarf multicannon is to kill the ice troll runts in the first island north of Neitiznot. This method requires completion of The Fremennik Trials to access Neitiznot. There are several guards nearby constantly fighting the trolls, who deal considerable damage and will help speed up kills. They also keep the trolls distracted so that players are able to range or mage without utilising safespots. Note that if guards deal the finishing blow, the Slayer experience received is halved, but drops are still received as long as the player dealt any damage. Fire spells are recommended, as ice trolls have a fire weakness of 100%.

variants.notes:
River trolls spawn upon attempting to fish in the Enchanted Valley. Bring a small net.
The combat level of the river troll is dependent upon the player's combat level.
It is highly recommended to not slay Enchanted Valley river trolls, as they provide severely reduced experience for both combat and slayer.
These only drop bones (including long and curved bones).

Ankou.title: Slayer task/Ankou
Ankou.intro:
Ankou can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 40 combat by various Slayer masters. They can be found in the Sepulcher of Death, Stronghold Slayer Cave, the Catacombs of Kourend, and Deepfin Mine, as well as in the Wilderness in both the Wilderness Slayer Cave and the The Forgotten Cemetery. There are five variations of normal Ankou ranging from level 75 to 98. An additional variation, Dark Ankou, only appear when fighting the boss Skotizo, but they spawn infrequently and are almost always ignored in order to kill the boss faster. Damaged Dark Ankou that automatically die after Skotizo is killed will not count for a Slayer task.

Ankou attack with a relatively inaccurate melee attack that has a max hit from 8 to 10. Protect from Melee can be used to negate all damage.

Ankou are undead, therefore the Salve amulet and its variations can give a bonus to the player's accuracy and damage. The bonuses of the Salve amulet do not stack with the bonuses given by the Slayer helmet or Black mask. It is advised to check a Dps calculator with the player's current stats and other gear to determine if the Slayer helmet or the Salve amulet should be used.

Unextended Ankou tasks are fairly fast even when using melee in single combat. In the Multicombat areas of the Wilderness Slayer Cave and the Catacombs of Kourend, they are potentially viable as a Burst, Barrage, or Venator Bow task, although even an Extended task will be exhausted quickly by this method. The effects of the Salve necklace do not apply to monsters other than the target when using area of effect spells.

A Cannon may be used against Ankou in all locations except the Catacombs of Kourend for an even faster task at a higher cost.

Ankou have a modest drop table, but will yield dozens of Death runes and Blood runes in a typical task. In the Catacombs of Kourend, Ankou will also drop Ancient shards and pieces of the Dark totem.

As Ankou are Spectral creatures, carrying the Ectoplasmator will give a small amount of Prayer experience with each kill. Ankou are the only spectral monster to also drop Bones, so a charged Bonecrusher or Bonecrusher necklace can also be used to receive additional Prayer experience. In the Catacombs of Kourend, using the Bonecrusher will also restore a single prayer point with each kill.

If killing Ankou in the Wilderness, players should minimise risk and carry a One-click teleport. In both locations, players should be mindful of the level of the Wilderness around them, as the Ankou in the Wilderness Slayer Cave straddle level 20 and those in the Forgotten Cemetery straddle level 30. A teleport which can be used in the 20-30 range should be carried, such as the Royal seed pod. Both locations are hotspots for Player killing.

Aquanite.title: Slayer task/Aquanites
Aquanite.intro:
Aquanites are Slayer monsters found in the Ynysdail Cavern beneath Ynysdail. They require level 78 Slayer to fight, and accessing Ynysdail itself requires 73 Sailing and a boat equipped with an adamant keel or better.

Aquanites can be killed normally and Mortimer can assign them as a Slayer task by default; however, to receive them as a Slayer task from Nieve or Duradel, players must first unlock them for 80 Slayer reward points. A task extension is also available for 100 points.
Aquanites can drop the unique Aquanite tendon, used to make the Aquanite hopper.

Accessing Ynysdail requires the player to enter the crystalline maze from the outside, or build the rowboat hotspot on the island. This rowboat, once built, will generate another one north of Gwenith. Using this rowboat requires completion of Song of the Elves. It is recommended to complete the quest to avoid having to set the ship back to a mooring point if a greater teleport focus is not on it.

While on an Aquanite slayer task, there is a 1/200 chance (1/150 with completion of the elite tier of Combat Achievements) for an Elder Aquanite to spawn after killing an Aquanite, provided the player has the Bigger and Badder unlock. Elder Aquanites have a special attack that will deal 50 damage if Protect from Magic has been active for some time, so flicking the prayer on and off between the enemy's attacks is required to avoid taking damage.

Aquanites attack with Magic and have high accuracy, so using Protect from Magic is highly recommended. Alternatively, they can be safespotted with a 9 or 10 tile attack range. They are located in a single-way combat area, and a Dwarf multicannon cannot be used as the ground is too damp to place one.

When hit with a slash attack, an Aquanite’s lure will be severed, reducing its stab Defence by 50 (from 60 to 10). This greatly improves the accuracy of subsequent stab attacks and is especially helpful for players with lower Attack levels. Because dealing damage is not required to sever the lure, a fast 4-tick slash weapon such as a Scimitar or Abyssal whip is recommended. The Saradomin godsword's special attack can also be used if no other special attack weapons are brought along. Alternatively, a weapon that has both attack styles may be used, such as the Ghrazi rapier, while swapping between slash and stab styles.
Aquanite.strategy:
Aquanites can be killed normally; however, to receive them as a Slayer task, players must first unlock them for 80 Slayer reward points. They may be assigned by Nieve, Duradel, and Mortimer. Aquanites are found in a single-way combat area, and a Dwarf multicannon cannot be used as the ground is too damp to place one.

Aquanites attack with Magic and have high accuracy, so using Protect from Magic is highly recommended.

When killing Aquanites with melee, slash attacks have a special effect: if an Aquanite is hit with a slash attack, its lure will be severed and its stab Defence will be reduced by 50 (from 60 to 10). This significantly improves the accuracy of subsequent stab attacks and is especially useful for players with lower Attack levels.

Because dealing damage is not required to sever the lure, a fast 4-tick slash weapon such as a Scimitar or Abyssal whip is recommended. The Saradomin godsword Special attack provides an efficient option to sever the lure while also restoring Prayer points.

Dust Devil.title: Slayer task/Dust devils
Dust Devil.intro:
Dust devils can be assigned as a slayer task by various medium and high-levelled Slayer Masters upon reaching 65 Slayer and 70 combat. In order to obtain these as a Slayer task, the player must have started Desert Treasure I.

Dust devils are an incredibly popular task amongst most slayers, as they have a superior, the choke devil, and are often found in multicombat areas which allows for chinning and burst/barraging. They have relatively decent drops which usually covers the cost of supplies.

Unlike most monsters, dust devils attack with ranged melee; their attacks are considered melee, but they roll on the player's ranged defence rather than melee. They have low defence but are surprisingly accurate for their level.

Players have three options to choose from when slaying dust devils:

• Catacombs of Kourend - this is the most easily accessible location. Dust devils here have access to the Catacombs of Kourend drop table.
• Smoke Dungeon - a more remote, quiet location. A multicombat area can be found to the west for on-task purposes.
• Wilderness Slayer Cave - a somewhat busy location, can only be killed on-task. This location is in level 25-28 Wilderness, so do not bring items you are unwilling to lose. A large amount of costs can be lowered via Blighted ancient ice sacks and the dust devils here have access to the Wilderness Slayer Cave drop table.

Unless killing them as part of Konar quo Maten or Krystilia's Slayer tasks, the Catacombs of Kourend are highly recommended for their ease of accessibility.

However, the tormented bracelet is generally inefficient to use as the bracelet of slaughter will increase the task's length and maximise overall Slayer experience rates.

It is recommended to use a staff or wand that can autocast Ancient Magicks. Kodai wand provides +15% magic damage bonus as well as infinite water runes and a chance to save runes, making it the most effective.

A goading potion, darts, knives, or a blowpipe may be used to lure. The special attack of the Dinh's bulwark in conjunction with a Lightbearer may also be used to lure, however it may cause stamina issues due to its weight for players with lower agility levels.

Fossil Island Wyvern.title: Slayer task/Fossil Island wyverns
Fossil Island Wyvern.intro:
Fossil Island Wyverns are a Slayer monster requiring 66 Slayer to kill. A combat level of 60, as well as the completion of the quests Elemental Workshop and Bone Voyage, is required for them to be assigned as a slayer task.

Similarly to their skeletal cousins, Fossil Island Wyverns use both melee and an icy breath. The icy breath requires the use of an Elemental shield, Mind shield, dragonfire shield, dragonfire ward, or ancient wyvern shield in order to take reduced damage from the breath; the latter also provides immunity from being frozen. Protect from Magic can also be used but only provides half the damage reduction of the prior protections. Antifire potions of any type and the anti-dragon shield do not work to mitigate icy breath.

There are four types of wyverns that fall under this category, of which three can be fought at 66 Slayer and the other at 82 Slayer.

For players seeking a quick clear of the task, Spitting Wyverns are the best to kill, as they can also use a very weak ranged attack in place of the ice breath. Long-tailed Wyverns can also be killed and while they have a typeless ranged attack, they will only use it if the player is not in melee distance. Taloned Wyverns should be avoided, as they can use their typeless ranged attack even when the player is in melee distance. Many players also wish to purchase the Stop the Wyvern reward as a way to block the task without using the blocklist. This is because the Wyverns on fossil island are not particularly profitable, do not give good experience, and aren't the best for points.

At level 82 Slayer, the Ancient Wyvern can be killed for the purposes of this slayer task. These, much like the Taloned Wyvern, are often ignored, as they are a much stronger version of them with higher stats. They can also use a typeless ranged attack from any distance.

Wyverns may drop Fossil Island fossils of various sizes. Both caves have a Fossil Storage box by their respective entrances.

Attacks with melee, typeless ranged, and icy breath. Can use the typeless attack from any distance, making it less favourable to kill. Has higher stats but better drops compared to the other wyverns. Requires 82 Slayer to kill.

Frost Dragons.title: Frost dragon
Frost Dragons.intro:
Frost dragons are a type of adult dragon located in the dungeon on the island of Grimstone, requiring 87 Sailing to access. A combat level of 85 is required to be assigned them as a slayer task, along with the Sailing requirement to access the island and completion of Dragon Slayer I. Once players have moored on the island at least once, it can also be accessed via fairy ring code fairy ring DLP.

Like chromatic dragons, frost dragons attack with melee and short-ranged dragonfire. However, they differ in several respects: their melee defences are weakest to crush, then stab, rather than stab alone; they have a 100% elemental weakness to fire spells rather than 50% to water spells; and while heavy ranged remains the best ranged option, they are more resistant to ranged attacks overall. As with all dragons, they are weak to dragonbane weapons.

Additionally, their dragonfire is considered icy, and will briefly freeze the player if they do not have adequate protection. This icy dragonfire can be partially negated by a regular antifire potion, or fully negated using either a regular antifire potion with an anti-dragon shield, or with a super antifire potion alone. Because they only use melee and short-ranged dragonfire, frost dragons can be safespotted.

They have the highest drop rate for dragon metal sheets and dragon nails which is increased further when on a Slayer task. Loot from frost dragons spawns on their central north-eastern tile, as opposed to the south-westernmost tile for most monsters.

They do not count as blue dragons or metal dragons for Slayer tasks and instead have their own task. The odds of getting this task can be increased by 60% by purchasing the Chance of Heavy Frost unlock in the slayer rewards store. Also, the number of dragons assigned per task can be increased by purchasing the I see Dragons unlock.

Blue Dragon.title: Slayer task/Blue dragons

infobox.otherReq: Partial completion of Dragon Slayer I

Blue Dragon.intro:
Blue dragons can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 65 combat by mid- and high-level Slayer masters after starting Dragon Slayer I. They can be found in various caves across Gielinor, with most of them having some requirement to access, such as completion of quests, a dusty key, or level 70 Agility.

Blue dragons attack using melee, as well as dragonfire, for which some form of dragonfire protection should be considered. Additionally, brutal blue dragons can also attack with magic. Due to their large size, blue dragons can usually be safespotted with ranged, magic, or halberd-like weapons. Like all dragons, they are also susceptible to dragonbane weapons.

When assigned a general task of blue dragons, players who seek a fast task are recommended to bring a dwarf multicannon to Taverley Dungeon, using it against the baby blue dragons in the main dungeon, as the task-only area is full of adults. Players who want slightly more profit are recommended to kill the adult dragons. If players want the maximum profit from the task, it is highly recommended to complete Dragon Slayer II in order to access Vorkath, who has very consistent and valuable commons.

If assigned as a task by Konar quo Maten, it is recommended to skip all tasks that send the player to the Ogre Enclave, Catacombs of Kourend, or Ruins of Tapoyauik. The dragons in the enclave are very far apart, while the latter two prevent the use of a cannon. It is acceptable if she sends the player to the Isle of Souls Dungeon, as a cannon can be placed there, but the room is filled with both adults and babies.

Cave Horror.title: Slayer task/Cave horrors
Cave Horror.intro:
Cave horrors can be assigned as a slayer task starting at level 58 Slayer and 85 combat by Chaeldar, Nieve, Mortimer, and Duradel. Cave horrors are found exclusively in the Mos Le'Harmless Cave, requiring completion of Cabin Fever.

You must wear a witchwood icon to fight cave horrors at melee distance, otherwise they will use a special attack which always deals damage equal to 10% of the player's base Hitpoints level, rounded down (e.g. 9 damage at 96). This can be completely mitigated by using Protect from Melee, or using a safespot.

A light source is also required to fight them without taking additional damage, unless a fire of eternal light is lit.

Cave horrors attack with Magic-based melee, meaning that Protect from Melee will negate the damage, but high magic defence will help when not praying. They have fairly low Hitpoints, and they are relatively spread apart, so it is generally best to use a fast-firing Ranged weapon like a toxic blowpipe, magic shortbow (i), Hunters' sunlight crossbow, or Karil's crossbow. If using Melee, it is recommended to use equipment that provides high Prayer bonus (such as Proselyte armour) and always use Protect from Melee so a better amulet can be used. A dwarf multicannon can also be used to speed up kills. Cave horrors can alternatively be safespotted by using the mushrooms, stalagmites, and boulders inside the cave, such as the area by the swamp near the cave entrance.

Additionally, if using melee, it is helpful to bring a way to cast Bones to Peaches (or the tablet version) as having good magic defence lets you out-heal their damage with the peaches. This can help save prayer potions and extend trips to the cave with extra healing. A herb sack, seed box, log basket, and reagent pouch should be brought as well, as herbs, seeds, unnoted mahogany logs, and limpwurt roots are commonly dropped.

equipment.name: Prayer Melee
equipment.text:
This setup is used if planning to fight the cave horrors with use of Protect from Melee, to negate all damage and use a stronger amulet. Prayer gear should be the focus to save on prayer potions, as strength gear will have diminishing returns due to their low health making them prone to overkill damage. The abyssal whip can be substituted for any melee weapon, as cave horrors are not specifically weak to any style.
• Before obtaining a black mask, replace with the best melee strength or prayer headgear item available.
• Kandarin headgear can be substituted with any light source, or replaced with more supplies if the Fire of eternal light is built.
• Using a dragonbone necklace or bonecrusher necklace instead, can get you (close to) sustaining Protect from Melee without the use of prayer potions.

equipment.name: Witchwood Melee
equipment.text:
This setup is used if planning to fight the cave horrors without use of Protect from Melee, to save on using prayer potions. Most ranged armours are effective, as they will typically have high magic defence. The abyssal whip can be substituted for any melee weapon, as cave horrors are not specifically weak to any style.
• The Mixed hide top can be brought instead for +2 strength bonus, but -15 magic defence compared to black dragonhide.
• Runes are brought for casting Bones to Peaches to provide more food and lengthen trips, and Teleport to house to leave for resupply. Tablets for both may be brought instead, if neither is unlocked.
• Before obtaining a black mask, replace with the best melee strength or prayer headgear item available.
• Kandarin headgear can be substituted with any light source, or replaced with more supplies if the Fire of eternal light is built.

equipment.name: Ranged safespot
equipment.text:
This setup is used for safespotting the cave horrors, using one of the many safespots available throughout the cave, with some examples provided below. Any fast ranged weapon will prove effective, and no resources are needed as the player cannot be reached by the cave horrors to be attacked.
• Proselyte can be worn instead to save on prayer potions, for only a small loss in dps.
• Prayer potions are not needed if not intending to use Eagle eye.
• Runes are brought for casting Telekinetic Grab to avoid needing to leave the safespot, and Teleport to house to leave for resupply. Nature runes are simply stored in the pouch from the ones dropped by the cave horrors.
• Before obtaining or imbuing a black mask, replace with the best ranged or prayer headgear item available.
• Kandarin headgear can be substituted with any light source, or replaced with more supplies if the Fire of eternal light is built.

equipment.name: Slayer Maxed Melee
equipment.text:
This setup is used if planning to fight the cave horrors with use of Protect from Melee. This setup is for use in slayer tasks with best-in slot equipment. The bonecrusher would normally ensure no prayer potions are needed if using the saradomin godsword's special attack.
• Kandarin headgear can be substituted with any light source, or replaced with more supplies if the Fire of eternal light is built.

This setup is used if planning to fight the cave horrors with use of Protect from Melee. This setup is for use in slayer tasks with best-in slot equipment. The bonecrusher would normally ensure no prayer potions are needed if using the saradomin godsword's special attack.
• Kandarin headgear can be substituted with any light source, or replaced with more supplies if the Fire of eternal light is built.

Elves.title: Slayer task/Elves
Elves.intro:
Elves can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 70 combat by various Slayer masters after completion of Regicide. Elves either use ranged or melee, depending on their weapon; wielding either a crystal bow or a crystal halberd, of which the latter has an attack range of 2 tiles.

Until the player has access to Lletya, the only place for them to kill elves is the Iorwerth Camp. Reaching the camp can be very tedious without using an Iorwerth camp teleport, and players intending to use a dwarf multicannon are discouraged from doing so as the camp is impeded by tents, barrels, and crates. Players may prefer reanimating elves using the Arceuus spellbook spell Adept Reanimation at the Dark Altar, the ensouled heads being purchasable through the Grand Exchange, and gaining 754 Prayer experience per kill but gaining less Slayer and combat experience.

Once enough progress is made in Mourning's End Part I, players can kill elves in both Lletya and Mourner Headquarters. As with the Iorwerth Camp, getting to Lletya can be tedious, and the elves of Lletya have no notable drops other than Crystal teleport seeds. As for the Mourner Headquarters, only the level 108 mourners downstairs will count toward the task, and cannot be reached without a full set of mourner gear; the mourners upstairs do not count toward the task, despite all of them being elves.

After completing Song of the Elves, players gain access to Prifddinas and, most notably, the Iorwerth Dungeon. The dungeon contains 13 Iorwerth Warriors and allows the use of a cannon. The elves in Prifddinas (and the warriors in the dungeon) can drop crystal shards and enhanced crystal teleport seeds, which sell for a good price on the Grand Exchange. However, given their lower weight from higher-levelled slayer masters and the seed being a bit rare, players are recommended to skip elf tasks when they get the chance.

Kurask.title: Slayer task/Kurask
Kurask.intro:
Kurask can be assigned as a Slayer task by various medium and high levelled Slayer masters upon reaching 70 Slayer and 65 combat level.

Kurask are found in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon, the Iorwerth Dungeon after completing Song of the Elves, and in the Kurask Lair on Laguna Aurorae with 58 Sailing. In the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon, there is also a separate task-only area. There are two 3D models for kurask, normal and big, but this is merely a cosmetic difference as there is no difference in stats.

Kurask attack with somewhat inaccurate crush attacks that can hit up to 11. Protect from Melee will negate all their damage. For players with at least 75 Defence, there is a viable strategy to not pray against them, and instead collect their bones and occasionally cast Bones to Peaches (unlocked from the Mage Training Arena) to restore health at a significantly lower cost at the expense of moderately more attention required.

The king kurask is the superior version of the kurask unlocked with Bigger and badder. It has no special mechanics, but is significantly more accurate and has a max hit of 33. If players are using the Bones to Peaches strategy, it is advised to turn on Protect from Melee and bring at least one prayer potion in case the superior spawns.

They are weakest to stab, ranged, and magic attacks, but similarly to turoth, kurask have the leafy attribute, meaning they can only be damaged with leaf-bladed weapons (the leaf-bladed sword, battleaxe, and spear), broad-tipped ammunition (broad bolts and arrows), or the spell Magic Dart. All other weapons, spells, and other sources of damage, including cannons and thralls, will not deal any damage. However, the special attacks of the Saradomin godsword, ancient godsword, and toxic blowpipe will heal the player as if the attack performed its rolled damage. The set effect of Guthan's equipment will not activate. The Burning Claws special attack will not deal damage but it does apply burn.

Kurask can be a profitable task, as they frequently drop weapons and armour suitable for High Level Alchemy, as well as the requisite nature runes. Players should bring a herb sack as kurask always drop three herbs when they roll the herb drop table. They also drop seeds, worthwhile quantities of coins, and valuable noted stacks of white berries, big bones, coconuts, and papaya fruit. Kurask in the Iowerth Dungeon additionally drop crystal shards.

Waterfiend.title: Slayer task/Waterfiends
Waterfiend.intro:
Waterfiends can be assigned as a slayer task at 75 combat level by two Slayer masters, Konar quo Maten and Duradel. Waterfiends can only be assigned as a slayer task after being granted access to the Ancient Cavern. They are found in the Ancient Cavern, Kraken Cove, and Iorwerth Dungeon. Iorwerth Dungeon is only accessible after completing Song of the Elves.

Waterfiends attack with Magic and magical Ranged so protection Prayers cannot be used to negate all of their damage. However, both types of attacks roll against the player's Magic Defence, so armour with Magic Defence bonuses, such as fortified Masori armour, Eclipse Moon armour, or dragonhide armour is most helpful when fighting them. A saturated or imbued heart can also help slightly increase magic defence. Protect from Missiles will be the most helpful if they are dealing too much damage.

Waterfiends have low crush Defence, so crush weapons are recommended, such as a soulreaper axe (on crush), Inquisitor's mace, or abyssal bludgeon. Ranged can also be used in the case of Ranged armour being used to defend against their attacks.

Waterfiends also have a 100% elemental weakness to earth spells, which makes maging them generally faster than meleeing them, but at a greater cost. Using non-earth magic is only recommended if player has either the Eye of Ayak or Tumeken's shadow.

Bringing runes for High Level Alchemy is recommended due to their somewhat common armour and staves drops.

Because waterfiends have moderately high stats and are fairly accurate, it is advisable to skip their tasks. They do not provide as many valuable drops as other preferable Slayer monsters, aside from the mist battlestaff for Ironmen. It is not advised to block waterfiends, as they have an incredibly low weight value of 2, thus making them very unlikely to be assigned.

Zygomite.title: Slayer task/Zygomites
Zygomite.intro:
Zygomites can be assigned to level 60 combat and level 57 slayer by Chaeldar, Konar quo Maten, Nieve, and Duradel. Zygomites cannot be killed unless a fungicide spray has been used to deliver the final blow.

Zygomites can be safespotted by trapping them and moving out of their attack range. For instance, in Zanaris near the Cosmic Altar, players may trap them using a pillar and standing back near the mysterious ruins.

Players can alternatively kill Ancient Zygomites on Fossil Island or in the Stalker Den.

Custodian Stalker.title: Slayer task/Custodian stalker
Custodian Stalker.intro:
Custodian stalkers can be assigned as a Slayer task starting at level 54 by Chaeldar, Nieve, and Mortimer, and can be found in the Stalker Den after the completion of the Shadows of Custodia quest. There are multicombat areas where cannons can be placed in the south-western side of the dungeon, and single-combat caverns in the south-eastern and northern parts.

The stalkers all drop broken antlers, which are used to create atlatl dart tips for creating atlatl darts outside of subduing the Moons of Peril. The mature and elder variants are also able to drop the antler guard, a powerful off-hand item boasting offensive stats in all styles, with no defence requirement to wield. These tougher variants require a higher Slayer level to fight however, of level 67 and 76 respectively.

While most damage can be prevented with the use of Protect from Melee, once their Hitpoints get low they will use a special attack that causes a bleed effect; this attack can be blocked with Protect from Magic. When fighting multiple at once, changing prayers can be unwise, so some healing may be necessary. Gear with high magic defence such as dragonhide armour can be beneficial to reduce the amount of damage taken. Bones to Peaches can also allow the player to sustain longer trips with only prayer gear and potions. Stalkers also drop cooked fish, which may be enough to keep up with damage.

Players who wish to do this task are encouraged to get 76 Slayer in order to kill the elder stalkers. In addition to better drops, only the elders can spawn a superior slayer monster, the Ancient Custodian.

Scabarite.title: Slayer task/Scabarites
Scabarite.intro:
Scabarites refers to any of the minions of Scabaras. They are fairly strong monsters that can hit rather hard. To receive them as a Slayer assignment, players must have completed most of the Contact! quest.

When given Scabarites as a Slayer task, only small scarabs, scarab swarms, locust riders, and scarab mages will count, along with the Giant Scarab in Nightmare Zone.

Brine Rat.title: Slayer task/Brine rats
Brine Rat.intro:
Brine rats can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 47 Slayer, level 65 combat and completion of Olaf's Quest by various Slayer masters. Brine rats have relatively low Defence, but fairly high Strength and Attack. As such, it is recommended to bring food if players do not have high (~70) Defence.

Players may instead opt to bring a number of Bones to Peaches tablets to convert their bones drops to peaches, which heal 8 hitpoints each. Bringing logs and a tinderbox to cook and eat the raw rat meat and occasional drops of raw swordfish and raw shark, may also be done, though this is significantly more time-consuming and less efficient than using peaches. Alternatively, Olaf, outside the caverns, has a permanent fire located beside him, so players may cook any unnoted food drops on his fire if they are willing to exit and re-enter the caverns. A fish barrel can be used to store the unnoted raw fish, though these drops are infrequent.

There are two safespots, one being the black bones to the south-east, and the other in the north-west corner of the cave. If the brine rats are in the north half of the cave, you are able to safespot them from behind the bones in the corner.

Rat bone weapons can be used to kill brine rats and have an added 10 hitpoints of damage added to the player's max hit, making these weapons incredibly effective compared to other weapons with similar stats. Even compared to the highest tier weapons, rat bone weapons might still be more effective depending on your stats and boosts, as the difference in max hit based on other weapon's strength bonuses might not be enough to reach 10 hitpoints of extra damage towards their max hit.

Turoth.title: Slayer task/Turoth
Turoth.intro:
Turoth can be assigned as a Slayer task from Vannaka, Nieve/Steve, Chaeldar, Konar quo Maten, or Mortimer, requiring 55 Slayer and 60 combat. They are melee based, and as such Protect from Melee will negate all of their damage. They are only found in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon.

Turoth can only be damaged with leaf-bladed weapons, broad arrows and bolts, or the Magic Dart spell. Attacking with any other weapons or spells will always deal 0 damage.

The superior variant is the spiked turoth; the Bigger and Badder Slayer reward must be unlocked for it to spawn.

Due to their high herb drop rates, it is recommended players bring a herb sack with them for the task if they have one.

Hydra.title: Slayer task/Hydras
Hydra.intro:
Hydras can be assigned as a slayer task at level 95 Slayer. This is a task exclusive to both Konar quo Maten and Mortimer; the latter requires partial completion of Fallen From Grace.

Mortimer is the best way for players to obtain hydra tasks. Not only does Mortimer assign more on average, he also has various incentives when completing these tasks from him, such as additional kills, increased clue scrolls or superior drop rates. Given the nature of his assignments however, players should try to complete the task accordingly to benefit from the incentive. Mortimer has a small pool of tasks, and coupled with his unique ability for the player to assign themselves appropriately from two or three (after completing 50 tasks with him), means it is very easy to be given hydras from him. Assuming that every task can be offered with two of the normal tasks (which have a weight of 10) are blocked, there is a 4.0% chance for hydras to be offered.

Konar, the original master who could assign hydras, has a huge pool despite having a total lower weight of 250. To get the best possible chance to be given a hydra task, the player must block a lot of other tasks, especially ones that are the same, close to or higher than hers, such as metal dragons, drakes and wyrms (both of which share the same weight as hydra tasks). Because of the larger pool of tasks and traditional slayer assignments, it is harder to get a task from Konar compared to Mortimer, and the only incentive for completing the task from Konar are slayer points and the chance for brimstone keys.

There are two different types of hydras: normal hydras and the Alchemical Hydra, both of which are only found in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. The dungeon requires the player to wear boots of stone, boots of brimstone or granite boots to protect themselves from the extreme heat of the dungeon floor, unless the player has completed the Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary.

Hydras start off with a random combat style between ranged and magic at the start of the battle, switching randomly between one and three attacks, regardless if they hit or not. After the first switch they will only switch after three attacks of the same type. If the hydra still persists after roughly 30 seconds (or they are on their 12th attack) into a fight, it will spit poison at three random tiles (one at the player's location, two elsewhere), dealing 4 poison damage every two ticks (or 1 to 2 damage if the player has poison immunity) when the player is standing on one. The initial splat has a 3x3 AoE. It is recommended to start by activating the protection prayer that protects the player against the attack style they have lowest defence towards, typically magic if wearing melee armour or ranged if wearing ranged armour, then switching to the other protection prayer if the hydra starts with an attack of the other style.

Normal hydras additionally have a superior, the Colossal Hydra. These hydras share the same normal attacks, but rather than spitting poison, they launch electricity at the player in a manner similar to that of the lightning phase of the Alchemical Hydra.

A boss variant, the Alchemical Hydra, can be killed in place of normal hydras. This boss has very lucrative commons and players can last a long time in the arena without needing to bank, along with a large health pool meaning lots of experience gained per kill.

In general, if the player is seeking a somewhat fast task with a good chance of getting an imbued heart, players should kill normal hydras, as colossal hydras have the highest drop rate for it, at 1/160. If players are wishing to maximise the most profit or collection log slots, they should kill the boss instead. Ranged is a common option regardless of the route taken, as both have very high Magic levels, making the twisted bow very effective on them, while the distance provided from ranged makes attacks easier to dodge. Dragonbane weapons are a good second option (unless using melee, in which it is the best), though this makes hydra attacks harder to avoid.

Jelly.title: Slayer task/Jellies
Jelly.intro:
Jellies can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 52 Slayer and level 57 combat by various medium-level Slayer masters. They are found in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon. They are popular to kill similarly to hellhounds due to their high drop rate of hard clue scrolls. While fairly weak, jellies have an unusually high Defence level compared to other similar monsters around their level.

It is not recommended to kill normal jellies in most circumstances as they have a fairly poor drop table and are very far from a bank.

Two stronger variants of jellies can be found on Zeah; the Warped Jelly in the Catacombs of Kourend, and the Chilled jelly in the Ruins of Tapoyauik/Grimstone Dungeon.

Warped jellies are in a Multicombat area and are popular for barrage tasks, along with having a better drop table and the Catacombs table. Chilled jellies are in a single combat area and require completion of The Heart of Darkness or level 87 Sailing; they have the exact same table as warped jellies (except without the Catacombs table and including frozen tear and moon tooth half drops if fought in the Ruins of Tapoyauik), but have a 50% susceptibility to fire spells. Despite their higher Magic level, they are still easy to hit with magic.

Players who are assigned jellies by Krystilia can kill them in the Wilderness Slayer Cave, where nine jellies can be found in a multicombat area. As this location is in the Wilderness, players should be mindful of the risk they bring and not bring items they are unwilling to lose, as the cave is a popular player killing hotspot. There is only one entrance to the jellies and they are below level 30 Wilderness, so players can easily escape with a one-click teleport such as a royal seed pod if any player killers arrive.

Lesser Nagua.title: Slayer task/Lesser Nagua
Lesser Nagua.intro:
Lesser Nagua are a potential Slayer assignment rarely assigned by Konar quo Maten or Chaeldar after completion of Perilous Moons.

Players have three options when assigned Lesser Nagua, depending on their quest completion:
• Players who have completed Perilous Moons can be assigned to kill Nagua at Neypotzli, where Sulphur Nagua can be found.
• Players who have completed The Heart of Darkness can be assigned to kill Nagua at the Ruins of Tapoyauik, where Frost Nagua and Amoxliatl can be found.
• Players who have completed The Final Dawn can also be assigned to kill Nagua at the Crypt of Tonali, where Earthen Nagua can be found.

Nagua are very popular for mid-level players for AFK combat, especially at Neypotzli where supplies are basically free as food is plentiful within and both prayer and combat potions are filled by moonlight potions, which act as a super combat, divine super defence, and prayer potion.

Sulphur Nagua have a special attack used every 5 auto-attacks that drains 5 prayer points if not avoided, though it is generally ignored given the amount of free supplies that can be found in the prison.

Frost Nagua will periodically mark the tile the player is on, which drains prayer if not avoided. There are four Moonlight Moths available at each of the four corners of the frozen platform. Players with 75 hunter along with an insect net (85 for barehanded) and optionally a Butterfly Jar can catch and use them to restore 22 prayer points.

Earthen Nagua have a unique mechanic in which they will add armour onto themselves upon reaching 60% or less hitpoints, shuffling their melee defence; they become slightly more resistant to stab and slash attacks, but are much weaker to crush attacks.

All Lesser Nagua make use of flat armour, which increases/decreases damage dealt to them. Fortunately for Lesser Nagua, they have negative flat armour, so attacks will deal more damage to them. This means that weapons that make multiple hitsplats are generally more effective, such as the Dual Macuahuitl. Sulphur, Frost, and Earthen Nagua all have -4 flat armour, while Amoxliatl has -2 flat armour.

Alternatively, those assigned Nagua at the Ruins of Tapoyauik may kill Amoxliatl, a boss variant of the frost Nagua. She has better drops compared to frost Nagua.

Since the task is rare (1-2% chance to be assigned) consider using Bracelets of Slaughter if doing lesser Nagua bosses (perilous moons don't count for this task).

Ice Warrior.title: Ice warrior
Ice Warrior.intro:
Ice warriors are mid-level ice elementals. They have a 100% elemental weakness to fire spells. Ice warriors can be assigned by Krystilia for a Wilderness Slayer task, or by Vannaka or Mazchna for normal tasks.

The ice warriors in the Ice Queen's Lair, the Ice Queen's Royal Guard, will become aggressive to the player if the player goes near the Ice Queen, even if the ice warriors would otherwise be tolerant.
Ice Warrior.strategy:
Ice warriors have good accuracy and can cut through Ranged and Magic armour with ease. They also seem to have higher levels of aggression than many other mobs as they'll often engage the player from a rather long distance. If using melee, wearing at least adamant or rune armour and using high quality food is advised.

Fire spells are extremely strong against ice warriors. Using fire bolt with chaos gauntlets is an economical option and gives you a max hit of 30. If you receive ice warriors as a Slayer task, using your best fire spell will most likely be the fastest way to complete the task.

In the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon, they can be safespotted by trapping an ice warrior on one side of a plus-shaped formation of rocks (not to be confused with the floor ice spikes) in the north-western area of their room.

At the White Wolf Mountain they can be safespotted south of the middle dungeon marker outside of the triple ladder enclosure, though there are level 25 and 38 wolves which will be aggressive unless the player's combat level exceeds double their level.

Magic Axe.title: Magic axe
Magic Axe.intro:
Magic axes are monsters that resemble translucent iron battleaxes.

The axes in the magic axe hut can be given as a wilderness Slayer assignment by Krystilia. Players require 32 Thieving for magic axes to be assigned as a task.

Bear.title: Slayer task/Bears
Bear.intro:
Bears can be assigned as a slayer task at level 13 combat by various low-level Slayer masters. Bears can be found in various locations throughout Gielinor.

Black bears, bear cubs, grizzly bears, grizzly bear cubs, reanimated bears, Artio, and Callisto can all be killed to satisfy the task. Angry bears (found in Tolna's rift), the Headless Beast (fought during the quest Getting Ahead), and the Crystalline and Corrupted Bear (fought in the Gauntlet and the Corrupted Gauntlet respectively) do not count towards the task.

Those with lower combat levels would find it in their best interest to kill bear cubs, found in the Fremennik Province and throughout Kourend. Black bears would also be a good option, with a combat level of 19. Grizzly bears in most cases are an option if they are close, as most are level 21 combat. The only level 42 combat grizzly bears are found in Tirannwn. Grizzly bear cubs, too, can only be found in Tirannwn, with combat levels ranging from 33 to 36.

Players with 21 Magic, ensouled bear heads, may find casting Basic Reanimation and killing reanimated bears easier compared to regular bears, due to their lower hitpoints.

Players who seek a greater challenge or assigned bears by Krystilia can opt to kill Callisto or Artio for their slayer task, as they count towards it and provide a generous amount of drops. They are especially popular for Wilderness slayer due to their higher value. Remember that both bear bosses reside in the Wilderness, and it is not recommended for players to bring items they are unwilling to lose. Accessing Artio requires completion of the Hard Wilderness Diary, while Callisto only requires the Medium Wilderness Diary but is located in significantly deeper Wilderness that is a Multicombat area. A one-time fee of is required to access the boss, which must be paid again if the player dies to another player in the Wilderness.

Ice Giant.title: Slayer task/Ice giants
Ice Giant.intro:
Ice giants can be assigned as a Slayer task at 50 combat by Vannaka and Krystilia. They are the second strongest generic giants for their category, only slightly stronger than their mossy counterparts, with very slight defensive bonuses and having a 100% weakness to fire spells.

Ice giant tasks are generally not completed by players not training via Wilderness Slayer, as they have very unimpressive drops and many of them are far from a bank.

They are primarily killed as part of Krystilia's Slayer tasks, as a cluster of 14 slightly stronger ice giants can be found in the Wilderness Slayer Cave. These giants are found below level 20 Wilderness and are cannonable in a multicombat area, making it a very quick task for plenty of points. As the cave is a popular player killing spot, players should not take items they are unwilling to lose. Normal ice giants can be found at the Frozen Waste Plateau, but escape is next to impossible if caught by a player killer.

Eldric the Ice King, part of a duo that makes up the Royal Titans encounter, can be killed in place of normal ice giants if assigned by Vannaka. The task buffs will not apply for his counterpart, Branda the Fire Queen.

The giants located at the ground level of the White Wolf Mountain are rather tricky to reach. To reach them, mine the boulder located west of the ice warriors (requires 50 Mining) and climb down the southernmost ladder, then take the south-west path leading to another ladder, then climb up. Once you come up the ladder, the first two can be safespotted by the trees. Alternatively, you can use a ranged weapon to hit them from the mountain path, but this puts you at risk of being hit by the wolves (something to take into account if you're a low-level).

The giants in the Settlement Ruins can be safespotted in many places using any of the destroyed buildings or ice chunks scattered around the location. The ice spiders nearby are only aggressive if you stand adjacent to them, and can be easily trapped if you accidentally draw their attention, so they're of little concern. A cannon can be used at this location and it is multi-combat.

Lesser Demon.title: Slayer task/Lesser demon
Lesser Demon.intro:
Lesser demons can be assigned by Krystilia, Chaeldar, and Vannaka. They are combat level 82, 87, and 94 and all have the same drop table, with the exception of the Wilderness Slayer Cave.

When not killing lesser demons as part of a Krystilia task, players have many spots to choose from to kill lesser demons.

The most common spots would be the Chasm of Fire and Catacombs of Kourend. The former can drop contracts after speaking to Yama after A Kingdom Divided, which makes killing the demons there much more lucrative compared to any other spot. However, catering to the preferred method will slow down times. There are four demons in a very small area, which allows for easy AFK times. The demons in the Catacombs are in a multicombat area and can be AFK'ed with access to the catacombs table, but a dwarf multicannon is not allowed. If none of these locations are available, it is best to kill them in the Crandor and Karamja Dungeon; the southern area contains six lesser demons with a fair amount of safespots and allows a cannon.

In the Wilderness, players have a few options to kill lesser demons. The only reasonable location is the Wilderness Slayer Cave, as the demons have better drops, allows a cannon and is a multicombat area. The demons are below level 30 Wilderness, so a one-click teleport such as a royal seed pod will allow for an easy escape. In the event of player killers, the player may also use the two shortcuts to escape, which requires 77 Agility (which is boostable). The other locations where they can be found are past level 40 Wilderness, making it impossible to teleport away in the event of an attack, and are near high-traffic areas which further complicates the problem.

Mammoth.title: Mammoth
Mammoth.intro:
Mammoths are a species of elephant-like creatures that inhabit the area south-east of the Ferox Enclave. They are not very intelligent.

Mammoths can be easily safespotted due to their large size (3x3). Players can use the many trees or tree stumps in the area to safespot them from behind. It is an efficient place to train with a Dwarf multicannon due to the high hitpoints of the Mammoths, a nearby altar providing unlimited Prayer for boosts, and the short walk to the Enclave for resupplying. However, players are vulnerable to player killers while training and are therefore advised not to carry too many supplies on them at once.

Killing a Mammoth is a task in the Easy Wilderness Diary.

Spider.title: Slayer task/Spiders
Spider.intro:
Spiders can be assigned as a Slayer task by Turael, Spria, and Krystilia. They can be found in numerous places across Gielinor.

Most spiders generally use melee, but a few stronger ones will also use Ranged and/or Magic alongside them. Low-levelled spiders are generally weak to all forms of combat, though higher-levelled spiders are weaker to crush.

There are many varieties of spiders that players can kill as part of a Slayer task, though for low-levels, the spiders around Lumbridge are a reasonable spot.

Due to the low number of spiders assigned by the Slayer masters, it is generally recommended to not kill the minions when fighting Sarachnis if choosing to fight her for the task, as she spawns four minions per fight when faced solo, which can quickly end the task.

Araxytes can be killed in place of a spider task, though this option requires 92 Slayer in order to fight them. A boost from wild pie can be used at 87 Slayer, but it is recommended to wait at least until 90 Slayer before using boosts for a reasonable amount of uptime. Killing the minions in this encounter does not decrement the task, but will still grant Slayer experience.

Players who seek a greater challenge or assigned spiders by Krystilia can opt to kill Venenatis or Spindel for their Slayer task, as they count towards it and provide a generous amount of drops. They are especially popular for Wilderness Slayer due to their higher value. Remember that both reside in the Wilderness, and it is not recommended for players to bring items they are unwilling to lose. Accessing Spindel requires completion of the Hard Wilderness Diary, while Venenatis only requires the Medium Wilderness Diary but is located in significantly deeper Wilderness that is a multicombat area. A one-time fee of coins is required to access the boss, which must be paid again if the player dies to another player within any of the wilderness bosses respective lairs. Taking out the Spiderlings in either fight will not decrement the player's Slayer task.

If the player is assigned spiders by Krystilia but does not want to kill the spider bosses, it is recommended they head to the "spider hill" (located around level 46 Wilderness, with a cut sapphire being the location's landmark) and place a cannon there with very little risk. All of the spiders here are aggressive with low hitpoints, making the task breeze by in a matter of minutes. Alternatively, the player can bring a very fast ranged attack weapon (such as darts or knives) to very quickly kill the Level 1 spiderlings, which have 2 HP each, so that even a task of 100 spiders can be completed in about 5 minutes without using a cannon.

Scorpion.title: Slayer task/Scorpions
Scorpion.intro:
Scorpions can be assigned as a slayer task at level 7 combat by various low end Slayer masters and are generally meant as tasks for beginners. Scorpions attack with melee and a few certain varieties are capable of poisoning. Interestingly various fightable lobsters also counts as scorpions.
Scorpions have very limited drop tables, usually only dropping ensouled scorpion heads and beginner clue scrolls.

Players can also kill Scorpia as part of a scorpion task; however, she is located in extremely deep (50+) Wilderness in a multicombat area, and freezes are required in order to kill the boss efficiently. It is a very popular player killing spot, so players should not bring items they are unwilling to lose.

Abyssal Demons.title: Slayer task/Abyssal demons

infobox.otherReq: Priest in Peril or Fairytale II - Cure a Queen

Abyssal Demons.intro:
At level 85 Slayer and Combat level, the player may be assigned Abyssal demons by mid and high levelled Slayer Masters and Krystilia. They can be found in the Abyssal Area, the Catacombs of Kourend, the Wilderness Slayer Cave, and in the Slayer Tower, where they are found on the third floor and in the task-only basement.

Abyssal demons use a fairly accurate melee stab attack, but with a relatively low max hit of 8. With Bigger and badder unlocked, the Greater abyssal demon has a chance to spawn as a Superior slayer monster. The greater abyssal demon is much more powerful and accurate with a max hit of 27. Protect from Melee will neutralise all damage taken from either variation.

Players on abyssal demon tasks may also opt to kill the Abyssal Sire boss instead, which can be very profitable as compensation for significantly lower experience rates compared to Abyssal demons.

Abyssal demons have a unique mechanic in which they frequently teleport around the area they're being attacked in. They also have a high chance to teleport the player up to 20 tiles away. It is highly recommended to acquire and read a Teleport anchoring scroll before fighting Abyssal demons for the first time, as this will eliminate the chance for the player to be teleported. If the player doesn't have access to the anchoring scroll, it is recommended to enable Auto Retaliate to continue attacking after being teleported. The greater abyssal demon also teleports around the player, and afterward will always land a successful hit if its attack is not prayed against. By having only two open sides through backing yourself into a corner, you can maximize multi-target ice spells since they will no longer be able to teleport behind you. This is best combined with either goading potions in the Catacombs of Kourend or a dwarf multicannon in the Wilderness Slayer Cave.

Abyssal demons are Demons, meaning they are subject to the various accuracy and damage bonuses of Demonbane Weaponry including Arclight, Emberlight, the Scorching bow, and Demonbane spells, although generally, these are not used in favour of damage dealt through area of effect damage.

Because they potentially offer high rates of Slayer experience, players should extend Abyssal demons as soon as possible.

The drop table for Abyssal demons is generally unremarkable with a few exceptions. They drop the Abyssal whip at a 1/512 rate, and therefore will drop an average of one whip every other extended task. They are also one of the only sources of the Abyssal dagger, but this is an extremely rare drop. Ensouled abyssal heads will appear several times in a task, making a Soul bearer useful. The Herb sack will also allow the player to profit further, and an Explorer's ring 4 may be used for the few alchable items among their drops. Abyssal demons in the Catacombs of Kourend also have access to that location's drop table which includes pieces of the Dark totem. Greater abyssal demons in the Catacombs will always drop a piece of the Dark totem.
Abyssal Demons.strategy:
The Wilderness Slayer Cave is the only location in which a Cannon can be used against Abyssal demons, although as part of the Wilderness, it is also a Player killing hotspot. The Wilderness Slayer Cave also allows taking advantage of cheaper Blighted supplies and the passive effects of the Accursed sceptre (a) and other weapons charged with Revenant ether.

With their 1x1 size, Abyssal demons are ideal for use with area of effect weapons including the Venator bow and Ancient Magicks. The Catacombs and Wilderness Slayer Cave are the only two Multicombat areas with Abyssal demons. As Abyssal demons are not aggressive, a method to cause them to attack the player, such as Dinh's bulwark or a Goading potion, is recommended.

Because of the teleportation mechanic, Smoke Barrage or Smoke Burst are favoured over their Ice equivalents. After teleporting away, frozen abyssal demons will not move back toward the player until they're unfrozen. Blood spells are significantly more expensive than Smoke and are not recommended.

Killing Abyssal demons outside multicombat areas, usually done only on a Konar task, will result in a slower task requiring more attention. If required to kill Abyssal demons in a single combat zone, it's recommended to use an Expeditious bracelet with a melee setup.

If the player is comfortable with the risk, Abyssal demons in the Wilderness Slayer Cave will provide some of the best rates of Slayer experience in the game. Abyssal demons in the Catacombs are still an outstanding source of experience.

By having only two open sides through backing yourself into a corner, you can maximize multi-target ice spells since they will no longer be able to teleport behind you. This is best combined with either goading potions in the Catacombs of Kourend or a dwarf multicannon in the Wilderness Slayer Cave.

equipment.name: Catacombs magic
equipment.text:
This is the recommended equipment for barraging or bursting abyssal demons in the Catacombs of Kourend.

Abyssal demons in the Catacombs are excellent experience due to the AoE effect of ancients; The chambers contain plenty of spawns that can be grouped together for barraging or bursting, making them highly suited for multitarget strategies. This means they're some of the highest slayer experience in the game, and therefore the bracelet of slaughter is preferable over a tormented bracelet or confliction gauntlet as it will increase task length. This is especially true for player looking to train their slayer and magic levels.

Because abyssal demons have low magic defence, magic damage and prayer bonus should be prioritised over magic accuracy. Magic attack bonuses are far less important than damage multipliers.

equipment.name: Wilderness slayer cave
equipment.text:
The cannon will not be lost if you die while it is placed on the ground.

The accursed sceptre (a) is notable here, as it provides a 50% boost to both Magic accuracy and damage against any NPC in the Wilderness, making it a powerful option. This effect stacks with the slayer helmet (i). Players should 3-item, or 4-item if using Protect Item, keeping only their sceptre and a few key magic strength pieces as their core items that are kept on death. The rest of the setup can consist of inexpensive equipment, such as monk's robes, bracelet of slaughter, and free items like the completed book of darkness.

Blighted supplies are recommended for food and prayer restoration as well as blighted ice sacks. This is because they are inexpensive and top tier, but can only be used in the wilderness.

equipment.name: Melee
equipment.text:
Meleeing abyssal demons offers good experience and easily allows the player access to the Arceuus spellbook for offering spells, thralls, and death charge. If in the Slayer tower bonus experience will also be awarded, scaling with completion of the Morytania Diary.

Use of demonbane weaponry like Arclight or Emberlight is strongly recommended for highest damage output.

Chaos Druid.title: Chaos druid
Chaos Druid.intro:
Chaos druids are low-level humans commonly killed for their frequent drops of herbs. Unlike other druids, they worship Zamorak. They attack with their fists and make use of a spell that appears to be a combination of the Confuse and Bind spells, binding their target very briefly if successful.

Players who decide to kill chaos druids in the Edgeville Dungeon should beware of player killers who disguise themselves in Zamorak robes to take on the appearance of a chaos druid. If you attack another player, you will become skulled and potentially lose all of your items.

Dust Devils.title: Slayer task/Dust devils
Dust Devils.intro:
Dust devils can be assigned as a slayer task by various medium and high-levelled Slayer Masters upon reaching 65 Slayer and 70 combat. In order to obtain these as a Slayer task, the player must have started Desert Treasure I.

Dust devils are an incredibly popular task amongst most slayers, as they have a superior, the choke devil, and are often found in multicombat areas which allows for chinning and burst/barraging. They have relatively decent drops which usually covers the cost of supplies.

Unlike most monsters, dust devils attack with ranged melee; their attacks are considered melee, but they roll on the player's ranged defence rather than melee. They have low defence but are surprisingly accurate for their level.

Players have three options to choose from when slaying dust devils:

• Catacombs of Kourend - this is the most easily accessible location. Dust devils here have access to the Catacombs of Kourend drop table.
• Smoke Dungeon - a more remote, quiet location. A multicombat area can be found to the west for on-task purposes.
• Wilderness Slayer Cave - a somewhat busy location, can only be killed on-task. This location is in level 25-28 Wilderness, so do not bring items you are unwilling to lose. A large amount of costs can be lowered via Blighted ancient ice sacks and the dust devils here have access to the Wilderness Slayer Cave drop table.

Unless killing them as part of Konar quo Maten or Krystilia's Slayer tasks, the Catacombs of Kourend are highly recommended for their ease of accessibility.

equipment.name: Magic (Barrage)
equipment.text:
The confliction gauntlets (+7%) or tormented bracelet (+5%), occult necklace (+5%), Virtus robes (+5% each when using Ancient Magicks) or Ancestral robes (+3% each), and imbued god capes (+2%) increase the maximum hit of the player's Magic spells. However, the tormented bracelet is generally inefficient to use as the bracelet of slaughter will increase the task's length and maximise overall Slayer experience rates.

It is recommended to use a staff or wand that can autocast Ancient Magicks. Kodai wand provides +15% magic damage bonus as well as infinite water runes and a chance to save runes, making it the most effective.

A goading potion, darts, knives, or a blowpipe may be used to lure. The special attack of the Dinh's bulwark in conjunction with a Lightbearer may also be used to lure, however it may cause stamina issues due to its weight for players with lower agility levels.

Ent.title: Ent
Ent.intro:
Ents are monsters found in the ent cavern beneath the Woodcutting Guild and in the forests north and east of the Chaos Temple. Ents are found on members' worlds exclusively.

Upon death, the ent's trunk will fall and remain on the ground for 1 minute. These remains can be chopped to give several sets of noted logs according to the player's Woodcutting level. Players also have a chance to receive a bird nest while chopping the ent trunk. While cutting the trunk, players get 25 experience per set of logs received no matter the type. Completing the medium Wilderness Diary increases the chance of successfully chopping ents in the Wilderness by 15%. Ents can be safespotted by moving 1-3 tiles adjacent to a tree and using a ranged weapon, halberd, or magic attack.

Chopping the trunks requires an axe that the player has the Woodcutting level to use. The type of logs that can be received is determined by a player's base Woodcutting level, with higher levels giving better logs. The chance to successfully receive logs is determined by the player's current Woodcutting level (boosted or drained), with higher levels increasing success chance. The distribution of log types is determined by the axe used, with better axes providing a greater amount of higher tier logs.

While Ents do drop slayer's enchantments, while on a Wilderness slayer task, they do not drop looting bags or Larran's keys. Unlike logs which are chopped from the trunk, slayer's enchantments are dropped when the ent is kil

Jellies.title: Slayer task/Jellies
Jellies.intro:
Jellies can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 52 Slayer and level 57 combat by various medium-level Slayer masters. They are found in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon. They are popular to kill similarly to hellhounds due to their high drop rate of hard clue scrolls. While fairly weak, jellies have an unusually high Defence level compared to other similar monsters around their level.

It is not recommended to kill normal jellies in most circumstances as they have a fairly poor drop table and are very far from a bank.

Two stronger variants of jellies can be found on Zeah; the Warped Jelly in the Catacombs of Kourend, and the Chilled jelly in the Ruins of Tapoyauik/Grimstone Dungeon.

Warped jellies are in a Multicombat area and are popular for barrage tasks, along with having a better drop table and the Catacombs table. Chilled jellies are in a single combat area and require completion of The Heart of Darkness or level 87 Sailing; they have the exact same table as warped jellies (except without the Catacombs table and including frozen tear and moon tooth half drops if fought in the Ruins of Tapoyauik), but have a 50% susceptibility to fire spells. Despite their higher Magic level, they are still easy to hit with magic.

Players who are assigned jellies by Krystilia can kill them in the Wilderness Slayer Cave, where nine jellies can be found in a multicombat area. As this location is in the Wilderness, players should be mindful of the risk they bring and not bring items they are unwilling to lose, as the cave is a popular player killing hotspot. There is only one entrance to the jellies and they are below level 30 Wilderness, so players can easily escape with a one-click teleport such as a royal seed pod if any player killers arrive.

Revenant.title: Revenants
Revenant.intro:
Revenants are the ghostly versions of creatures slain during the God Wars found in the Revenant Caves within the Wilderness in levels 19 to 40. They are capable of hitting high and accurately for their combat levels, although most of the damage can be mitigated with a charged bracelet of ethereum. As the Revenant Caves location is members-only, all revenants are members-only creatures.

Revenants have a fairly generous drop table, but as they are in the Wilderness, the player is always at risk of getting killed by other players. Due to the revenants' lucrativeness, player killers are common. The caves they inhabit are singles-plus combat, where PvP situations take priority over PvM: a player in combat with a revenant can be attacked by another player.

Unique drops from the revenants include the Wilderness weapons, a set of weapons that have increased effectiveness against monsters in the Wilderness when charged with revenant ether. They also drop various ancient artefacts, which can be sold to the Emblem Trader wandering within the Revenant Caves for a set amount of coins, as well as ancient crystals, four of which are used to construct an obelisk in the superior garden of a player-owned house.

Rogue.title: Rogue
Rogue.intro:
Rogues are human monsters that can also be pickpocketed, with level 32 Thieving. Pickpocketing a rogue grants 36.5 Thieving experience. It is the only pickpocketing target found exclusively in the Wilderness. The level 135 variant cannot be pickpocketed.

Unlike many other NPCs found in the Wilderness, rogues are not hostile and will only attack players if provoked or if they try to loot the chests within their castle.

Skeleton.title: Slayer task/Skeletons
Skeleton.intro:
Skeletons are undead monsters that can be assigned as tasks at combat level 15 by various low-level Slayer masters. They are often found in cemeteries and dungeons. A good strategy to kill them is to use melee with a weapon with crush bonuses (such as a Viggora's chainmace) and a salve amulet or salve amulet (e), due to their low crush defence.

Another strategy to kill them would be with magic. Many skeletons have an elemental weakness to earth spells, making those a very effective option.

Players who seek a greater challenge can choose to kill Vet'ion or Calvar'ion. These bosses are significantly stronger than the typical skeleton, but provide plenty of rewards for players who seek to kill them. In order to access Calvar'ion, the player must have completed the Hard Wilderness Diary. Vet'ion only requires completing the Medium Wilderness Diary, but is deeper in the Wilderness and resides in a multicombat area. Accessing the bosses requires a one-time payment of coins, which must be repaid again if the player dies to another player in the Wilderness. Note that the skeletal hellhounds they summon also count towards the task, so every kill at the boss is equal to five skeletons per spawn.

If players are not seeking to kill either skeleton boss but are assigned them in the Wilderness, an ideal location would be the Edgeville Dungeon, as there is a good cluster of skeletons that can be easily cannoned and has a quick escape, provided that the player is paying attention.

Bandit.title: Slayer task/Bandits
Bandit.intro:
Bandit can be assigned as a slayer task. It does not have a required combat level to be assigned by Krystilia. Bandits are most commonly found in Bandit Camp (Wilderness).

Along with Bandits and Guard Bandits, Speedy Keith, Donny the lad, and Black Heather can be killed to satisfy the task.

The bandits are guarded by Guard Bandit. These bandits are aggressive, so players should take caution when approaching the camp. However, camp leaders (like Donny the lad) are not aggressive.

If you'd like to prioritize barraging the level 130 bandits, you can setup a cannon slightly southwest of the first spear wall near the entrance. This extends the task as you'll only rarely target a single lower level bandit while being able to barrage up to 7 or 8 high level bandits. Their far aggressive range, high hitpoints and fast respawn time make it an effective task for experience. You can quickly teleport out to regain aggression.
