Dark Warrior.title: Dark warrior
Dark Warrior.intro:
Dark warriors are mainly found in the Dark Warriors' Fortress, a castle in level 12 to 16 Wilderness north-west of Edgeville. Some dark warriors can also be found in Great Kourend, accompanying necromancers. The warriors in Great Kourend are different combat levels than those found in the Wilderness.

Dark warriors found in the fortress come in both level 8 and 145 variants, the latter of which only appears in members' worlds. The area is multi-combat and a Dwarf multicannon can be set up in the centre of the inner courtyard of the fortress. To speed up a Krystilia Slayer task, it is possible for the player to focus on the Level 8 Dark warriors roaming the corridors of the fortress, while leaving the cannon to deal with the Level 145 ones inside the courtyard, making sure to close the courtyard doors so that the warriors don't get out of range of the cannon by going inside the corridors.

Alternately, for those looking for a barrage task with high hitpoint, fast respawning, and aggressive monsters, you can setup a cannon in the middle of the courtyard. If you see more than one warrior in the room east of the courtyard, you can tag them to bring them back into the centre where they will respawn. You can nestle yourself in the northeast part of the room, in the corner of two crates, and the warriors will either spawn under or near you, and target you soon after respawning.

Green Dragon.title: Slayer task/Green dragons

infobox.otherReq: Partial completion of Dragon Slayer I

Green Dragon.intro:
Green dragons can be assigned as a slayer task at level 52 combat by Krystilia after partial completion of Dragon Slayer I. As Krystilia is the only Slayer master to assign green dragons, they must be fought in the Wilderness, and other variants outside the Wilderness do not count. They attack with melee and dragonfire, thus some protection against it should be considered. Due to their large size, they are usually able to be safespotted with ranged or halberd-like weapons. As dragons, they are also weak to dragonbane weapons.

A majority of dragons are above the level 20 line, thus a level 30 teleport such as an amulet of glory or royal seed pod is recommended for escaping player killers. A small cluster of three dragons can be found below level 20 Wilderness just west of the Dark Warriors' Fortress, making it ideal for killing with good attention, as the use of a teleport tab is enough to escape any hostile players. The dragons near the Lava Maze are above level 30 Wilderness, and thus it is not recommended to kill them there.

Moss Giant.title: Slayer task/Moss giants
Moss Giant.intro:
Moss giants can be assigned as a Slayer task from Slayer Masters Vannaka, starting from level 40 combat, and Krystilia, at any combat level. Bryophyta can be slain in their stead.

Moss giants are located across Gielinor and most of these locations have safespots. Moss giants have zero defence against every attack style and are 50% weak to fire damage. Their most notable drops are the mossy key (required to loot Bryophyta's chest) and their somewhat valuable seed drop table. The mossy key drop rate is improved to 1/75 while slaying moss giants on task.

Bryophyta, the moss giant boss, drops mossy keys at a much higher rate of 1/8 while on a moss giant slayer task.

Moss giants slain in the Catacombs of Kourend (or the Giants' Den) may drop the dark totem pieces at a rate of 1/440 each. Like all monsters killed on task for Krystilia, moss giants also have a chance to drop the slayer's enchantment (1/272) or a Larran's key (1/533).

Black Knight.title: Black Knight
Black Knight.intro:
Black knights, also known as the Kinshra, are Zamorakian warriors found mainly in their fortress and stronghold. They are central to the Black Knights' Fortress quest.

Once Wanted! has been completed, black knights can be slain in order to increase the player's White Knight rank. As their rank gets higher, they unlock more white equipment. Even though the quest, as well as white equipment, is only for members, non-members are still able to increase their rank.

Hill Giant.title: Slayer task/Hill giants
Hill Giant.intro:
Hill giants can be assigned as a slayer task from Mazchna and Vannaka at level 25 combat. Hill giants can be found many places both above and under ground. They all attack with melee. They always drop big bones and their drop table includes runes, herbs, limpwurt roots and the giant key, which is required to access the hill giant boss Obor. Cyclopes also count as hill giants for tasks.

Lava Dragon.title: Lava dragon
Lava Dragon.intro:
Lava dragons are former red dragons that have been transformed after being surrounded by lava for too long. They reside in the Lava Dragon Isle in the Wilderness (between level 36 and 42 Wilderness), and attack with melee as well as with dragonfire. Due to their low Magic level they are particularly weak to Magic, which combined with their weakness to water spells makes water bolt a slow but profitable method of killing them.

Lava dragons can be safespotted both inside and outside their isle. The many piles of skeletons and edges at the isle allow for players to safespot them inside. Alternatively, players can camp some of the southern spawns outside the isle. Having 74 Agility is recommended when killing them to use the stepping stones to escape the isle, as the area is frequented by player killers.

Bringing a pestle and mortar is optional to grind the scales into shards, in addition to High Level Alchemy runes to alch their common adamant and rune equipment drops. If killing them from outside the isle, Telekinetic Grab will be needed to grab their drops. Although it is possible to stay at the isle indefinitely using this method, it is advisable to bank every 10–20 minutes as the isle is commonly targeted by player killers.

Lava dragons are the only monsters to drop the lava dragon bones, which give 85 Prayer experience when buried. However, burying them on Lava Dragon Isle grants 340 Prayer experience (400%) instead.

Pirate.title: Slayer task/Pirate
Pirate.intro:
Pirates can be assigned as a Slayer task from Krystilia.

Pirates can be found at level 55 Wilderness in the Pirates' Hideout. A lockpick is required to enter. They are combat level 26 and have a very minimal droptable. They are located in single-way combat.

Alternatively, Zombie pirate can be killed. They are combat levels 22, 28, and 34 located at the Chaos Temple. It is located in multi-way combat and a cannon can be used. Nearby Elder Chaos druids will consistently teleblock the player and Protect from Magic is highly recommended. There is a nearby altar to recharge prayer. Zombie pirates have a generous drop table making them a popular monster to kill. It is recommended to complete the medium Wilderness Diary which increases the drop table roll from 15% to 50%.

Zombie.title: Slayer task/Zombies
Zombie.intro:
Zombies can be assigned as a slayer task at level 10 combat by various Slayer masters. Zombies are most often found in places that depict death, such as graveyards.

Monkey Zombies, Undead chickens, Undead cows, Undead Druids, Undead ones, Vorkath, Zogres, and Zombie rats can all be killed to satisfy the task. The Zombies Champion does not count towards the task.

Zombies are primarily ignored as they have a very poor drop table, though players who are assigned them have the option of killing Undead Druids or Vorkath, provided they have the requirements to do so.

When assigned by Krystilia as part of a Wilderness task, zombies are more lucrative, with players having the option of killing zombie pirates, who have a generous drop table provided that the player has completed the Medium Wilderness Diary. If not killing the pirates, the only options are the Graveyard of Shadows and the eastern ruins, both of which are popular player killing hotspots due to being next to the lairs of Calvar'ion and Spindel respectively. The Graveyard of Shadows is more open and thus a cannon is more effective there.

Undead cows and chickens are good for players who wish to quickly complete the task. It is not recommended to kill Monkey Zombies, as they have no tradeable or useful non-quest drops. Vorkath is the highest level alternative to this task, and can only be accessed during and after Dragon Slayer II.

Jungle Horror.title: Jungle horror
Jungle Horror.intro: Jungle horrors are horrors that live on the island of Mos Le'Harmless. Players must have completed Cabin Fever to gain access to the island. They can be assigned as a Slayer task by Chaeldar and Vannaka. They are a weaker relative of the cave horrors that live inside the caves on the island. A witchwood icon is NOT required to kill jungle horrors.

Crabs.title: Slayer task/Crabs
Crabs.intro:
Crabs can be assigned as a Slayer task by various Slayer masters. They have no requirements to be assigned and are found in many areas across Gielinor. Crabs are often used as popular monsters for combat training, due to their low offence and high hitpoints. King Sand Crabs and Giant Rock Crabs are the exceptions, having much higher combat stats, and are only advisable to kill for a Slayer task if seeking specific drops from them (such as pieces of rock-shell armour).

As most crabs deal relatively little damage, no particular gear is required for them. Accounts with lower combat levels may need to wear armour or bring food, but at higher levels, neither are necessary. All crabs use the crush attack style, so if wearing armour, armour with the highest crush defence is advised. For example, a chainbody will offer more crush defence than a platebody.

All types of crabs initially appear as unattackable "rocks", but will emerge when a player stands in a neighboring tile. They will be aggressive, automatically attacking the player, but will become tolerant after 10 minutes have passed, and will no longer emerge. As they must be active to fight, the player must reset the crabs' aggression timer by leaving their immediate area and then returning.

The Gemstone Crab and hermit crabs do not count for a Slayer task.

Tzhaar.title: Slayer task/TzHaar
Tzhaar.intro:
TzHaar are an ancient race dwelling underneath the Karamja Volcano in Mor Ul Rek that can be assigned as a Slayer task if the player has unlocked the perk Hot Stuff for 100 slayer points.

TzHaar come in four varieties: the artisans TzHaar-Hur, the sages TzHaar-Mej, hunters TzHaar-Xil, and guards TzHaar-Kets. Killing any of these while wearing a ring of wealth increases their chances of dropping gems (and Onyx bolt tips for level 221 TzHaar-Kets).

The Hur and Ket primarily attack with melee, while the Xil can use either melee or ranged, depending on the weapon they are using; those wielding Toktz-xil-ul (resembling a throwing disc) will be able to use both styles, while those wielding Toktz-xil-ak or Toktz-xil-eks use only melee. TzHaar-Mej attack with magic.

Players killing TzHaar are recommended to kill the Ket or melee-using Xil, as they are easily safespotted through the many vents littering Mor Ul Rek. Attacking a Hur will cause all nearby TzHaar to attack the player, while attacking a Mej will cause nearby Xil and Ket to attack the player. When facing Ket, the player can also choose to kill the stronger level 221 variants in the inner area of the city, who can also drop pieces of obsidian armour. Accessing this inner area requires the player to show a fire cape to the Ket guards standing by the gates leading inside.

When offered an assignment of TzHaar, the Slayer master may instead allow the player to kill TzTok-Jad or TzKal-Zuk, with the latter requiring that the player has at least one TzKal-Zuk kill count. This can be further increased to two and three kills per task with the completion of the master and grandmaster combat achievement tiers respectively. While completing these tasks, the player will obtain slayer experience from every volcanic creature killed in their respective area and benefits from the slayer helmet's bonus for the entire run. If the player dies or leaves, the task is cancelled and no points are used.

A single kill of TzTok-Jad awards 37,010 slayer experience (25,250 from Jad and 11,760 from the pre-wave monsters, including the four healers), while a single kill of TzKal-Zuk yields ~125,000 experience (depending on how many cycles of monsters spawn while fighting Zuk, and the amount of both Jad and Zuk healers killed); 101,890 experience comes from Zuk, and the remaining from pre-wave monsters. Killing them on a slayer task not only speeds up kill times, but also increases the drop rate of their respective pets by 50% and 25%, making them much more rewarding for pet hunters.

Shadow Warrior.title: Shadow warrior
Shadow Warrior.intro:
Shadow warriors are monsters that can be found in the dungeon beneath the Legends' Guild. They are not considered undead, so the salve amulet has no effect on them, and they are one of few monsters that are hidden on the player's minimap.

After completion of Legends' Quest, shadow warriors are a possible Slayer task from Chaeldar and Vannaka.

Although they do not have the undead or spectral attributes, they are still undead according to the 36th Postbag from the Hedge, as Radimus Erkle says that the shadow warriors are resurrected with necromancy. They also wear spectral plate armour.

Mutated Zygomite.title: Slayer task/Zygomites
Mutated Zygomite.intro:
Zygomites can be assigned to level 60 combat and level 57 slayer by Chaeldar, Konar quo Maten, Nieve, and Duradel. Zygomites cannot be killed unless a fungicide spray has been used to deliver the final blow.

Zygomites can be safespotted by trapping them and moving out of their attack range. For instance, in Zanaris near the Cosmic Altar, players may trap them using a pillar and standing back near the mysterious ruins.

Players can alternatively kill Ancient Zygomites on Fossil Island or in the Stalker Den.

Fever Spider.title: Fever spider
Fever Spider.intro:
Fever spiders are Slayer monsters that require a Slayer level of 42 to kill, found only on Braindeath Island, in the brewery basement. This indirectly means players must also have started the Rum Deal quest in order to access them. Players must wear slayer gloves while fighting them, or face being damaged for 12.5% of their Hitpoints level and becoming diseased. Fever spiders are considered to be a relatively fast task due to the large quantity of spiders and their low Defence.

Players only need to wear slayer gloves if they are being hit by fever spiders, so players using Ranged or Magic may make use of safespots in order to wear better offensive gloves such as Barrows gloves. A notable safespot is located in the south-west corner, where players can trap the spiders on the edges of crates; however, due to the two tile wide nature of the spiders, many suitable safespots exist. Players safespotting the spiders without wearing slayer gloves are advised to bring a Relicym's balm in case the player accidentally becomes diseased.

Harpie Bug Swarm.title: Harpie Bug Swarm
Harpie Bug Swarm.intro:
Harpie bug swarms are mid-level slayer monsters that require a Slayer level of 33 to kill. A lit bug lantern, which requires a Firemaking level of 33 to light, is required to damage these monsters (the lantern must be lit and equipped). If you do not have 33 Firemaking, you cannot be assigned harpie bug swarms as a Slayer task.

Harpie bug swarms should be an easy task for well-equipped mid-level players; their abundance as well as the fact that they remain aggressive to players until level 93 combat makes this task very click-easy. As harpie bug swarms are very accurate, and will often hit for up to 6 Hitpoints, it is advisable to have Defence levels from 40-50+ and to bring food appropriate for the player's level, such as lobsters. Another option is to keep Protect from Melee up and recharge prayer at the relatively nearby altars.

It is recommended to bring nature runes while slaying this monster since it has many drops that can be alched to free up inventory spaces, and fire runes are frequently dropped from this monster.

Cockatrice.title: Cockatrice
Cockatrice.intro:
Cockatrice are Slayer monsters that require level 25 Slayer to kill. A mirror shield or V's shield is highly recommended. Without one, the cockatrice will attack with its piercing gaze, which has a range of 5 tiles, hits for 11 damage that can be negated by Protect from Melee, and rapidly drains combat stats. Otherwise, do not expect much of a fight from cockatrices. As 20 Defence is needed to wield a mirror shield, players who do not meet this requirement will not be assigned them as a task.

They are rarely killed outside of Slayer tasks, generally only by those hunting the rare mystic boots (light) and cockatrice head drops.

If necessary, players can utilise the large rock formation to the north of the cave to safespot cockatrice on the opposite side, even without a mirror shield, due to the limited range of piercing gaze. This is useful for pures who cannot wield a mirror shield, or for players who wish to use two-handed weapons like shortbows, but it is not generally recommended. Note that cockatrice have a unique mechanic where they will "retaliate" against any player who is within 10 tiles and is attempting to attack them without a mirror shield, even if the player has not actually attacked yet. This can be exploited to aggro distant cockatrice by merely red-clicking them.

A dwarf multicannon cannot be set up in the Fremmenik Slayer Caves. Those looking to use a cannon should kill moonlight cockatrice instead (requires 48 Slayer to begin the Perilous Moons quest. For access to Neypotzli, only partial completion of the Perilous Moons quest is required).

Infernal Mage.title: Slayer task/Infernal Mages
Infernal Mage.intro:
Infernal Mages can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 45 Slayer, level 40 combat, and completion of Priest in Peril by Vannaka or Mortimer.

Players who plan on fighting them should be wary of their accurate magic attack, although Protect from Magic negates this completely.

Shade.title: Slayer task/Shades
Shade.intro:
Shades can be assigned as a slayer task, with no Slayer level requirement by Mazchna and Vannaka. The easiest method to complete this task is by killing Loar Shades in Mort'ton as they are much faster to kill than the level 159/140 Shades found in Stronghold of Security and Catacombs of Kourend respectively.

Shades are susceptible to the Salve Amulet and Crumble Undead (however, their 40% weakness to wind spells means that Wind Bolt will do more damage than Crumble Undead for the same cost of a chaos rune, providing the player has 35 Magic or more). Combat experience gained while fighting the shades in the Stronghold of Security is drastically reduced; the player will gain 1 experience for 10 damage dealt.

Otherworldly Being.title: Otherworldly being
Otherworldly Being.intro:
Otherworldly beings are unusual Zanarian monsters. They are commonly assigned as Slayer tasks by Vannaka. They are found south of the bank in Zanaris and can be safespotted by standing next to the flower pond and attacking the ones on the other side, however they move around quite a lot and players may find them difficult to safespot. An alternate and more consistent safespotting method is standing on the north or south of the pond and corner trapping the mobs on the pond corners.

More specifically, five of the six otherworldly beings have a wander radius which permits safespotting without having them retreat as long as the player stands right next to the pond. One of these five will retreat if attacked horizontally across the pond, and another will retreat when attacked vertically. The other three will not retreat as long as you stay next to the pond.

Otherworldly beings may be a decent source of Magic experience, herbs, runes, and the materials for rings of forging for Ironmen.

As Otherworldly beings are considered spectral creatures, the Ectoplasmator will provide Prayer experience when killing them.

Pyrefiend.title: Slayer task/Pyrefiends
Pyrefiend.intro:
Pyrefiends can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 30 Slayer and level 25 combat.

Pyrefiends attack with magic-based melee, meaning armour that provides magic defence should be worn or Protect from Melee should be used with Prayer equipment, alternatively Prayer flick.

Spiritual Creature.title: Slayer task/Spiritual creatures
Spiritual Creature.intro:
Spiritual creatures are a potential Slayer assignment given by medium and high-levelled Slayer Masters after completion of Death Plateau, a combat level of 60 and either 60 Strength or Agility with a minimum Slayer level of 63 in order to be assigned them.

There are three types of spiritual creatures players can kill as part of a task: spiritual rangers, the weakest at 63 Slayer, warriors at 68 Slayer, and mages, the only NPCs that drop dragon boots, at 83 Slayer.

These creatures are only found in the God Wars Dungeon and the Wilderness God Wars Dungeon. As followers of their respective gods, they are aggressive to anyone that is not wearing an item aligned to their god, but will be tolerant otherwise. This is essentially required, as the dungeons are multicombat areas with many monsters, likely resulting in a swift death if this is not met.

In the God Wars Dungeon, players are encouraged to wear at least one Zamorak-affiliated item, as Zamorak's followers are found in all corners of the main section of the dungeon. Depending on the god that the player is focusing on, they should also bring one of that item to ensure tolerance. This is usually a Saradomin item, since Bandos and Armadyl-affiliated spiritual creatures are rarely killed.

In the Ancient Prison, only a Zaros-affiliated item is required, as none of the other gods' followers are found inside. It is still recommended to bring one Saradomin- and Zamorak-affiliated item, as the player will have to run past Saradomin and Zamorak followers to reach the Ancient Prison's entrance.

In the Wilderness God Wars Dungeon, it is recommended to bring three god-affiliated items: one of either Armadyl or Bandos (depending on the entrance entering from), one Saradomin, and one Zamorak. Zamorak's followers are essentially everywhere in the dungeon.

The stats of spiritual creatures are generally similar, with minor variations.

• Armadyl's spiritual creatures - An additional requirement of 70 Ranged, along with a crossbow that can fire a mithril grapple. The rangers are the strongest, the warriors are the second strongest, and the mages are the weakest. Unlike Aviansie, they can be attacked with all melee weapons.
• Bandos' spiritual creatures - An additional requirement of 70 Strength and a hammer. The warriors are the strongest, the mages are second strongest, and rangers are the weakest. Barring the mages, the rangers and warriors have the most health of monsters in this category.
• Saradomin's spiritual creatures - No additional requirements are needed, as these are found in the main dungeon. The mages are the strongest, the rangers the second strongest, and warriors the weakest.
• Zamorak's spiritual creatures - An additional requirement of 70 Hitpoints, and the player will lose all prayer points upon entering Zamorak's Fortress. The mages are the strongest and cast Flames of Zamorak, which drains Magic if not protected against, the rangers are second strongest, and warriors the weakest.
• Zaros' spiritual creatures - The player must complete the miniquest The Frozen Door, which has a requirement of 70 Strength, Hitpoints, Ranged, and Agility. The mages are the strongest, the warriors second strongest, and rangers the weakest. They are significantly stronger than the other gods' spiritual creatures.

In the Wilderness dungeon, only one requirement of either 60 Agility or Strength is required.

Many players tend to block spiritual creatures, since they are neither cannonable nor AFK'able, have low experience rates, and have poor drops compared to other similarly levelled monsters. Ironman players may wish to unblock the task once they have 83 slayer in order to get dragon boots.

When killing spiritual creatures, players are recommended to:

• Spiritual rangers - skip or block
• Spiritual warriors - if killing, Zamorak's Fortress
• Spiritual mages - if killing, Armadyl's Eyrie or Ancient Prison

variants.notes: The Zarosian variant can occasionally launch an arrow into the air, which if hit by, will deal heavy damage, disable overhead protection prayers and bind the player for a few seconds.

The Zarosian variant periodically unleashes smoke clouds in an X formation surrounding the player, descending onto their location when the attack was used in 5 ticks. Failing to move away deals up to 40 damage.

The Zamorakian variant's Flames of Zamorak will drain Magic levels if it successfully hits and damages the player.
The Zarosian variant uses the Ancient Magicks - smoke will poison the player, shadow drains the player's Attack level, blood heals the mage and ice freezes the player. These secondary effects will occur on successful hits, even if the damage would be blocked by prayer.

Mogre.title: Mogre
Mogre.intro:
Mogres are Slayer monsters and a type of ogre that are found in Mudskipper Point, requiring level 32 Slayer to kill. Mogres appear when disturbed by the player, who must lure them using Fishing explosives on an Ominous Fishing Spot. Previously, they could only be killed by players who had completed the Skippy and the Mogres miniquest. Since the release of Sailing, Mogres swimming in the ocean can now be killed with cannons from the player's boat. Doing so does not require completion of Skippy and the Mogres and does not demand the use of Fishing explosives, but still requires having level 32 Slayer.

Mogres can only be "lured" by clicking Use on the fishing explosives in your inventory, then clicking on the ominous fishing spots while also standing a few tiles away. Although the ominous fishing spots do have an options to "Lure" or "Bait", both these options do nothing (even with fishing explosives) and instead merely say in chat "Something seems to have scared all the fishes away..."

Mogres are usually killed by players searching for their unique drops of flippers or Mudskipper hats.

Killing a Mogre is a requirement for completing the medium task set in the Falador Diary.

Ghoul.title: Ghoul
Ghoul.intro:
Ghouls are found just west of Canifis, north of the swamp and west of the fairy ring code fairy ring CKS. Though they may appear to be undead and are often mistaken for such, they are in fact still alive and thus immune to both the Crumble Undead spell and to the effects of the salve amulet and salve amulet (e). A ghoul bone is needed to complete the Rag and Bone Man II. Killing a ghoul is a requirement for the easy Morytania Diary.

Ghouls can be somewhat troublesome to kill. When a ghoul has low hitpoints, it will stop attacking the player and retreat, allowing other ghouls to attack. Applying poison can be an effective method of killing the previous ghoul whilst attacking the next one.

It is possible for a ghoul to randomly attack a player lower than level 85 combat, ignoring any current engagement that player may be in. This is especially annoying as you won't be able to secure the kill to get the Slayer experience, because the game will say
Ghoul.strategy:
An efficient way to kill a ghoul can be through magic or ranged. Melee is possible, but they do flee when their health gets low. The effect of their retreat can be minimised by spending 10 minutes in the area (either while using magic or ranged, or simply waiting) for the Ghouls to become tolerant so that other Ghouls will not attack.

The ghouls to the west of Canifis are safespottable using the gravestones. A very useful safespot is between two gravestones and a cross on the eastern side, directly north from the Large grave. Any ghoul from the north-east gets stuck on the northern gravestone. Keeping you from being attacked while shooting ghouls over the gravestones. When retreating, they will walk back to the water and will still be within range.

If a player lures one of the two south-most ghouls to the south-west of the ghoul area, just to the left of the west-most plant, the player can run to the north side of the ghoul, effectively trapping it in that corner. The ghoul will be unable to retreat as the player will move with it as it tries to run away, and continue to block it from moving further. Occasionally, another ghoul will get close enough to interrupt the final blows of the fight, but the player can run south of the almost dead ghoul and keep it trapped between the player and the aggressive ghoul.
.]]

infobox.otherReq: Completion of Death to the Dorgeshuun

Molanisk.intro:
Molanisks are Slayer monsters that require level 39 Slayer to kill.

A Slayer bell is necessary to fight them. Players should remember to bring a light source when fighting them, as they are only found underground. Despite what their level would suggest, Molanisks do unusually low damage, meaning a relatively mid-level player with half-decent armour should easily be able to kill several of them.

Molanisks can only be safespotted on certain rocks, notably the large one down the path south of the fairy ring AJQ fairy ring.

variants.notes: Molanisks are found attached to cave walls and must be lured off with a Slayer bell to allow players to attack them.

Werewolf.title: Werewolf
Werewolf.intro:
Werewolves are found in Canifis. They appear as level 24 humans wandering the village until they are attacked, causing them to transform into level 88 werewolves unless the player attacks with Wolfbane, in which case they will remain in human form as long as it is equipped. They will always drop wolf bones, regardless of their form upon death. However, their human and werewolf forms have a separate loot table.

Werewolves do not count towards a regular wolf slayer task. Additionally, it is important to note that they will only count towards a werewolf Slayer task if killed after transforming: killing them in their human form with Wolfbane will not award experience or decrease the slayer task counter.

Werewolves can also be found in the God Wars Dungeon (and Wilderness version). These are slightly stronger than their Canifis variant, and aggressive to those not wearing an item of Zamorak. The werewolf bone for Rag and Bone Man II is not dropped in the God Wars Dungeon, only from the werewolves in Canifis.

Ogre.title: Slayer task/Ogres
Ogre.intro:
Ogres can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 40 combat by Vannaka. Ogres are most commonly found in Kandarin.

Along with ogres and ogress warriors and shamans, mogres, zogres, and skogres can be killed to satisfy the task. Jogres do not count towards the task.

While zogres and skogres both have a lower combat level than the rest, players should still take caution, as they are capable of inflicting disease.

Players with level 41 Magic can use ensouled ogre heads to cast Adept Reanimation and kill reanimated ogres.

Crocodile.title: Slayer task/Crocodiles
Crocodile.intro:
Crocodiles can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 50 combat by Vannaka. Although Vannaka suggests using a stab weapon for melee, their lowest defence is slash. However, they lack high defence in all three melee attack styles; making any melee weapon sufficient. If using melee, bringing a ranged weapon to range the crocodiles from across the river like darts can be useful, as they can swim in the water. Magic attacks work well, and with the weakness to Earth spells, the crocodiles take damage nearly every hit.

There are multiple locations to fight crocodiles across the desert. Player are recommended to carry waterskins with them to fight the desert heat. They can easily be refilled from nearby towns in fountains or sinks. Alternatively a knife can be brought to cut Kharidian cacti to refill them on the spot. Waterskins are prefered over equiping desert clothing, other heat resistant clothing, or the water circlet after completion of the Beneath Cursed Sands quest, as it will reduce the defensive or offensive stats of the player's gear.

A great place to fight crocodiles is on the south side of the River Elid, south of Pollnivneach. Because crocodiles are aggressive from a few squares away, this place attracts crocodiles from in the water where they cannot usually be reached, and is much less click-intensive. There is a safespot for crocodiles directly east of the lily island. There are two crocodile spawns that can be safespotted, which makes the task considerably easier. For food, players can take a small amount of coins to buy kebabs from Ali the Kebab seller for 3 coins each or jugs of wine from Ali the Barman for 1 coin each. Players may also sell noted food to the general store and buy it back in item form, usually only losing a few coins per item, or exchange noted food with the Banknote Exchange Merchant. If players have completed the Spirits of the Elid quest, they can use the Elidinis Statuette in Nardah to recharge their Prayer points, run energy, and Hitpoints. There is also a fountain to fill waterskins with.

Alternatively, they can be safespotted on the fence east of the Ruins of Unkah, removing the need to bring waterskins.

Another place to fight crocodiles is just north of Sophanem, by the river just outside the gate. After completion Icthlarin's Little Helper. There is an altar for prayer, and a sink just south of that inside of the city, allowing for prolonged trips.

The area south of the Ruins of Ullek, south-west of the teak trees has 12 crocodile spawns and does not require water for the player to survive, so long as the player stays in the grassy area near the water. This can be useful for players who do not wish to bring many waterskins with them.

There are three varieties of crocodile: one can only walk on water, one can only walk on land, and one can walk on both land and water. The ones confined to the water are most easily safespotted, simply by standing one tile back from the shore. If a crocodile dies while its south-west tile is over water, it will not drop bones, though it can still drop herbs which must be telegrabbed if the herb is not on or adjacent to a traversable tile.

Terror Dog.title: Terror dog
Terror Dog.intro:
Terror dogs are Slayer monsters that require a Slayer level of 40 (not boostable) to kill. Being the personal pets of Tarn Razorlor, they are first encountered during the miniquest Lair of Tarn Razorlor, in which the player must fight two terror dogs, alongside some animated armour in addition to Tarn himself. Upon completion of the miniquest, more terror dogs can be found in the room.

Terror dogs use an accurate melee attack. As the room they are fought in is a multi-combat area, fighting them can become very dangerous quickly, as multiple terror dogs can attack the player all at once.

Terror dogs do not count toward fulfilling a Slayer task for dogs; they are a separate task. They are the only monsters that drop the Granite helmet.

Killing a Terror Dog is one of the tasks for the Medium Morytania Diary.

Sea Snake.title: Slayer task/Sea snakes
Sea Snake.intro:
Sea snakes can be assigned as a slayer task by Vannaka at level 40 Slayer and level 50 combat after the completion of Royal Trouble. They are found in the Miscellania and Etceteria Dungeon, which can be entered during and after the quest. They attack with melee and are poisonous so antipoisons of any variety are strongly recommended. Both variants share the same drop table, although the hatchling drop regular bones whereas the young drop big bones (and by extension long and curved bones).

Dwarven multicannons can be used in the dungeon, although it is in single combat.

Crawling Hand.title: Slayer task/Crawling Hands
Crawling Hand.intro:
Crawling Hands can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 5 Slayer by various Slayer masters.

Due to their undead status, the Crumble Undead spell and the salve amulet do work on them.

Banshee.title: Slayer task/Banshees
Banshee.intro:
Banshees can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 15 Slayer and level 20 combat by various Slayer masters. They are found in the Slayer Tower and the Catacombs of Kourend. Players must wear earmuffs or a Slayer helm when fighting banshees. Lower levelled players who do not have access to a Slayer helm can wear a salve amulet. Note that the bonuses from the salve amulet do not stack with those from the Slayer helmet.

Banshees are primarily known for their common drops of pure essence, which is helpful for ironmen for runecrafting.

A stronger variant of banshee, the Twisted Banshee, can be found in the Catacombs of Kourend. These are often killed over normal banshees as they are still easy to kill (notably being safespottable) and have much better drops; battlestaves, rune equipment, and larger quantities of herbs.

Catablepon.title: Catablepon
Catablepon.intro:
Catablepon are magical creatures that appear to be green bulls with reptilian tails. They are found on the third level of the Stronghold of Security. They drop the top of sceptre, one of four parts of the Skull sceptre.

They have a weakening glare which drains your Strength, but will stop casting once 8% + 3 of your total strength level has been drained.

Cave Bug.title: Cave bug
Cave Bug.intro:
Cave bugs are monsters that require level 7 Slayer to kill. They are found in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves, requiring a light source and a rope to enter, and stronger variants can be located in the Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon. They are a good source of low level herbs, which can aid beginning players in training Herblore. Their Hitpoints regenerates once every 5 game ticks, 20 times faster than regular NPCs.

Cave bugs that are significantly more powerful—with a combat level of 96—can be found and safespotted in the Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon, located south of the city of Dorgesh-Kaan, but can only be accessed after the completion of the Death to the Dorgeshuun quest through fairy ring fairy ring AJQ. After entering the dungeon and climbing down the ladder to the dungeon floor, level 96 cave bugs can be safespotted by standing in a passage between frogs and cave bugs (south-west of the ladder).

A light source is required for these dungeons, along with a rope to place down on the hole leading to the Lumbridge Swamp Caves, if it has not been done so previously.

Players should be on the lookout for wall beasts within the Lumbridge Swamp Caves, which are monsters that will grab and attack you, if you are in their line of sight. To avoid being hit, either stand one square directly beside a hole in the wall and run across to the other side, or have a spiny helmet equipped.

Cave Crawler.title: Slayer task/Cave crawlers
Cave Crawler.intro:
Cave crawlers can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 10 Slayer and level 10 combat by various Slayer masters. A form of poison protection is recommended when killing them, as they inflict a strong poison.

Players with very low Defence should use Ranged or Magic to attack these monsters in order to avoid being damaged and possibly poisoned, utilising the rocks around the room's walls in Fremennik Slayer Dungeon as safespots. You can use the fairy ring just outside, fairy ring AJR, as a fast means of banking.

When fighting cave crawlers in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves, be aware that any exposed light sources (i.e candles) may explode, and can cause a considerable amount of damage. As such, a bullseye lantern or an oil lantern is recommended as it is not an exposed light source. You can use the Zanaris Shed to be teleported to Zanaris as a fast method for banking (either within Zanaris or to teleport elsewhere using the fairy ring itself).

Lower level players should be aware that they have a rapid natural health regenerate rate, regenerating 1 hitpoint every 5 ticks.

Cave Slime.title: Slayer task/Cave slimes
Cave Slime.intro:
Cave slimes can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 17 Slayer and level 15 combat by various lower leveled Slayer masters.

Cave slimes are found in two rooms of the Lumbridge Swamp Caves. A rope is needed if you have not entered the dungeon before. A light source is also required, but be aware that any exposed light sources (such as a candle) may explode, dealing up to 25% of the current Hitpoints level in damage if you go into the northern spawning room. A good option for an enclosed light source is a bulleyes lantern. However, the entire southern room is risk free. For either room you will have to pass by a wall beast, so head protection (spiny helmet/Slayer helmet) can be helpful to avoid damage.

They may also be found in the Dorgesh-Kaan South Dungeon after completion of the Death to the Dorgeshuun quest. A light source is also required but there is no risk of them exploding or wall beasts to go through.

Rockslug.title: Rockslug
Rockslug.intro:
Rockslugs are Slayer monsters that require level 20 Slayer to kill. A bag of salt must be used on it when it has 4 or less Hitpoints to finish it off. If used on a rockslug with 5 or more Hitpoints, the bag will be consumed but have no effect. If a rockslug's health is reduced to 1 but a bag of salt is not used on it, the rockslug will stop retaliating and wander off.

Players can buy the "Slug salter" perk from a Slayer Master for 10 Slayer points, which will automatically salt the rockslug when it falls below 4 Hitpoints, provided that the player has a bag of salt in their inventory. Alternatively, a brine sabre can be used to kill them without the need for bags of salt.

They are rarely killed due to their mediocre drops, which consists of low level ores and seeds. They may rarely drop the mystic gloves (light).

Bat.title: Slayer task/Bats
Bat.intro:
Bats can be assigned as a Slayer task from Turael, Spria, and Mazchna. They have a requirement of level 5 combat to be assigned and are generally meant as tasks for beginners. There are a variety of bats, but the most commonly killed are regular bats and giant bats. Bats only drop bat bones or nothing at all, meaning there is little reason to slay higher-level bats.

Although they are called bats, dire bats in Vampyrium do not count towards this Slayer task.

Flesh Crawler.title: Flesh Crawler
Flesh Crawler.intro:
Flesh Crawlers are medium level monsters found in the second level of the Stronghold of Security. They drop the bottom of sceptre, one of four parts of the skull sceptre. Flesh crawlers drop herbs often, and are frequently killed for their uncommon grimy ranarr drops.

They are scavengers, and will eat anything if given the chance.

Ghost.title: Slayer task/Ghosts
Ghost.intro:
Ghosts can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 13 combat by Turael, Spria, and Mazchna. Ghosts spawn in various locations throughout Gielinor.

Only regular ghosts, forgotten souls, tortured souls, death wings and Revenants can be killed to satisfy the task. Spectres, ghasts, banshees and shades will not count towards the task.

Most areas that contain ghosts contain those of combat levels 19, 24, and 29. Ghosts with a combat level of 76 and 77 can only be found in the Sepulchre of Death, the bottom floor of the Stronghold of Security.

Wall Beast.title: Slayer task/Wall beast
Wall Beast.intro:
Wall beasts can be assigned as a Slayer task by Mazchna at 35 Slayer and 5 Defence in order to equip a Spiny helmet. They are only found in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves. As the Spiny helmet (or Slayer helmet) is only required to block their initial attack, players without the Slayer helmet may wish to bring their black mask to swap to afterwards.

A wall beast can be found a few tile west of the rope after climbing down the rope in the Lumbridge Swamp. After killing the Wall Beast, climbing out of the cave then back in seems to reset its spawn timer.

Wolf.title: Wolf
Wolf.intro:
Wolves are canine monsters that can be found in various places around Gielinor. They have a variety of different combat levels, with level 64 wolves being the most common, and level 11 and 14 wolves only being found in the Stronghold of Security.

Their bones can be used with a chisel to create wolfbone arrowtips used to make ogre arrows, which are necessary for completing Big Chompy Bird Hunting and Freeing Skrach Uglogwee during Recipe for Disaster.

Killerwatt.title: Killerwatt
Killerwatt.intro:
Killerwatts are Slayer monsters located in the Killerwatt plane, accessible through a portal at the top floor of Draynor Manor after completion of Ernest the Chicken. A Slayer level of 37 is required to kill them.

If a player is not wearing a pair of insulated boots while fighting them, both their Ranged and Melee attacks will have a much higher maximum hit. Even when wearing insulated boots, their attacks are still rapid and highly accurate, and they have an attack range of 13 tiles, meaning it is not possible to safespot them with long ranged weapons. A dwarf multicannon cannot be set up in the Killerwatt plane.

Killerwatts are a commonly skipped Slayer task due to their relatively high damage output combined with their mediocre drops, except for those seeking their unique air diamond drop.

Brutus can be killed on a cow task, making it a great alternative for low level players wanting a more challenging fight and getting used to combat mechanics.

Icefiends can be assigned by Turael/Aya and Spria. They are the weakest type of fiend, and commonly drop nothing but Fiendish ashes. They are generally only killed on slayer tasks, except by players trying to obtain moon key halves in the Ruins of Tapoyauik. Although not very commonly, they also drop easy clue scrolls.

Due to the low amounts of icefiends assigned per task, most players choose to complete this task nearby teleports such as Lassar Teleport, rather than travelling to the Ruins of Tapoyauik for the additional drops.

Minotaurs.intro:
Minotaur are found on level one of the Stronghold of Security. They drop the right skull half, one of four parts of the skull sceptre. These monsters are great for training due to their low Defence, but have high attack damage making them dangerous for un-equipped players.

Minotaurs are a common method of Ranged training as they can be safespotted and commonly drop iron arrows.

Ghosts.title: Slayer task/Ghosts
Ghosts.intro:
Ghosts can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 13 combat by Turael, Spria, and Mazchna. Ghosts spawn in various locations throughout Gielinor.

Only regular ghosts, forgotten souls, tortured souls, death wings and Revenants can be killed to satisfy the task. Spectres, ghasts, banshees and shades will not count towards the task.

Most areas that contain ghosts contain those of combat levels 19, 24, and 29. Ghosts with a combat level of 76 and 77 can only be found in the Sepulchre of Death, the bottom floor of the Stronghold of Security.

Bears.title: Slayer task/Bears
Bears.intro:
Bears can be assigned as a slayer task at level 13 combat by various low-level Slayer masters. Bears can be found in various locations throughout Gielinor.

Black bears, bear cubs, grizzly bears, grizzly bear cubs, reanimated bears, Artio, and Callisto can all be killed to satisfy the task. Angry bears (found in Tolna's rift), the Headless Beast (fought during the quest Getting Ahead), and the Crystalline and Corrupted Bear (fought in the Gauntlet and the Corrupted Gauntlet respectively) do not count towards the task.

Those with lower combat levels would find it in their best interest to kill bear cubs, found in the Fremennik Province and throughout Kourend. Black bears would also be a good option, with a combat level of 19. Grizzly bears in most cases are an option if they are close, as most are level 21 combat. The only level 42 combat grizzly bears are found in Tirannwn. Grizzly bear cubs, too, can only be found in Tirannwn, with combat levels ranging from 33 to 36.

Players with 21 Magic, ensouled bear heads, may find casting Basic Reanimation and killing reanimated bears easier compared to regular bears, due to their lower hitpoints.

Players who seek a greater challenge or assigned bears by Krystilia can opt to kill Callisto or Artio for their slayer task, as they count towards it and provide a generous amount of drops. They are especially popular for Wilderness slayer due to their higher value. Remember that both bear bosses reside in the Wilderness, and it is not recommended for players to bring items they are unwilling to lose. Accessing Artio requires completion of the Hard Wilderness Diary, while Callisto only requires the Medium Wilderness Diary but is located in significantly deeper Wilderness that is a Multicombat area. A one-time fee of is required to access the boss, which must be paid again if the player dies to another player in the Wilderness.

Zombies.title: Slayer task/Zombies
Zombies.intro:
Zombies can be assigned as a slayer task at level 10 combat by various Slayer masters. Zombies are most often found in places that depict death, such as graveyards.

Monkey Zombies, Undead chickens, Undead cows, Undead Druids, Undead ones, Vorkath, Zogres, and Zombie rats can all be killed to satisfy the task. The Zombies Champion does not count towards the task.

Zombies are primarily ignored as they have a very poor drop table, though players who are assigned them have the option of killing Undead Druids or Vorkath, provided they have the requirements to do so.

When assigned by Krystilia as part of a Wilderness task, zombies are more lucrative, with players having the option of killing zombie pirates, who have a generous drop table provided that the player has completed the Medium Wilderness Diary. If not killing the pirates, the only options are the Graveyard of Shadows and the eastern ruins, both of which are popular player killing hotspots due to being next to the lairs of Calvar'ion and Spindel respectively. The Graveyard of Shadows is more open and thus a cannon is more effective there.

Undead cows and chickens are good for players who wish to quickly complete the task. It is not recommended to kill Monkey Zombies, as they have no tradeable or useful non-quest drops. Vorkath is the highest level alternative to this task, and can only be accessed during and after Dragon Slayer II.

Skeletons.title: Slayer task/Skeletons
Skeletons.intro:
Skeletons are undead monsters that can be assigned as tasks at combat level 15 by various low-level Slayer masters. They are often found in cemeteries and dungeons. A good strategy to kill them is to use melee with a weapon with crush bonuses (such as a Viggora's chainmace) and a salve amulet or salve amulet (e), due to their low crush defence.

Another strategy to kill them would be with magic. Many skeletons have an elemental weakness to earth spells, making those a very effective option.

Players who seek a greater challenge can choose to kill Vet'ion or Calvar'ion. These bosses are significantly stronger than the typical skeleton, but provide plenty of rewards for players who seek to kill them. In order to access Calvar'ion, the player must have completed the Hard Wilderness Diary. Vet'ion only requires completing the Medium Wilderness Diary, but is deeper in the Wilderness and resides in a multicombat area. Accessing the bosses requires a one-time payment of coins, which must be repaid again if the player dies to another player in the Wilderness. Note that the skeletal hellhounds they summon also count towards the task, so every kill at the boss is equal to five skeletons per spawn.

If players are not seeking to kill either skeleton boss but are assigned them in the Wilderness, an ideal location would be the Edgeville Dungeon, as there is a good cluster of skeletons that can be easily cannoned and has a quick escape, provided that the player is paying attention.

Using Ancient Magicks to kill skeleton monkeys is considered one of the best magic training methods. Due to the high cost of runes it is recommended to bring good equipment to minimise the amount of splashing. Note that in some cases prayer bonus should be prioritised over magic bonus.

Rats.title: Slayer task/Rats
Rats.intro:
Rats can be assigned as a slayer task from Turael and Spria. They have no requirements to be assigned. There are a wide variety of rats that can count toward the task, but the most commonly killed are rats and giant rats, which are low-level, rarely deal damage, and practically ubiquitous. It is recommended to use Rat bone weapons as it has greatly increased effectiveness against rats.

Scurrius can be fought for greater experience and profit, although his minions will also decrement the task, reducing how many times the boss can be fought on task. Brine rats are accessible during Olaf's Quest, and drop medium clues and the elusive brine sabre.

Hell-rat behemoths can be accessed after Freeing Evil Dave, and drop full spice shakers for spicy stews. Crypt rat and giant crypt rat variations require completion of Priest in Peril for access to Morytania and may be slain by players for the higher Slayer experience reward or for changing their reward potential inside the Barrows minigame.

Wolves.title: Slayer task/Wolves
Wolves.intro:
Wolves can be assigned as a slayer task at 20 combat level by Turael and Mazchna. They can be found in a variety of locations around Gielinor. The task is very straightforward as regular Wolves only attack with their fairly accurate melee bites; it is recommended to either safespot them or keep Protect from Melee on at all times.

One fast way to complete a wolves Slayer task is with a Dwarf multicannon in the Stronghold of Security, as it has a large amount of wolves.

Kalphites.title: Slayer task/Kalphites
Kalphites.intro:
Kalphites can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 15 combat by all Slayer masters, with the exception of Mortimer and the Wilderness Slayer master Krystilia. Kalphites come in a wide variety of levels, which is why they are possible tasks from nearly all Slayer masters. They can be found in the Kalphite Lair in the north-west Kharidian Desert, as well as in a Slayer task-exclusive area, the Kalphite Cave, just east of Shantay Pass.

Kalphites comes in four varieties: workers, soldiers, and guardians, as well as the boss monster the Kalphite Queen. With the exception of the Queen, all Kalphites use melee attacks. Additionally the soldiers and guardians can induce poison starting at 4 and 6 Hitpoints damage respectively. This poison bypasses protection prayers. Protect from Melee and some type of poison immunity will completely negate damage from the workers, soldiers and guardians.

Birds.title: Slayer task/Birds
Birds.intro:
Birds can be assigned as a Slayer task from Turael or Spria. They have no requirements to be assigned and are generally meant as tasks for beginners. There are a wide variety of birds, but the most commonly killed are chickens, seagulls and ducks, which are low-level, rarely deal damage and easy to access. Chickens drop bones, raw chicken and feathers, but most other birds only drop bones or nothing at all, meaning there is little reason to slay higher-level birds.

Birds introduced with the Sailing skill do not reward Slayer experience and thus do not count towards task completion.

Sourhogs.title: Sourhog
Sourhogs.intro:
A sourhog is a boar-like monster introduced in A Porcine of Interest. It requires reinforced goggles to kill, or a Slayer helmet after the quest. If no protection is worn, the caustic saliva they spit will burn the player's eyes, draining the player's current Attack and Defence by 90% and cause 20-30 damage each hit accompanied by the player exclaiming . Sourhogs are aggressive to players regardless of their combat level.

According to Spria, the sourhog was created when two farmers competed in a competition each year, with the same farmer winning each year. The other farmer, who was jealous of his rival, hired a dark wizard to alter one of his pigs, turning it into the Sourhog. This sourhog escaped and successfully bred more of its own kind. Sourhogs prefer to live in underground caves and in primitive tribes.

Spiders.title: Slayer task/Spiders
Spiders.intro:
Spiders can be assigned as a Slayer task by Turael, Spria, and Krystilia. They can be found in numerous places across Gielinor.

Most spiders generally use melee, but a few stronger ones will also use Ranged and/or Magic alongside them. Low-levelled spiders are generally weak to all forms of combat, though higher-levelled spiders are weaker to crush.

There are many varieties of spiders that players can kill as part of a Slayer task, though for low-levels, the spiders around Lumbridge are a reasonable spot.

Due to the low number of spiders assigned by the Slayer masters, it is generally recommended to not kill the minions when fighting Sarachnis if choosing to fight her for the task, as she spawns four minions per fight when faced solo, which can quickly end the task.

Araxytes can be killed in place of a spider task, though this option requires 92 Slayer in order to fight them. A boost from wild pie can be used at 87 Slayer, but it is recommended to wait at least until 90 Slayer before using boosts for a reasonable amount of uptime. Killing the minions in this encounter does not decrement the task, but will still grant Slayer experience.

Players who seek a greater challenge or assigned spiders by Krystilia can opt to kill Venenatis or Spindel for their Slayer task, as they count towards it and provide a generous amount of drops. They are especially popular for Wilderness Slayer due to their higher value. Remember that both reside in the Wilderness, and it is not recommended for players to bring items they are unwilling to lose. Accessing Spindel requires completion of the Hard Wilderness Diary, while Venenatis only requires the Medium Wilderness Diary but is located in significantly deeper Wilderness that is a multicombat area. A one-time fee of coins is required to access the boss, which must be paid again if the player dies to another player within any of the wilderness bosses respective lairs. Taking out the Spiderlings in either fight will not decrement the player's Slayer task.

If the player is assigned spiders by Krystilia but does not want to kill the spider bosses, it is recommended they head to the "spider hill" (located around level 46 Wilderness, with a cut sapphire being the location's landmark) and place a cannon there with very little risk. All of the spiders here are aggressive with low hitpoints, making the task breeze by in a matter of minutes. Alternatively, the player can bring a very fast ranged attack weapon (such as darts or knives) to very quickly kill the Level 1 spiderlings, which have 2 HP each, so that even a task of 100 spiders can be completed in about 5 minutes without using a cannon.

Abyssal Sire.intro:
The Abyssal Sire is an abyssal demon Slayer boss that requires level 85 Slayer to kill. To access the boss, the player must have visited the Abyss at least once, either through the Mage of Zamorak or the Fairy Ring network. As with all other Slayer bosses, the Sire can only be fought when assigned abyssal demons (outside of Krystilia) or itself as a Slayer task. Although it resides in a multi-combat area, it is a solo-only boss.

According to The Overseer, the Abyssal Sires are the engineers of the Abyss from a time before the God Wars. As their resources began to deplete and they had no means to escape, they constructed the Nexus and remained there in deep stasis.

It is known for dropping the unsired, which can be placed in the Font of Consumption behind The Overseer for a chance of obtaining an abyssal whip, abyssal dagger, abyssal head, jar of miasma, a part of the abyssal bludgeon - the axon, claw, or spine - or, rarely, an abyssal orphan.

The Sire was introduced in a Slayer expansion developer blog on 2 June 2015 and subsequently polled with 89.8% of the votes in favour of its addition.
Abyssal Sire.strategy:
The Abyssal Sire is a level 350 Slayer boss that can only be killed when assigned Abyssal demons or the Sire itself with the required Slayer level of 85.

It is mainly killed for its unsired drops, which can be used at the Font of Consumption to obtain valuable rewards such as the abyssal dagger, parts of the abyssal bludgeon, or the abyssal orphan pet.

Note that while the Sire is a boss residing in a multicombat area, it can only be fought by one player at any given time. If the attacker does not fight the Sire in ~20 seconds from their last attack, another player may attack it.

Phase 1:
The Sire wakes up and begins the fight when attacked. If not stunned, it will summon miasma pools under the player and create spawns. The six tentacles will also awaken. These tentacles are static, but attack with typeless crush that can deal up to 30 damage, slightly reduced with Protect from Melee.

If the Sire is attacked by a player but that player stops attacking it for some reason, the Sire can be attacked by another player after ~20 or so seconds pass.

The player needs to kill all four respiratory systems to progress. However, with the Sire awake, the tentacles will protect the respiratory systems from attacks, and any attacks dealt to them while the boss is awake will be reduced to 0-3 damage regardless of the experience drop given.

In order to remove the protection provided by the tentacles, the Sire must be disoriented. This can be done in one of two ways; dealing 75 damage with ranged or magic (as the boss is not accessible with melee), or using a shadow spell against it. Shadow spells, if they successfully disorient the Sire, will do so for 30 seconds. The chance of this occurring is dependent on the tier of shadow spell; Shadow Rush has a 25% chance, Shadow Burst 50%, Shadow Blitz 75% and Shadow Barrage guarantees it. While casting a shadow spell on an inactive Sire will both wake it up and potentially stun it, the stun from this spell will not be applied for 10 game ticks after being cast. A shadow spell cast on an awoken Sire will be applied instantly.

When stunned, the respiratory systems should be killed with ranged or magic, depending on what the player prefers. Upon a successful hit, demonbane weapons and spells (other than holy water) will destroy them instantly regardless of the player's bonuses. It is highly recommended players bring a scorching bow and bronze arrows, since these are cheap and readily available, and the bow has high accuracy even when not bringing ranged armour switches.

If a non-demonbane weapon is used, the player will deal anywhere from 50%-100% of their maximum hit as damage. Bringing a weapon that has a max hit of 50 or higher will be sufficient enough to destroy the respiratory systems in two hits.

Within 30 seconds, the player will be easily able to destroy all of the respiratory systems in one cycle with demonbane. Without demonbane, it is possible to do so if they can be two hit; three hits will likely require a second stun. Despite the 30 second stun timer, it is actually 27 seconds, as the tentacles will awaken at this mark and immediately protect the systems.

Overall, the optimal strategy for this phase is as follows:
• Switch to your ranged or mage gear and attack the Sire with any ranged or magic weapon/spell that is not a shadow spell to wake it up.
• Cast Shadow Barrage on the Sire to stun it.
• Begin killing respiratory systems. Focus on killing the systems on either the east or west side, re-stun the Sire with Shadow Barrage if needed, then finish off the remaining systems.

Any damage dealt to the Sire during this phase will only count for the purposes of disorientation; if the Sire has taken any damage, it will be restored back to full health until the end of the phase.

After the last respiratory system is killed, head back to the centre and attack the Sire as soon as it steps out into the main arena (or in transit if range/mage). While damage is reduced by 50%, the amount of time the Sire takes to begin the next phase is usually significant enough to deal some damage. If the Sire somehow reaches 0 health before the next phase starts, it will begin the next phase with 40% of its health.

Phase 2:
Stay on Row 1 during this phase, as attacking it from outside melee distance will cause the Sire to teleport you to itself and discharge a damaging blast of energy.

At this point, if the Sire is not in combat for ~1 minute, it will despawn, resetting the fight.

The Sire will use melee attacks that can hit up to 26 through prayer. Watch for miasma pools underneath the player; when they appear run to the other marked tile on Row 1. Ignore spawns unless killing the Sire at low levels with low DPS (in which case long kill times may make removing minions desirable). If reducing the Sire's defence, use one special attack now, otherwise save all special attack energy for phase 3.

Once the Sire is damaged below 50% of its health (212 health or less) it will start walking south. Run to Row 2 and activate Protect from Missiles. Advanced techniques can be used to pull the Sire south while attacking it, reducing the amount of time spent waiting for the Sire.

If the Sire reaches 0 health before the next phase starts, it will begin the next phase with 20% of its health.

Araxxor.intro:
Araxxor is the boss version of araxytes found in an instanced lair inside the Morytania Spider Cave, requiring level 92 Slayer and access to Morytania to kill. As a Slayer boss, he may only be killed while on a spider or araxyte Slayer task. Konar quo Maten can also assign Araxxor specifically when she assigns a boss task.

Araxxor is currently the strongest Slayer boss in-game by combat level. He uniquely drops pieces of the noxious halberd, a strong two-handed slash weapon, and the araxyte fang, which can be combined with the amulet of torture to create the amulet of rancour, the best-in-slot melee amulet.
Araxxor.strategy:
Araxxor is a level 92 Slayer boss found in the Morytania Spider Cave. In order to fight him, completion of Priest in Peril to access Morytania is required, as well as having been assigned an Araxyte or spider Slayer task.

If the player dies while fighting Araxxor, their grave will be placed outside the entrance to his lair, which follows normal death rules.

Fight overview:
As with all araxytes, Araxxor's attacks can inflict venom, and as with most spiders, is weak to crush. He has a Defence level of 135, with his lowest defence bonus being crush at +15. His Defence level can be only drained by up to 45 levels, therefore one elder maul special attack will suffice. Alternatively, a dragon warhammer special attack is nearly as effective, draining 40 Defence levels. Though Araxxor has an elemental weakness to fire spells, his high magical defences makes this trait mostly thematic, and the generally lower defences of magic robes will have the player take more damage overall.

Araxxor spawns in the middle of his chamber and attacks with melee; if out of his melee range, he will close the distance and attack with either magic or ranged - whichever of the player's defensive rolls is lower. Araxxor is capable of attacking diagonally, in which case he will use melee. The melee attack can deal up to 38 damage, and using Protect from Melee will significantly reduce the damage up to a max of 5. The ranged attacks can deal up to 34 damage, with Protect from Missiles reduces the damage by ~45%, with a max hit of 18. A successful ranged attack will additionally drain 9% of the player's Defence level. The magic attacks deal up to 21 damage, with Protect from Magic reducing the damage by ~50%. A successful magic attack additionally drains 9% of the player's Prayer. These attacks are calculated upon start and late reactions will not mitigate damage.

As the attack style used is dependent on the player's defence rolls, prayers such as Rigour might change which style the boss uses. Aranea boots can be used to block Araxxor's ranged attack once every 8 ticks (4.8 seconds), but not his magic attacks. Players with high magic defence armour can take advantage of this negation effect by moving out of the melee range every second attack; forcing a ranged attack. The high magic defences are easiest to achieve whilst ranging and using high end ranged gear such as fortified masori.

Around Araxxor's lair, there are nine eggs; three each of red, white, and green. The first egg hatches after three standard attacks from Araxxor, hatching clockwise starting from the south-easternmost egg, with subsequent eggs hatching after every six standard attacks.

The eggs will always follow one of three potential patterns, with the last two sets copying that of the first:
• Green > White > Red
• White > Red > Green
• Red > Green > White

Players can opt to destroy the eggs, which have 65 Hitpoints. If an egg has been fully destroyed, Araxxor will simply spawn an araxyte from the next egg in the rotation, skipping over the destroyed egg. Any damage dealt to an egg without destroying it will carry over to the hatched araxyte, however if an egg has taken more damage than the araxyte that would have hatched from it (58 Hitpoints), then the egg will simply despawn, and Araxxor will use another six standard attacks before the next egg in sequence hatches.

Players will always max hit when attacking the hatched araxytes with a noxious halberd, crush weapons, or heavy Ranged weapon (such as a crossbow or ballista) if crush or ranged is their highest accuracy style respectively. Attacking the hatched eggs with anything else - or attacking the unhatched eggs - does not guarantee a max hit, and rolls damage normally. Both the eggs and the araxytes count as on-task monsters for the purposes of benefiting from the slayer helmet's damage bonus, but will not reduce the player's task kill count.

Every six standard attacks, Araxxor will use the same one of three possible special attacks for the remainder of the fight, which can be quickly determined by identifying the south-easternmost egg. All of these attacks leave acid pools, which inflict venom and deal increasingly larger damage (starting from 4) the longer the player stays on them.

It is always best to lure the red araxytes so they explode underneath Araxxor for the extra damage; while optional, it is generally recommended to lure them to white eggs if the player does not wish to directly attack them to avoid wasting time preparing to kill the white araxytes.

If attacking the white araxytes directly, they can be one-hit with a crush weapon while under the effects of vengeance, and also with the same methods as all araxytes, listed below. Alternatively, a noxious halberd will one-hit them which saves a lot more time on average than having to weaken the eggs.

Enrage phase:
When Araxxor falls below 255 health, he will enter an enrage phase. This is signified with a distinct screeching sound, along with Araxxor coating his two front legs with venom. This will additionally increase his Defence level by 35, Magic by 28 and Ranged by 31; drained stats will carry over to enrage. Alongside the increased stats, Araxxor's attack speed is increased from 6 (3.6 seconds) to 4 (2.4 seconds).

Barrows Brothers.intro:
The Barrows is a series of six burial mounds east of Mort'ton in which the Barrows brothers were entombed after their deaths during the Third Age. 'Barrows' also commonly refers to the minigame-like dungeon-delving experience of looting the chest at the centre of the tunnels beneath the crypts, released on 9 May 2005.

Players can attempt to rob valuable items from the Barrows brothers' crypts. However, due to an ancient spell, the brothers' wights continued to dwell in the barrows, protecting these treasures.

Looting the Barrows is popular due to the potential of receiving valuable rewards, including the unique Barrows equipment, with increasingly valuable rewards for killing more monsters in the crypts, including the Barrows brothers themselves.

In the miniquest His Faithful Servants players are tasked to slay all six Barrows brothers and then loot the chest for the strange icon. Completing the miniquest rewards 20,000 Prayer experience and the ability to use the minimap within the Barrows tunnels.
Barrows Brothers.strategy:
This page shows various strategies which may help you in the Barrows.

Equipment:

Magic (Low level)=
Due to the elemental weakness of the Barrows brothers, and their low magic level, very little gear is needed to kill them. Some players prefer to wear tankier armour to defend against the crypt monsters, but even low level magic armour is generally more effective.

Inventory:

• If your Ranged level is high enough, bring Dragonhide armour and a ranged weapon for Ahrim.
• Use a melee weapon to kill monsters in the tunnels for reward potential.
• A Dragon dagger for quickly killing Karil.
• Food for healing from Verac or the crypt monsters.
• Prayer potions
• Combat and Ranging potions
• Restore potion for Ahrim's Strength drain
• Runes for Air spells or Iban Blast.
• Use the dueling ring to teleport to Ferox Enclave after each run, to bank and use the Pool of Refreshment to restore your stats. Otherwise bring a ring to boost your melee attacks for getting reward potential.

|-|
Magic (High level)=
Magic can be used effectively against each Barrows brother. However, Ahrim is weakest to ranged and will be harder to hit without Air spells or a Tumeken's shadow.

Inventory:

• With a 1-handed staff, a Ghommal's hilt 2 or better can replace a magic offhand if you wish to avoid the prayer drain effect.
• Range equipment for Ahrim. With Air spells or a Tumeken's shadow this can be skipped for fewer equipment switches.
• Melee equipment for melee special attacks or getting reward potential.
• A saturated heart or other magic potion will boost powered staves considerably.
• Super combat and Ranging potions will speed up killing Ahrim and Karil.
• Use the rune pouch to store any mind, chaos, death and blood runes in.
• A Spade to enter the crypts.
• Teleport to house tablets could be replaced by a Construction cape or max cape.
• Barrows teleport tablets could be replaced with the barrows teleport in the Portal Nexus.
• Bringing a Strange old lockpick helps speed up runs by skipping through any doors in the crypts.

|-|
Ranged (Ahrim)=
Without a Shadow or Air spells, Ahrim is easiest to defeat with ranged attacks. A Blowpipe, Magic shortbow, or Karil's crossbow are common weapons to use. Use your special attacks on Ahrim to speed up the fight, as he can drain your other combat stats the longer the fight continues.

Callisto.transport:
• With 90 Magic, players on the Ancient spellbook can use Annakarl Teleport, which will teleport them into the Demonic Ruins. Simply go south of your location after arriving. Be wary of PK'ers upon arrival. This is the fastest way to reach Callisto.
• Alternatives to this also include the Annakarl teleport tablet and a portal attuned to Annakarl. Be wary of PK'ers on arrival; if using the house portal, you should have a scrying pool to check the area first.
• With 57 Woodcutting, players can make a Waka canoe and use it to go to the Wilderness. Go north-east of your location, but be wary of PKers.
• Having a royal seed pod makes this strategy more effective as this teleport takes the player close to a gnome glider which they can then take to Al Kharid (specified as Kar-Hewo on the destinations menu) and then walk to the canoe station past the Al Kharid toll gate. This means that the royal seed pod can be used as a lv 30 Wilderness teleport, as a banking tool, and as a way to reach Callisto.
• If you have neither of these requirements, simply use the games necklace to teleport to the Corporeal Beast's lair, exit the cave then run up north. Be wary of PKers and the poison spiders if you do not plan to hug the lava river.
• Players who have completed the Hard or Elite Wilderness Diary can use the Wilderness Sword to teleport to the Fountain of Rune and run south-west to Callisto.

Callisto.intro:
Callisto is an enormous bear empowered by the corruption of the Wilderness that resides in Callisto's Den at level 40 Wilderness and is the one of two monsters to drop the tyrannical ring.

Ironmen are eligible for drops from Callisto when defeating it alongside other players.

In order to enter Callisto's lair, the player must have completed the medium Wilderness Diary tasks, OR they must have a Callisto boss Slayer task (a bear Slayer task does not bypass the diary requirement). Entering the boss lair requires players to pay a fee of 50,000 coins; this fee does not need to be brought along in the inventory, and can be deducted from the bank.
Callisto.strategy:
Callisto is a level 470 bear that can be found inside Callisto's Den. He is killed for the valuable Voidwaker hilt, claws of Callisto, tyrannical ring, and Callisto cub, though he can also drop the dragon 2h sword and dragon pickaxe. Completion of the medium Wilderness Diary is required to fight Callisto.

• Like all Wilderness bosses, Callisto resides in a multi-way area and in level 39 Wilderness. You may be attacked at any time during the kill. Do not bring any items that you are not willing to lose.

Cerberus.transport:
Cerberus' Lair can be found in Taverley Dungeon, at the hellhounds' area. There will be a small opening that players can crawl into to enter the lair.

Effective ways to get to Taverley Dungeon include teleporting to Falador and using the wall shortcut near the West bank, only a short run from the dungeon entrance, or moving one's Player-owned house to Taverley, exiting via the house portal and running south. Alternatively, if using Arceuus spellbook for thralls, one can change their death respawn location to Falador, and use the respawn teleport running west to the wall shortcut.

Due to the huge distance from a bank to Cerberus' lair, it is highly encouraged that players do not attempt the boss until they have 65 or higher Agility, as attempting to run from the entrance to her lair the normal way is extremely unfeasible. 70 Agility is required for the pipe shortcut, and 80 for the wall trap shortcut. Both can be boosted, meaning 65/75 Agility is the minimum needed to use the shortcuts. This avoids the use of a dusty key; if entering from pipe, have Protect from Magic active before going in to avoid potentially getting scorched by a blue dragon. If entering from the wall spikes, attack a skeleton and let it attack once before jumping, as the occasional poison spider can wander around the area.

Alternatively, key master teleports can be used to teleport directly to the Key Master outside Cerberus' Lair.
