Cerberus.intro:
Cerberus is a level 318 hellhound boss who resides in Cerberus' Lair, deep beneath the Taverley Dungeon in the cave entrance in the north-east part of the hellhound area, which is found beyond the poisonous spiders. Defeating Cerberus requires a Slayer level of 91, along with a task of hellhounds or Cerberus herself. In the event of a hellhound or elite clue scroll task, wild pies may be used to boost the player's Slayer level. While boosting, the player's Slayer level must remain at or above 91.

Cerberus drops three different crystals: the eternal, pegasian, and primordial crystals which are used to upgrade the infinity, ranger, and dragon boots to the eternal, pegasian, and primordial boots respectively, which boast the second highest bonuses for the feet slot. She can also drop the smouldering stone at a much better rate compared to her lesser brethren, along with the jar of souls and the hellpuppy pet.

A dwarf multicannon cannot be set up inside Cerberus' Lair; if attempted, players will receive the message:
Cerberus.strategy:
.]]
Cerberus is a high level Slayer boss. A Slayer level of 91 and a slayer task of Cerberus or hellhounds is required to inflict damage. Wild pies can be used to boost the player's Slayer level, but only if they have a minimum of 86 Slayer, and the boost must be maintained for the entire kill.

It is the only monster to drop the eternal, pegasian, and primordial crystals which are used to upgrade the infinity, ranger, and dragon boots into the eternal, pegasian, and primordial boots respectively.

In addition, it is also able to drop a Smouldering stone, which can be combined with a dragon axe, pickaxe, or harpoon to turn them into their respective infernal counterparts: the infernal axe, pickaxe, and harpoon.

General strategy:
While fighting Cerberus, it is recommended to activate Protect from Magic.

For the most kills per hour, the player should be on the Arceuus spellbook for thralls and bring a Book of the Dead. If using melee, you can optionally bring soul and death runes for Death Charge for more frequent special attacks but less space for supplies. Runes to cast Ward of Arceuus are recommended for players who do not own a spectral spirit shield to reduce prayer drain, although beware the spell will not reduce damage inflicted by standing in lava pools. Otherwise, no spells are needed and you do not need to bring any runes. Demonic Offering can also be used to restore prayer points, and can be useful when countering the souls attack, since there is no penalty for not having 30 prayer upon being hit. If you are suiciding supplies into the room for longer trips, bring alch runes.

As a hellhound-type boss, Cerberus has high offensive stats (220) but has a low Defence level (100). She is weak to melee attacks, primarily crush-based ones. She is slightly resistant to stab attacks and resistant against slash, magic and ranged attacks. As a demonic creature, she is also weak to Arclight and Emberlight, which should be set to stab unless the player is using oathplate armour which offers significant accuracy bonuses to slash. Despite her resistance to ranged, ranged weapons can still be extremely effective against her, in particular the twisted bow. A scorching bow also offers a very practical means to kill the boss, offering similar DPS to non-max melee setups.

Upon spawning, Cerberus cannot be attacked; rather, she only has an examine option as she is sitting. Once she detects a player in the arena, she will stand up to confront the intruder and become attackable. If no players are present inside, she will return to the centre of her chamber and her attack option will be removed, which will also restore all of her health if damaged.

It is recommended to deal damage as quickly as possible while taking note of Cerberus' attacks. The most common cause of death is the lava pool and soul combo, regardless of which one comes first. For example, during attacks 14 and 15, Cerberus will summon souls first, then follow up this attack with lava pools. The pools usually disorient players as they try to avoid them and eat up, forgetting about the souls who can deal heavy or fatal damage in the process. Simply count Cerberus' attacks and deal with the spirits as highest priority. Ranged users usually have an advantage over melee users since the targeted pool is not applied on the same tick Cerberus initiates the mechanic, giving them more time to move away from the pool and granting their full attention to the incoming souls. Melee users will simply need to count the attacks and try to avoid running into any other pools in place.

The summoned souls are the most resource-intensive part of the fight, as they cause heavy, unavoidable damage/drain; an unblocked hit deals 30 damage, while a blocked one drains 30 prayer instead, which can significantly cut into profits and supplies. Having a spectral spirit shield halves the drain to both prolong trips and increase overall profit, while Ward of Arceuus reduces the drain by 33%; having both reduces the drain by 66%. While very expensive and only particularly useful for melee users, an elysian spirit shield can reduce the damage taken from each soul attack from 30 to 22. It is also possible to use Demonic Offering to reduce prayer consumption. For an incoming souls attack, one needs to have just enough prayer for the first 2 attacks (so slightly more prayer points than is drained from 1 attack). Then quickly, after the second hit and with 0 prayer, cast Demonic Offering on the ash from the previous kill (restoring a bit of prayer), and immediately pray against the third attack.

It is recommended to start each Cerberus kill standing underneath her and attacking her from there.

Cerberus attacks on a six-tick (3.6s) cycle, while a scythe attacks on a five-tick (3.0s) cycle. It is possible to hit Cerberus twice for every attack she makes due to this by going under her for a few ticks, then coming out to attack. This significantly increases the scythe's damage and minimises the amount of attacks Cerberus can perform. With high hits and proper execution, this will remove a lot of the boss's health, and in some cases, even kill her before she can summon souls.

No Ghosts Strategy:
A slower but less resource intensive strategy (particularly for ironmen who don't have a spectral spirit shield or hardcore ironmen who want to avoid dealing with the lava pools and ghosts at once), the player can hit Cerberus to just above 400 hitpoints and wait until the 14th attack (~56 seconds) which ensures no ghosts will appear until the 28th attack. This will reduce prayer potion usage to about two doses per kill if prayer flicking is used while waiting for the 14th attack. It is recommended to put on defensive gear, such as a Dinh's bulwark, and step away from Cerberus while waiting for the 14th attack to minimise damage taken while waiting. Guthan's the Infested equipment can also be used (consider equipping a Lightbearer too), as its subpar dps might get Cerberus to 400 h

Chaos Elemental.intro:
The Chaos Elemental is a dark cloud with six tentacles that dwells in the members-only section of the Wilderness, just west of the Rogues' Castle. This area is moderately easy to access from the deep Wilderness teleport lever in Ardougne or Edgeville. The nearby Wilderness Obelisk can randomly teleport players south-east of the Rogues' Castle; after the hard Wilderness Diary is completed, the location can be chosen from any Wilderness obelisk.

The Chaos Elemental is generally killed for its dragon 2h sword and pickaxe drops. It also has a higher drop rate of the pet chaos elemental compared to the Chaos Fanatic. In addition, it is immune to venom—any items that are able to inflict venom will inflict regular poison instead.

• As this boss is located deep within the Wilderness, and wanders around in a multi-combat zone, beware of player-killers! Do not bring items you are not willing to lose.

Killing the Chaos Elemental is a requirement for the Hard Wilderness Diary.

Fighting the Chaos Elemental is a matter of countering its unequip attack by keeping your inventory full and avoiding player killers. As it attacks with random damage types, you will always be taking damage unless you are flinching or using the safe spot. Therefore, it is critical to maximise the amount of healing you bring while minimising your risk. Dragonhide armour is effective. Always check your Items Kept on Death before fighting this boss, and never bring anything you are not willing to lose.

Chaos Fanatic.intro:
The Chaos Fanatic is a relatively simple boss that resides west of the Lava Maze in level 42 Wilderness, surrounded by miniature chaotic clouds that serve as unattackable scenery. His special attack mechanic is similar to that of the crazy and deranged archaeologists.

The Chaos Fanatic is notable for dropping one of the three shards that form the malediction ward and odium ward, with the Crazy archaeologist and Scorpia dropping the other pieces. Killing all three at least once is a hard Wilderness Diary task.

He is one of the only monsters to drop the ancient staff, along with mummies, Calvar'ion, and the thermonuclear smoke devil.
Chaos Fanatic.strategy:
The Chaos Fanatic is a relatively simple boss similar to the Crazy archaeologist and the Deranged archaeologist; his special attack has the potential to cause major damage if not avoided.

Due to his high magic level and defensive bonuses, the most effective strategy is to use Ranged while protecting from magic and avoiding his green special attack by moving away from where you are standing.

Players can optionally walk to the altar that lies to the south-west in order to recharge their prayer after each fight, although this is a highly active player killing spot. Player killers can only attack you in between kills while waiting for the boss to respawn, so always be aware of players nearby who may be waiting for you to finish your kill.

In order to escape from player killers, a good option is to make use of the Wilderness obelisk to the north to teleport to level 13 Wilderness (possible to guarantee after completion of the hard Wilderness Diary) which will then allow the player to teleport away using a standard teleport method. Players can also run east into the King Black Dragon Lair (non-Wilderness) and teleport from there.

Equipment:

Activate Protect from Magic, and be prepared to use Protect Item if 4-iteming. Similar to the chaos elemental, he can unequip your items.

Note: Ensure you are not risking more than you are willing to lose.

It is recommended to use inventory blocking food as he cannot disarm you if there are no slots in your inventory for your weapons. Examples of this are Pies, Curry, and Stew. Another option since the release of Sailing are Armadyl brews, which can heal up to 44 in a single inventory slot, keep your ranged boost up, leave a vial behind and works well with blighted super restores.

If you are using potions, it is advised to make sure that vial smashing is turned off. This option can be turned off in the settings menu under the gameplay section. Blighted super restore can be used, as it's in the Wilderness.

Commander Zilyana.intro:
Commander Zilyana is the appointed leader of Saradomin's forces in the God Wars Dungeon and one of only three known still living representatives of the Icyene race, one being the half-human half-Icyene Safalaan and the other being a full-blooded Icyene encountered during the quest The Blood Moon Rises.

To gain access to her chamber within the Saradomin Encampment, players must use an ecumenical key or have killed 40 of Saradomin's followers throughout the dungeon. Furthermore, in addition to an Agility level of 70 (cannot be boosted), players must bring two ropes on their first visit in order to navigate obstacles in the encampment. Note, if this is your first time entering the God Wars Dungeon, you will need a total of three ropes.
Commander Zilyana.strategy:
This is a guide to defeating Commander Zilyana, the Saradominist general in the God Wars Dungeon.

While Commander Zilyana has an equal amount of resistance to all attacks, Magic (apart from the Tumeken's shadow) is generally impractical here due to the lack of defence provided by magic armour and unnecessary rune costs.

Requirements:
• Completion of Death Plateau and the start of Troll Stronghold to the point where you defeat Dad
• Alternatively, Ghommal's hilt can be used to teleport to Trollheim without requiring either quest
• One rope is required to access the God Wars Dungeon for the first time.
• Two (additional) ropes are required to navigate Saradomin's Encampment for the first time.
• Level 70 Agility is required to access Saradomin's Encampment (cannot be boosted).
• Level 37 Prayer to activate Protect from Magic.

General Strategy:
Similarly to Kree'arra, many players prefer using an ecumenical key to skip kill count. Although Saradominist kill count is considered to be somewhat quick, this is only partially true if the player has 83 Slayer, as Saradominist spiritual warriors and mages are aggressive towards Zamorakian followers. The remaining Saradominist followers are passive and will only attack in self-defence.

Zilyana attacks with both melee and magic. Pray Protect from Magic while killing Zilyana if using ranged or Protect from Missiles if using mage. If done correctly the only damage you should take is from the range or mage minion, respectively. Although her max hit is relatively low, with her melee attacks dealing up to 27 damage and her magic dealing 10-20 damage, she makes up for this with an attack speed of 2 (1.2 seconds). Combined with her tremendous accuracy, this makes fighting her in melee range extremely dangerous, as the precise attacks and rapid attack speed will cause a swift death for her target. Like Graardor and K'ril however, Zilyana can only attack when in melee distance of a player.

Zilyana has three bodyguards; Bree, Growler and Starlight, who use ranged, magic and melee with maximum hits of 16, 16 and 15 damage respectively. Her bodyguards are significantly weaker compared to the other generals', but they still should not be underestimated.

The kiting method should be used when fighting Zilyana, as her chamber is quite large. This means that damage will only be incurred from the bodyguard that the player is not protecting against, as Starlight and Zilyana will not be able to reach the player unless they stop moving. The most common method involves running around the chamber, though there are advanced methods that reduce or even negate the need for stamina potions, even with low Agility levels.

Bellock, the crazy archaeologist, is a relatively simple boss that resides in the ruins south of The Forgotten Cemetery within level 23 Wilderness. His special attack mechanic is similar to that of the Deranged archaeologist and the Chaos Fanatic.

Dagannoth Kings.intro:
The Dagannoth Kings (commonly abbreviated DKs) are a group of three dagannoth that live deep in the cave on Waterbirth Island which is a multiway combat area. They are all level 303, and also represent the combat triangle. Each of the kings uses a different combat style, is weak against the type that defeats them on the combat triangle, and has a high defence against all others. They all have their own unique ring drops, with Rex having two - these rings give the second best bonuses for their respective combat styles in the ring slot. All three kings have the ability to drop the dragon axe, and also drop dagannoth bones.

Killing all three Dagannoth Kings is a requirement for the Elite Fremennik Diary.
Dagannoth Kings.strategy:
Dagannoth Kings are a trio of bosses found in the Waterbirth Island Dungeon, known for their dragon axe, berserker ring, archers ring, warrior ring and seers ring drops. Their bones are also valuable, making them consistently rewarding to kill.

Strategy:

As the Kings all attack with different styles, reducing the amount of time spent attacking multiple Kings is essential for staying alive and extending trips. This can be done by killing the Kings in a cycle and utilising the downtime before they respawn to safely kill the other kings, by safespotting, or by attacking a King outside the aggression range of the others. The aggression range for Dagannoth Rex is 5 tiles from their south-western tile. The aggression range for Dagannoth Prime and Dagannoth Supreme is 7 tiles from their south-western tile. As Dagannoth Kings are size 3x3 monsters you can get closer to Dagannoth Kings if you're in the north-eastern side of the room.

Download the tile markers above to show safespots for Rex, along with ladder locations throughout the entire dungeon route.

Equipment:
The Dagannoth Kings can take a long time to reach and can be difficult to setup properly, so it is often more valuable to reduce unnecessary gear switches and bring extra supplies in order to extend trips. Balance damage output between each style, (if killing all 3 Kings), with ranged defence and prayer bonus to reduce unnecessary damage taken from the Spinolyps.

Tribrid (Solo) =
A tribrid setup means a single player using Magic, Ranged and Melee to kill all three Dagannoth Kings. It is only recommended for people who can afford good enough equipment to be able to kill all Kings fast enough.

If the player is not experienced, an alternative to attacking all three kings is to have another person targeting Rex, while the player targets Prime and Supreme. The person targeting Rex may help defeat Prime/Supreme if needed.

Because the run there takes so long, especially without the shortcuts, overall kills per hour are maximised by ensuring you complete a full Slayer task in only 1 trip, or as few trips as possible. It's preferable to sacrifice some DPS in favour of sustainability if you need to do so in order to last the full task. It's often worthwhile minimising gear swaps to bring more supplies (e.g. using Barrows gloves instead of Ferocious gloves + Zaryte vambraces, ignoring Bandos tassets) or favouring sustainability oriented gear (e.g. using Spectral spirit shield instead of a defender, using Guardian boots over Primordials, using SGS + Lightbearer over offensive options)

|-|
Magic (Rex only) =
This setup is used to solo Dagannoth Rex. Rex is the easiest out of all the Kings as it can be safespotted, and offers the chance of receiving the berserker ring. Long trips can be achieved using Guthan's armour set, a Saradomin godsword or blood spells on the Spinolyps in between kills.

Magic is highly effective against Rex due to his extremely low magic defence. With a decent Magic level, players can wear full melee armour for the increased ranged defence and still hit Rex consistently.

For midgame players, Rex's 35% weakness to earth spells means that Earth Wave will do more damage than Iban Blast at a Magic level of 75, or upon unlocking it if using an elemental amulet or amulet of earth. It will also outdamage the warped sceptre at most Magic levels. Earth Blast however will always be weaker than Iban Blast.

|-|
Ranged (Prime only) =
Players may wish to kill only Dagannoth Prime for its unique drops or the pet. Once inside the north-east corner of the room, Prime can be ranged while remaining out of aggression range of Supreme and Rex. Use of Telekinetic Grab will aid in collecting drops. Maximise ranged strength and accuracy, or bring additional tank gear or switches to heal while waiting for Prime to respawn.

The quickest methods of reaching Ghorrock Prison, where Duke Sucellus resides, are:
• Using the ring of shadows to teleport to the Ghorrock Dungeon. This requires having used the frozen tablet on it, which is an untradeable 1/25 drop from Duke Sucellus.

Duke Sucellus.intro: Duke Sucellus (pronounced ) is a chthonian demon sealed in Ghorrock Prison, who is encountered during Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire. A high-ranking commander of the Zarosian Empire, Sucellus took informal command of the remaining forces of the Empire after the Betrayal of Zaros. A stronger variant of him can be fought again after the completion of the quest.
Duke Sucellus.strategy:
After the completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire, players can fight a stronger variant of Duke Sucellus. An even stronger awakened variant can be fought by entering the asylum gates with an awakener's orb in the player's inventory and selecting "Yes" when prompted.

If the player dies while fighting Duke Sucellus, their grave will appear by the asylum gates. Players will have their reclamation fee reduced by 75% until they have five kills, after which the standard death cost will apply.

Battle phase:
Duke Sucellus has 485 health and attacks on a five-tick cycle (3.0s). It is highly recommended that players melee Sucellus, as he is weakest to slash attacks.

In addition, unlike other demonic monsters, Duke Sucellus only has a 70% vulnerability to demonbane weapons; Arclight gives a 49% boost to accuracy and damage as opposed to the usual 70%. The Ward of Arceuus spell can be used to reduce the damage of Sucellus' regular attacks (though the 10% damage reduction from the spell does not reduce damage of normal icicle attacks when using protect from melee as it is capped at 5), and the benefit does not apply to peripheral forms of damage like those inflicted by gas flares or extremities.

When in melee range (including diagonally across), Sucellus will raise his arms, causing icicles to spike up from the ground. These icicles have a 3x3 AoE and will deal up to 11 damage if Protect from Melee is not active, or 5 with. This is a standard attack and can occasionally miss, though Sucellus' high stats means this is very unlikely. Shortly afterwards, he will slam his arms back down, shattering the icicles in a 1x1 AoE on them. Getting caught in this slam will deal up to 56 damage without prayer, or 42 with, and will always hit regardless of the player's bonuses.

If outside of melee range, Sucellus will instead launch a blue projectile, which deals up to 48 damage if not protected against, and deals slightly less damage with Protect from Magic, though will generally deal significant damage. The damage only applies upon impact. However, getting hit by this attack, even if protected against, will disqualify the player from a "perfect" kill.

Due to the high, unblockable damage of Duke's magic projectile and slam attacks, players learning the Duke fight are recommended to stand directly behind the pillars on either side of Duke whenever they are not attacking. Standing behind these pillars will cause Duke to do his melee cycle, but because his slam attack does not reach diagonally, players will only take icicle chip damage.

Duke Sucellus has two special attacks:

• Freezing Gaze - Every fifth standard attack, he will open the eye within his body, indicated by the game message If the player is not standing directly behind a pillar 5 ticks (3 seconds) after the attack is initiated, the player will take up to 101 damage. This is almost assured to kill the player, so avoiding it is essential. This attack takes 6 ticks in total.
• Players can quickly get one more hit off shortly after the first game message appears, or resume attacking the instant the game message appears.
• Gas Flare - He will launch gas towards the vent closest to the player, leaving dangerous gas there for a few seconds. The gas deals up to 12 damage, which can be reduced with a slayer helmet or gas mask. Avoid them by moving to the opposite pillar.
• The Gas Flare attack will always be launched three standard attacks after the first Freezing Gaze. If above 75% health, Sucellus will use this attack after every five standard attacks, four above 25%, and three below 25%. However, Sucellus will never use this attack immediately after a Freezing Gaze, in which case it will do an extra standard attack. Once the 75% threshold is crossed (and 25% for enraged phase), the change in frequency of the Gas Flare attack will apply after the next gas flares are launched. If above 50% of his health (242 hitpoints), he will spit out one Gas Flare, and two otherwise.

Enrage phase:
Upon reaching 25% of his health (121 hitpoints), Sucellus will enter an enrage phase, attacking one tick faster to start on a 2.4 second (4 tick) cycle.

If using a five-tick weapon, you will only be able to safely attack Sucellus every two attacks, as the third attack will result in the player getting hit by his slamming attack when they do so. Should the player wish to, they may switch to a four-tick weapon such as Arclight or Emberlight to match his attack speed, however it is not necessary in normal mode.

Post fight:
If you wish to continue killing Sucellus after using up all of your Arder-musca poisons, run towards one of the mushroom spawns to immediately prepare picking them, as he will "respawn" shortly before one of them is reached.

When picking up drops, be mindful of mist rune and chaos rune drops if using the Arceuus spellbook, as these will cause other spells to become available, such as Vile Vigour and medium-tier thralls, potentially causing problems with muscle memory when spellbook filtering is enabled. These should be left on the ground until the trip concludes.

Equipment:
Duke Sucellus is weak to slash, so slashing weapons are preferred for the fight.

The scythe of Vitur will hit three times due to Sucellus' large size, but is costly to use. An Emberlight, if available, should be used for cost-conscious players as it performs slightly worse but with no upkeep, while being a 4-tick weapon which can allow for additional hits at some points in the fight. The soulreaper axe is another alternative as a five-tick weapon, however it will lose soul stacks every few kills, when the player must restock on poisons.

The effectiveness of different special attack weapons can vary depending on the rest of the gear, particularly whether you are using Oathplate armour. Without it, players can use a Bandos godsword to help lower Sucellus' Defence, as he has a very high Defence level. It is not recommended to use an elder maul or dragon warhammer because

General Graardor.intro:
General Graardor is the leader of Bandos' forces within the God Wars Dungeon. He is the only known living member of the Ourg race.

He is found in Bandos' Stronghold, which requires a Strength level of 70 and a hammer to access. To enter his quarters, players must have an ecumenical key in their inventory or have killed 40 of Bandos' followers throughout the dungeon, with goblins being the easiest of the followers to kill.
General Graardor.strategy:
This is a guide for killing General Graardor with Melee and Ranged. It has the basics of attacking and tanking, as well as providing a few examples of what equipment to bring. Note that ranged is the most straightforward combat style to use for solo players, since with proper play it is possible to avoid all damage from Graardor. In teams, it is recommended to have one player tank with melee while the rest of the party uses either melee or ranged. Requirements: • Completion of Death Plateau and partial completion of Troll Stronghold after defeating Dad. • Alternatively, Ghommal's hilt can be used to teleport to Trollheim without requiring either quest • One rope is required to access the dungeon for the first time. • Level 70 Strength is required to enter Bandos' Stronghold (cannot be boosted). • At least 43 Prayer for access to the protection prayers. • A hammer (if not bringing an Elder maul or Dragon Warhammer). General Strategy: General Graardor is a formidable foe, with high Defence, extremely powerful melee attacks, and Ranged attacks capable of hitting every player in the room at once. He is also accompanied by three goblin sergeants who use Melee (Sergeant Strongstack), Ranged (Sergeant Grimspike), and Magic (Sergeant Steelwill) attacks. In terms of Defence, as the bulk of incoming damage potential comes from his melee and Ranged attacks, players targeted by him directly should use Protect from Melee while wearing equipment with high Ranged Defence and moderate Magic Defence; in groups, those not targeted by him directly should use Protect from Missiles. When Graardor dies, his sergeants will all focus on a single player, typically the one who landed the killing blow on Graardor. With most setups leaving players the most vulnerable to Magic, the targeted player should first switch to Protect from Magic and focus on killing Steelwill. After that, switch to Protect from Missiles so as to block Grimspike's powerful and accurate attacks, leaving Strongstack - the least threatening of the three - for last. Inventory: • A weapon to autocast Ancient Magicks (such as a blood ancient sceptre, kodai wand or ancient staff) if using Blood Barrage, with a Magic robe top switch such as a virtus robe top or ancestral robe top • Saradomin godsword or Elder maul/Dragon warhammer (for special attacks) • Avernic or dragon defender switch if using dragon warhammer • Rune pouch filled with runes for Blood Barrage • Bones to peaches (tablet) tablets (or runes for Bones to Peaches in a rune pouch if not using Blood Barrage) • 2-4 super combat potions • 5-6 Super restores • 8-10 Saradomin brews • Teleport to house (tablet) or a one-click teleport (for emergency), can bring Max cape instead for the Construction and Prayer cape perks • Rest high-healing food such as anglerfish or manta rays |-| Magic= Tumeken's shadow is the most effective weapon to kill General Graardor with. Due to its multiplicative effect, small downgrades in gear and levels can have a notable impact on damage output, so it is strongly recommended to have access to gear such as Ancestral robes, an occult necklace and confliction gauntlets.

Pairing the Eye of Ayak with confliction gauntlets can be an effective strategy if freezing General Graardor due to the increased accuracy buff the confliction gauntlets provide as well.

Using thralls on the Arceuus spellbook results in the highest kills per hour, but Ancients can be easier to use by allowing players to freeze Graardor instead of 5:0 kiting, and increase sustain with Blood Barrage.

While lower tier magic weapons can be used, they will be significantly less effective and should not be used except in combination with otherwise best-in-slot gear. With a 40% Earth spell weakness, Earth Wave or Earth Surge can be a competitive option for DPS, but being on the Standard spellbook means relying on other methods to restore health. Giant Mole.intro:
The Giant Mole (Talpidae wysonian) is a relatively simple boss found in the Mole Hole under Falador Park.

The Giant Mole is notable for its guaranteed mole skin and mole claw drops, which can be traded to Wyson for unique bird nests, one of the only sources of consistent bird nests. These nests may be crushed, creating an ingredient for making Saradomin brews. It is also the source of the immaculate mole skin unique drop, used in creating the gem sack or traded to Wyson for five unique bird nests.

Killing the Giant Mole once is a hard Falador Diary task.

Grotesque Guardians.intro:
The Grotesque Guardians are a pair of gargoyles, Dusk and Dawn, found on the Slayer Tower's rooftop, whose entrance is found on the floor 2. In order to access the roof for the first time, players must unlock the gate using a brittle key obtained from killing gargoyles during a Slayer task (requiring 75 Slayer). This is a permanent unlock; once the brittle key has been used, the gate will remain accessible in future, and players will no longer be able to obtain the key as a drop.

Similar to other Slayer bosses, such as Cerberus and the Abyssal Sire, the Grotesque Guardians can only be killed while the player is assigned gargoyles or the Guardians themselves as a Slayer task. Players attempting to use the stairs to the roof without the proper Slayer task will be stopped via dialogue and be unable to proceed.

Upon Dusk's death, 1,350 Slayer experience is awarded. Completing additional tiers of the Morytania Diary will reward the player with more experience; with an additonal 33.7, 67.5, 101.5, or 135 Slayer experience after completing the easy, medium, hard or elite tier, respectively. Slayer experience per kill is not affected by the Double Trouble perk. Despite Dusk and Dawn being two different entities, killing both guardians only counts as one kill on the player's Slayer task. However, if the player has Double Trouble unlocked, two kills will be decremented from their Slayer task count upon defeating Dusk.

The Grotesque Guardians are a pair of gargoyle slayer bosses that reside at the roof of the Slayer Tower: the Guardian of Dusk and Guardian of Dawn. In order to access and fight them, players must first acquire a brittle key from regular gargoyles (or their superior variant). The key is only obtainable as a drop whilst assigned gargoyles as a slayer task, which is dropped at a rate of 1/150.

After obtaining the brittle key, players can unlock the tower's rooftop entrance on the floor 2 (right next to the gargoyle area), permanently unlocking access. However, the player must additionally be assigned gargoyles or the Grotesque Guardians themselves as a slayer task or boss task respectively.

If the player dies while fighting the Grotesque Guardians, lost items are placed into the magical chest near the rooftop entrance, where players must pay a fee of 50,000 coins to reclaim their items. Note that dying an unsafe death before reclaiming lost items from the chest will result in permanent loss of all the items inside; as such, unless the player has level 81 Agility (can be boosted) to climb the Ivy agility shortcut found west of the slayer tower's entrance, which leads up to the start of the top floor, it is highly recommended to bring a nosepeg or equivalent item to protect from aberrant spectres on the way back.

As with all other gargoyles, players must bring a rock hammer, granite hammer, or rock thrownhammer to finish them off.

Note that unlike other instances, players are kicked out of their instance after five minutes of inactivity; players are warned when there is one minute remaining, and another when thirty seconds remain. Players can reset this timer by ringing the Cloister Bell.

Requirements:
• 75 Slayer and a gargoyle slayer task
• Completion of Quest Priest in Peril to access Morytania
• A rock hammer or thrownhammer
• Unlocked the Slayer tower rooftop with a brittle key
• Melee equipment, plus Ranged or Magic if not using a halberd

Fight overview:
The fight is started by ringing the Cloister Bell, which initiates a cutscene in which the Guardians awaken and face the player; upon reaching five kill count for the boss, the bell gains a "Quick-start" option to start the fight immediately.

During the first three phases, Dusk uses a slash-style attack that deals up to 15 damage; Protect from Melee will reduce the damage dealt by 80%. Meanwhile, Dawn uses a ranged attack that deals two separate hits, both with a max hit of 9. If within melee distance, she may also kick the player for up to 15 damage. The attacks are partially blocked by prayer; praying against melee reduces the max hit of the melee attacks to 2.

Phase 1:

Dusk is immune to all damage during this phase, so the player must fight Dawn first. As she is airborne, the player must attack her with ranged, magic, or with a halberd; she is immune to non-halberd melee attacks.

Aside from her standard attacks, Dawn may launch a Stone Ball which has a 3x3 Area-of-Effect (1 tile from the centre). If struck, the player will become encased in stone, similar to the marble gargoyle's special attack, which acts as a freeze for 10 ticks (6 seconds) and deals up to 15 damage.

You can minimise damage by starting the fight from the left-most tile next to the bell, as this will automatically off-tick the Guardians.
Start with Protect from Missiles, switch to Protect from Melee when Dawn's attack animation starts, and switch back to Protect from Missiles immediately after Dusk's attack animation starts.
For less effort you can use Protect from Melee and stand next to Dawn, which will cause her to occasionally use melee attacks. Players can also dance under Dusk and use Protect from Missiles if desired.

The optimal method to attack Dawn with ranged is to stack both her and Dusk on top of each other, then using the venator bow. When charged, it will ricochet the shots and hit Dawn twice. Players can use a toxic blowpipe to attack Dawn whilst waiting for Dusk to approach. If using melee, a noxious halberd is required, as all other halberds hit too slow.

Upon reaching 55% health, she will ascend to the sky, beginning the next phase of the fight.

Phase 2:

Dusk becomes attackable during this phase. Dusk's armour protects him from both magic and ranged attacks, so players must use melee on him. Additionally, burn damage has no effect against him. Dusk has -1 flat armour, encouraging the use of multi-hit weapons, although his abysmal Defence and bonuses make any weapon viable to use.

After attacking once, he will start to charge his blinding attack, indicated by his missing wing starting to glow; simply move one tile away from Dusk to avoid the attack. Otherwise, the player will be knocked back and dealt damage in the high 20s. The player will be able to attack three times with any four or five tick weapon before needing to back away.

The knockback animation will only occur if players are right next to or under him. The timeframe to get hit by this attack is relatively short; it is safe to return back and attack Dusk once his wings cover his face, though running back to him just as he expands his wings will result in getting hit.

Throughout this phase, Dawn will also occasionally use a rockfall attack, throwing down 9-10 pieces of debris into the roof at four different speeds, indicated with looming shadows over the targeted tiles. Like Stone Ball, these rockfalls have a 3x3 AoE. Getting caught in the edges can deal up to 22 damage, while being caught directly in one will also knock the player out, stunning them for 10 ticks (6 seconds).

Lastly, standing under Dusk during this phase can result in him trampling the player for up to 40 damage and should be avoided at all costs.

When Dusk reaches 55% of his health, Dawn will descend, beginning the third phase of the fight.

K'ril Tsutsaroth.intro:
K'ril Tsutsaroth (pronounced ) is the leader of Zamorak's forces in the God Wars Dungeon.

He is located in Zamorak's Fortress, which requires 70 Hitpoints to cross the river to access. To gain access to his chamber, players must use an ecumenical key or have slain 40 Zamorakians throughout the dungeon.

He is typically killed on a Slayer task - K'ril Tsutsaroth is classified as a greater demon, and thus killing him counts towards any greater demon Slayer task and allows a player to take advantage of the damage boosting effects of a Black mask or Slayer helmet. As a demon, he is also susceptible to demonbane weapons and spells.
K'ril Tsutsaroth.strategy:
This is a guide on killing K'ril Tsutsaroth. K'ril Tsutsaroth is commonly killed for his drops which include the Zamorakian spear, staff of the dead and the Zamorak hilt. He can be fought with any of the three combat styles and either solo or in a team.

The Zamorakian encampment, including K'ril Tsutsaroth's chamber, appears shadowy and dark; the farther down players venture, the darker it becomes, becoming near pitch dark when outside the door leading to his chamber and inside itself. This is purely a visual change and has no actual gameplay effects. The shadow effect can be removed by consuming a Saradomin's light.

Requirements:
• Completion of Death Plateau and the start of Troll Stronghold to the point where you defeat Dad
• Alternatively, Ghommal's hilt can be used to teleport to Trollheim without requiring either quest
• One rope is required to access the God Wars Dungeon for the first time.
• 70 Hitpoints (boostable) are required to access Zamorak's Fortress.

General strategy:
K'ril attacks with both melee and magic, but his magic attack can only be used against players in melee range. As such, if using melee, it is recommended for solo players (or in groups, the tank) to wear armour with high magic defence and use Protect from Melee during the kill. While this approach does leave players susceptible to his occasional prayer smash attack, it is still generally more efficient than doing the opposite.

After K'ril has been killed, the minions each focus on a random player. Because of this, players should adjust their prayers accordingly and focus on killing minions which are focusing on the same player. As K'ril and his minions drop ashes, bones to peaches cannot be used, and players should manage their hitpoints adequately. In group encounters, using Guthan's is recommended; in solo encounters, Blood Barrage is more effective. When casting Blood Barrage, make sure to stack Tstanon on Zakl'n so both demons can be hit by the spell. Bringing water runes (or a Kodai wand) is optional for Ice Barrage, but can freeze Tstanon in place so the player doesn't have to flick between ranged and melee prayers as frequently.

Because bones to peaches cannot be used, it is worthwhile to bring runes for Boost Potion Share and Stat Restore Pot Share to extend trips when going in a team. If not using Lunar spells, players can use Ward of Arceuus to reduce damage taken, and Death Charge to boost special attack energy. In a team it is helpful (but not required) for one or more players to be on task.

Kalphite Queen.intro:
The Kalphite Queen (Kalphiscarabeinae pasha), also called the KQ, is the strongest of the Kalphites.

She is a powerful opponent that makes use of protection prayers, though they only function as an indicator to players of which attack styles may be most effective rather than outright blocking damage from them. She can use all three combat styles, of which her ranged and magic attacks always land as successful hits, and has two forms.

Unique drops from the Queen include the dragon 2h sword, dragon chainbody, dragon pickaxe and kq head drops. Killing her is additionally a requirement for the Desert Diary, with a hard task requiring players to kill her once and an elite task requiring the player to speak to a mounted head inside their own Player-owned house.
Kalphite Queen.strategy:
The Kalphite Queen is a boss located in the Kharidian Desert. She is stronger than her combat level suggests due to her damage output ability.

If using the non-instanced version of the Kalphite Lair, players may fill a looting bag and their inventory with supplies and die within the lair, leaving a pile of supplies on the ground for 60 minutes which allows much longer trips.

The fight:
Tip: Unless wearing a serpentine helm for the duration of the fight, either sip an antidote++ before going to the lair to save an inventory slot, or bring the potion in with you during the fight.

The Kalphite Queen has 510 Hitpoints, split across two phases. Her Magic and Ranged attacks will always land as successful hits. While unlikely, it is possible for them to land but deal no damage. Her Ranged attack will drain 1 prayer point if it rolls more than 0 damage, even if the player prevents the damage with Protect from Missiles. Her Melee attack does not share the unique accuracy mechanic, and is treated as a standard attack meaning that standing next to her will decrease her DPS. Unlike the soldiers and guardians, this melee attack does not poison. When standing in melee range of the Kalphite Queen, she has a 1/2 chance of doing a melee attack, while her Magic and Ranged attacks each have a 1/4 chance of triggering.

There are two phases of the fight, similar to Vet'ion. While in her grounded form, the Kalphite Queen has Protect from Magic and Protect from Missiles active; however, they only add increased Defence to those styles rather than full immunity like the player versions of them.

When her first form falls at zero health, her chitin will crack open to reveal her second form, a wasp-like creature. This airborne form has Protect from Melee active; however, like the first form, this only provides increased Defence.

Note: Upon triggering the second form, there is a time limit of 20 minutes for defeating it. If not defeated within this time frame, the Kalphite Queen returns to the first form, though she carries the health she had left in her second form upon reverting back.

Her ranged attack will hit players close to the main target. To avoid this, players in a group can stand on opposite sides of her. This positioning (combined with Protect from Magic) will greatly reduce the amount of damage taken over the course of the fight.

Throughout the fight, if the Kalphite Queen is near any of the bulging cocoons, there is a 1/20 chance it will hatch an aggressive Kalphite Worker each time the Queen is hit. These only stay for a while before despawning. It is advised to get the Queen near them so the workers will spawn. This is because if there are plenty of workers around her, she will be unable to move at all while they are present, and allow the player to easily flinch her for longer trips. This is only viable with melee, since melee attacks land instantly, while Ranged or Magic projectiles do not land quickly enough to flinch the boss. An exception to this are salamanders, which work like a melee weapon and can deal magic damage.

Her attacks can be tick-eaten, however her ranged and magic attacks do have different projectile speeds and as such, it is advised to always make sure to heal up when below 31 Hitpoints to prevent the risk of dying. It is recommended to step under her during this to not take more damage.

Equipment:

High Level / Resetting=
• A Dragon warhammer or Elder maul is important for lowering Kalphite Queen's defence if using melee and ranged, making both forms much faster to kill.

• The Ring of suffering (ri) is useful here due to Kalphite Queen constantly hitting you for high damage, triggering the recoil effect. Alternatively, the Lightbearer can give additional follow up special attacks if you are not resetting every kill. Both are generally better than strength rings, as extra defence reduction and recoiled damage add up over both phases.

• It is still recommended to occasionally flinch the boss when you have to eat or if your supplies are low towards the end of a kill. Step under the boss to limit the amount of times that the Kalphite Queen can hit. This can be further optimised by using a fast weapon, (such as a blowpipe), followed by a slower heavy hitting weapon, (such as a crossbow) each time you step out from underneath KQ before returning underneath. You are effectively doing 7 cycles of damage vs. the Queen's 4, and will significantly reduce the amount of damage you take throughout the fight.

• An Anglerfish can be eaten before banking for the fight to boost hitpoints for a slight advantage.

• Using a Slayer Helm (i) while on task provides a far greater bonus to DPS than any other piece of gear. If you are struggling, do Slayer tasks until you receive a kalphite task. This will massively improve your chances of success.

During both phases, it generally does not matter whether you pray Protect from Magic or Protect from Missiles, but Protect from Magic is still preferred in case another player crashes you as it can bounce between players. Also, Piety (or Mystic Vigour/Augury for magic) is strongly recommended to speed up kills. Immediately run under her again after killing off her first phase, heal up, and prepare for the second phase.

Second phase:
Players should continue to pray Protect from Magic during phase 2. Players should walk under her as soon as this phase begins, otherwise she will get an extra attack on you first. Use a DPS calculator to determine how accurate her melee attacks during this phase will be; stand within melee range if more than 50% of her melee attacks will miss on average.

King Black Dragon.intro:
The King Black Dragon, commonly referred to as KBD, is a three-headed dragon located in his lair, accessible only through the deep Wilderness. With a combat level of 276, he is one of the strongest dragons in Old School RuneScape.

His lair is a multicombat area. Though designated as a Wilderness boss, the lair itself is not in the Wilderness, so players cannot attack each other and there are no teleport restrictions. Completion of the Wilderness Diary also does not note his bone drops.

Players can pay to fight the King Black Dragon in an instanced area inaccessible by other players (right-click Private option on lever). Players do not need to carry coins on them, as the fee may be deducted from the bank. Items dropped by the boss in this instance will disappear after 30 minutes, though items dropped by the player will disappear after the typical 3 minutes.

The King Black Dragon counts towards a black dragon Slayer task, except when assigned by Krystilia.
King Black Dragon.strategy:
• While the King Black Dragon's lair is not considered to be a part of the Wilderness, you will need to cross a short distance in deep level 42-Wilderness that is commonly patrolled by Player killers. Do not bring any items into the Wilderness you are not willing to lose.

Kraken.intro:
The Kraken is a stronger and larger version of the cave kraken. It requires level 87 Slayer to kill and cannot be boosted. Located at the Kraken Cove, it can only be attacked if the player has it, or cave krakens as a Slayer task, which also requires level 50 Magic. Alongside its non-boss variants, it is the only monster that drops the Kraken tentacle and charged Trident of the Seas.

Like its smaller brethren, the Kraken is submerged underwater. Magic is the only reliable way of damaging it, as Ranged deals 1/7th of its normal damage. The Kraken cannot be reached with Melee weapons, and is additionally entirely immune to melee attacks, displaying the message if you were to hit it with a melee weapon with long enough range to reach it. To start the fight, players can use a fishing explosive on the large whirlpool. Otherwise, the four whirlpools around must first be disturbed; when all four whirlpools are disturbed, the larger one can be disturbed, which will result in the Kraken waking up. Either method will release level 112 Enormous Tentacles.

Both the Kraken and Enormous Tentacles use typeless Magic, and as such Protect from Magic does not provide any degree of damage reduction. The Kraken can hit very hard, but has very poor accuracy, while the tentacles are much more accurate but deal less damage. The Kraken's projectile resembles Fire Wave.

Players can create a Kraken instance for coins. This fee can be deducted directly from the bank; players do not need to carry coi
Kraken.strategy:
The Kraken is a Slayer boss and can therefore only be killed while on a Slayer task to kill it, or (cave) kraken. The Kraken is located in the Kraken Cove.

It is recommended to use the Magic attack style to fight the Kraken, as Ranged deals 1/7th of its normal damage and it is immune to Melee, due to the fact that it cannot be reached by Melee attacks. As there are no complex mechanics, the Kraken is a popular boss (therefore it may be hard to find an empty world). Players can alternatively create an instance for 25,000 coins, which lasts until the player leaves or logs out.

Kree'arra.intro:
Kree'arra is one of Armadyl's most trusted generals. He is the most powerful of the surviving aviansie, and leader to the forces of Armadyl's Eyrie in the God Wars Dungeon.

In order to reach the encampment, players must first wield any crossbow along with a mithril grapple. A Ranged level of at least 70 is then required to navigate the chasm. To enter the boss room, players must use an ecumenical key, or have slain 40 followers of Armadyl, with aviansie and their spiritual variants being his only followers within the dungeon.

Kree'arra can be seen yelling several battle cries in his chamber. However, unlike the other generals, his taunts are non-verbal.
Kree'arra.strategy:
This is a guide to defeating Kree'arra, the Armadyl-aligned general in the God Wars Dungeon.

As Kree'arra is airborne, regular melee attacks will not work; instead, Ranged or Magic must be used to fight him. Halberds and salamanders are the only melee options, but due to Kree'arra's extremely high melee defence, this is not generally recommended unless using the soulflame horn in small teams.

Kree'arra and his minions count toward aviansie Slayer tasks; Slayer helm (i) and black mask (i) both give the 15% accuracy and damage boost to those on task.

General Strategy:
When starting a trip at Kree'arra, many players prefer using an ecumenical key to skip kill count, as Armadylean kill count is very slow and requires the use of prayer. Kree'arra is also commonly killed on a Slayer task of Aviansie, so skipping kill count is even more desirable in this case as the player will progress their slayer task if they kill Aviansie for kill count, reducing the overall number of Kree'arra that can be killed on-task.

Kree'arra, unlike the other generals, utilises all three forms of combat. By default, he attacks with ranged and magic. The ranged attack consists of grey dust tornadoes, while the magic attack is a blue dust tornado. Kree'arra's magic attack is classified as ranged magic, meaning that its accuracy rolls against the player's ranged defence bonuses, rather than magic. The ranged attack can deal up to 69 damage, while his magic attack deals up to 21. Both of these attacks hit all players in the room, and can knock the player back a tile unless they are standing in the corners of the chamber. It is important to keep Protect from Missiles on at all times while Kree'arra is alive, or players will likely meet a swift death.

Should Kree'arra not be targeted, he will go up to his target and swipe his talons at them, dealing up to 26 damage.

Kree'arra has three bodyguards; Flight Kilisa, Wingman Skree and Flockleader Geerin, who use melee, magic and ranged respectively, capable of dealing up to 15, 16 and 25 damage respectively. Only Kilisa will be a threat, as Skree is generally inaccurate and the player is protected from Geerin's attacks.

When killed, Kree'arra and his bodyguards will drop bones, which can be converted into peaches with bones to peaches tablets. Peaches heal for 8 health, so the player can heal for 32 health after each encounter with Kree'arra and his bodyguards. The bodyguards occasionally drop two manta rays or three mushroom potatoes, which heal for 44 and 60 health respectively. These should be juggled if inventory is full.

Regardless of the method used, it is recommended to bring a staff that can autocast ancient spells to heal larger amounts after Kree'arra dies, conserving food for later kills.

Equipment:

Tumeken's Shadow=

Tumeken's shadow is currently the only weapon capable of killing Kree'arra directly that is competitive with black chinchompas. Note that it is dramatically more effective than any other magic weapon in this encounter, dealing roughly 50% more damage than the next strongest option. As such, no other magic weapons are recommended for killing Kree'arra directly.

Leviathan.requirements: • Completion of Quest Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire
Leviathan.intro:
The Leviathan is a large sea creature found within the Scar, who is encountered during Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire. Once dwelling in the Eastern Ocean, the Leviathan was inadvertently dragged into the Scar during the Battle for the Eye when Perseriya of the Forgotten Four accidentally opened an abyssal rift in an attempt to teleport reinforcements in.

It has since then adapted to the abyssal environment and has made itself at home in a large lake within the Scar, preying upon those who were unfortunate enough to be pulled into the Scar during the battle. This is seen clearly on accounts of survivors and what remains of the Zarosian fleet in the area.

It is replaced by a stronger variant after completion of the quest which the player can repeatedly fight.
Leviathan.strategy:
After the completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire, players can fight a stronger variant of the Leviathan. An even stronger awakened variant can be fought by climbing the handholds with an awakener's orb in the player's inventory and selecting "Yes" when prompted.

If the player dies while fighting the Leviathan, their grave will appear in the Scar by the rowboat. Players will have their reclamation fee reduced by 75% until they have five kills, after which the standard death cost will apply.

Fight overview:
The Leviathan uses a volley of rapid-firing attacks which deal damage upon impact; protection prayers will fully block these attacks. The lure on its head will change colours accordingly as another indicator of the attack style it is using.

Alongside the orb attacks, the Leviathan can also utilise a biting attack when in melee range, which Protect from Melee will fully block. This is rarely used since it interrupts the volley sequence, but it has no warning animation. It will only be used if the player is directly next to the pool (including diagonal tiles), and it is recommended to mark these tiles to avoid running into them.

At the end of each volley, the boss will roar and cause debris to fall around the arena, with one falling down on the player's location as a permanent spawn for the remainder of the fight. Players will take up to 7 chip damage from the roar but can avoid the debris by moving at least 1 tile away. Every subsequent volley of attacks will increase in intensity, which can make it difficult to switch prayers at later volleys. The sequence of attacks are as follows:
• 3 tick attacks with magic and ranged
• 2 tick attacks with magic and ranged
• 2 tick attacks with all three styles
• 1 tick attacks with magic and ranged
• 1 tick attacks with all three styles
• All three styles with faster projectile time (2 ticks to react)
• All three styles with even faster projectile time (1 tick to react)

At any point during the volley of attacks, players can cast any type of shadow spell to stun the Leviathan, where it will stay still for 15 ticks (9 seconds). Damage against it is capped at 10 when stunned, but the player can run around to attack the gaping wound on its backside. When attacking the backside with ranged, it deals at least a minimum of ~65% of your maximum hit as damage, whereas attacking with magic is not guaranteed to hit and is subject to the usual accuracy rolls, but will deal double damage. Using Tumeken's shadow during this mechanic can be a highly effective way to reliably deal 100+ damage, especially if stunning right before triggering enrage. The Leviathan will break out of its stun when this occurs and use a special attack as retaliation.

Leviathan will progress down this list, of attack styles, throughout the fight whether you stun or not!

If you:

Stun and attack the gaping wound on The Leviathan's back

- OR -

Stun and have done 25% of The Leviathan's health in damage

The Leviathan will reset to the 2nd attack style on the list and then progress downwards again. This will then repeat resetting to the 3rd on your second stun, so on and so forth until The Leviathan reaches its fastest attack. This means you should use your shadow spells to stun sparingly.

Enrage phase:

Upon reaching 180 hitpoints (20% of its health), the Leviathan will begin to focus on the player intensely, beginning the enrage phase. It will roar, causing one set of debris to drop on the arena, while an abyssal pathfinder will spawn. The abyssal pathfinder will spawn in the north-west corner of the arena, unless the spawn tile is blocked by debris. If blocked, it will instead spawn in the next corner following a clockwise pattern, unless all four spawn tiles are blocked, which will cause it to spawn in the original north-west corner. The Leviathan will also change its attack speed to 2, (i.e. 1.2 seconds) between attacks regardless of the state it was in before the phase started. It will only use magic and ranged orbs in this state, though it can still bite players if they are next to it.

The abyssal pathfinder has a 5x5 Area-of-Effect that the player must stand in; if the player is not in its AoE, the Leviathan's attacks will pierce through protection prayers and the player's attacks will deal less damage. The player will glow when they are within the pathfinder's AoE, and will be granted perfect accuracy and an increased minimum hit, so switching to a toxic blowpipe can be beneficial for its increased attack speed. Attacking with magic instead of ranged while within the pathfinder's AoE will grant doubled damage instead of perfect accuracy.

Players who have a webweaver bow can instead use the special attack twice to immediately finish it off, however in most cases a lightbearer will not be able to restore back to full energy for the next kill. This approach is not recommended for players with a zaryte crossbow, and players using the crossbow should bring a toxic blowpipe switch in place of the webweaver bow.

Until the phase ends, debris will continually drop from above, including the permanent blocker debris, so it is important to defeat the boss before too many appear and restrict movement. Once the Leviathan is slain, all debris on the field will be removed.

Phantom Muspah.transport:
The quickest methods of reaching Weiss, where the Phantom Muspah resides, are:
• Using the ring of shadows to teleport to Ghorrock Dungeon. Requires completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire and the frozen tablet, obtained from Duke Sucellus.
• Using an icy basalt. Go through the gap in the fence.

Once in Weiss, enter the salt mine (accessible from the staircase in Snowflake and My Arm's hut) and go deeper into the cave to enter the Ghorrock Dungeon. Then, run south.
Phantom Muspah.requirements: • Completion of Quest Secrets of the North to access the Ghorrock Dungeon
Phantom Muspah.intro:
The Phantom Muspah is a boss first fought as the Strange Creature during the Secrets of the North quest. After the events of the quest, leftover energy manifests into a stronger version of the boss that shares the same attacks and mechanics.

All forms of the Phantom Muspah have 33% freeze resistance, meaning it will only stay frozen for 66% of the base freeze duration.

If players die against the Muspah, their grave will appear outside the lair in the Ghorrock Dungeon. When the Muspah is defeated, it will respawn after 30 seconds.

Unique drops from the boss include ancient essence, used in the creation of forgotten brews or upgrading the imbued heart into a saturated heart; the ancient icon, used to upgrade the ancient staff into an ancient sceptre; and the venator shard, of which five can be combined to create the venator bow, a unique bow that shines in multicombat situations.
Phantom Muspah.strategy:
After completion of Secrets of the North, a stronger version of the Strange Creature can be fought again in the form of a Phantom Muspah (aka, "Muspah").

Fight overview:

The Phantom Muspah can spawn in ranged or melee form, and will trigger special attacks at 75% and 50% health. Ranged spawns will trigger Lightning clouds at 75%, melee spawns will trigger homing spikes at 75%. The unused special will always occur at 50% health.

• Players may deal large hits at the end of a ranged form, which will count towards ending the melee form.
• Hitting Muspah below 637 HP before hitting under 650 HP prevents Muspah from entering ranged form before his lightning cloud special attack. This allows you a full 100 damage against range form instead of switching to melee immediately after.
• Large amounts of damage dealt during the lightning cloud special attack can potentially skip the entirety of the final melee phase.
• Lightning Clouds - Muspah will rapidly teleport around the arena and spawn lightning clouds that travel across the area.
• Getting hit by a cloud will deal up to 20 damage, though they can be avoided by standing on a specific tile, provided with the button above. Players should avoid standing on this tile until the attack occurs, so that spikes aren't protruding on it.
• Muspah will always appear to the north-east when the move is finished.
• Muspah has combat stats equal to Range form, and can be attacked during this phase.
• Damage dealt during this phase does not count towards the damage threshold for a form swap.
• Homing Spikes - The Phantom Muspah will slam the ground, causing 2-4 spikes to home in on the player.
• Players can stand behind hardened spikes to avoid the homing spikes from reaching them if there's more than one spike grouped together.
• The spikes move 1 tile per 2 ticks, do not move diagonally, and cannot pass through idle spikes.
• After , the spikes harden and stop moving.
• Spikes that are directly adjacent to the player and under the Phantom Muspah will never be chosen to home in on the player.

Shielded phase:
Upon reaching less than 127 health, Muspah will teleport to the centre of the arena and unleash a massive shockwave that engulfs the entire arena. Players must stand behind a spike to avoid the attack, or it will deal up to 80 damage and the subsequent corruption will drain more prayer points compared to its magic attack. Players can place spikes on 8 specific tiles (also provided with the above button) to block the shockwave most efficiently. Spikes being on all 8 tiles is unlikely, but would completely negate a shockwave. Once Muspah finishes the attack, it will change into its shielded form, activating a prayer shield and Soul Split, as well as increasing the max hit and accuracy of its attacks.

The prayer shield has 75 health, and is drained by 2 after each attack. The Phantom Muspah will also heal itself for 50% of the damage inflicted, rounded down to the nearest whole number; e.g., a hit of 23 will cause it to heal 11 health. The player can further speed up the drain by using various prayer-draining methods, such as the Smite prayer or having a corruption spell active. If using a corruption spell it is recommended to activate Mark of Darkness first as it increases the effectiveness of corruption spells.

Using a crossbow with enchanted sapphire bolts or enchanted sapphire dragon bolts is highly recommended, as they have a 25% chance (27.5% with completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary) to activate their special effect against the prayer shield, draining around 33 prayer from it.

To successfully use Smite, players should avoid lining up their attacks with Muspah's ranged or magic attacks. Players can utilise the following five-tick cycle to determine when they can use Smite:

• Tick 1: Muspah's ranged attack damage is calculated (Protect from Ranged must be active on this tick to reduce damage)
• Tick 2: Empty (can use Smite)
• Tick 3: Empty (can use Smite)
• Tick 4: Muspah's magic attack damage is calculated (Protect from Magic must be active on this tick to avoid damage)
• Tick 5: Empty (can use Smite)

If the player is using a weapon with a five-tick attack speed, such as a crossbow on rapid, attacking Muspah on the first possible tick of the shielded phase will ensure that the player always attacks on Tick 2 of the above cycle, allowing them to flick Smite consistently. If players find themselves attacking on Tick 1 or Tick 4 of the cycle, it is advisable to delay their next attack by one tick to offset their attacks.

Note that because this attack cycle is one tick faster than in previous phases, there is one less tick between a magic attack landing and the next ranged attack being calculated. As a result, players should be prepared to switch prayers quickly after a magic projectile hits them.

Once the shield is depleted, Muspah will return to its ranged form—though still with a five-tick attack speed—and create a large number of spikes (including one on the player's position) before resuming combat as normal. The spikes will emerge every four attacks and cover more tiles, growing from existing clusters of spikes.

Equipment:

Ideally, use both Ranged and Magic, to exploit the weaknesses of both forms. Camping a single form will result in greatly increased kill times, with range camp generally being slightly more optimal. To a lesser extent, Magic-only setups with best-in-slot mage

Sarachnis.intro:
Sarachnis, the mother of the temple spiders, is a mid-level boss found in the Forthos Dungeon, in a former burial tomb south of the Spider Den.

Sarachnis has several notable unique drops, including the Sarachnis cudgel, a non-degradeable crush weapon, and the pristine spider silk, used to upgrade the herb sack into the Silklined herb sack. Other drops include the giant egg sac, which is one of the few consistent sources of non-Wilderness red spiders' eggs, and improved drop rates of Forthos Dungeon-unique items.

She additionally has a high drop rate of elite clue scrolls for the relative time to defeat her.

She can be killed as part of a spider Slayer task.

Players may choose to pay to fight Sarachnis in an instanced area via the thick web opening to her lair. This is reduced to after claiming the rewards from the hard tier of Combat Achievements. Payment for an instance will be taken from the player's bank.
Sarachnis.strategy:
Sarachnis is a mid-level boss located in the Forthos Dungeon. She is often killed for her Sarachnis cudgel, pristine spider silk, and elite clue scroll drops.

Players can create an instanced version of Sarachnis' arena for 25,000 coins via the thick web opening to her lair, which lasts until the player leaves or logs out.

Mechanics:

Sarachnis has several attacks that she will occasionally use other than the standard melee and ranged attacks. Her melee attacks consist of smashing the player with her legs, while she launches barbed projectiles as her ranged attack.

• Healing strike - Sarachnis' standard attacks will heal her on successful hits, indicated by a magenta hitsplat. She heals 5 health for every successful melee attack, and 10 health for every successful ranged attack, regardless of how much damage she actually deals, including zeros.
• Sticky web - Every four standard attacks, Sarachnis will screech out and shoot out a sticky web that leaves players bound for 6 ticks (3.6 seconds), then moving a short distance away from where she was before attacking the player. This attack can be completely negated by wearing aranea boots.
• Spawns - When Sarachnis reaches 66% and 33% health, she summons two Spawn of Sarachnis per player; a level 68 that uses Magic and has a maximum hit of 11, and a level 107 that uses Melee and has a maximum hit of 13. Both have 30 health.

Strategy:
Sarachnis is weak to crush weapons, and has high magic and ranged defence. Therefore, it is recommended to bring high strength bonus equipment and a crush weapon that can attack fast (such as an abyssal bludgeon).

Sarachnis attacks with melee when players are next to her, and Ranged when she cannot reach them; it is advised to pray Protect from Melee or Protect from Missiles accordingly, as these attacks can hit up to 31 if they aren't protected against, and also heal her if they do manage to hit. Her melee range is deceptively large, so players are advised to exercise caution when standing near her.

Additionally, lower-levelled players may wish to kill the blue magic-using Spawn of Sarachnis. The melee spawns may be tanked with sufficiently high defensive bonuses, but are not necessary to kill as the player should be praying Protect from Melee outside her web attack.

Players fighting Sarachnis can avoid getting snared by her web attack by wearing aranea boots throughout the fight. This allows the player to attack more frequently and avoid taking ranged attacks at all, avoiding prayer switches entirely. If these strategies are not able to be used, eating food only while bound by her web is recommended to maximise damage dealt.

All tiles directly adjacent to walls are out of Sarachnis's melee range. Standing on one of these tiles and praying Protect from Missiles will nullify all of her damage, but not the damage of her spawn.

When Sarachnis is killed, any remaining spawns will automatically die off with her. She will respawn in 17 ticks (10.2s).

Aranea boots allow the player to avoid Sarachnis' web attack, but their cost may be prohibitive for lower level players. Without their use, it is beneficial to be prepared to swap to Protect from Missiles during the fight when outside of her melee range.

Scorpia.intro:
Scorpia is a large female scorpion boss that resides in a cave beneath the Scorpion Pit located in Wilderness level 53-55.

Scorpia is notable for dropping one of the three shards that form the malediction ward and odium ward, with the Crazy archaeologist and Chaos Fanatic dropping the other pieces. Killing all three at least once is a hard Wilderness Diary task.
Scorpia.strategy:
Scorpia is a powerful Wilderness boss capable of poisoning her opponents starting at 20 damage as well as hitting up to 16 with melee. Her lair, located beneath the Scorpion Pit, is filled with many Scorpia's offspring, which use accurate ranged attacks with a max hit of 2 and inflict poison starting at 6 damage.

Once Scorpia reaches 99 health or lower, she will summon two Scorpia's guardians which will continually heal Scorpia when within 3 tiles of her until they are killed or despawned. They will not heal her if they are underneath her. The guardians will not respawn if killed, and will despawn if they are unable to reach Scorpia for 15 seconds.

An effective strategy is to exploit her low magic defence by using Ice Barrage to freeze her (Ice Burst, Ice Blitz, or Entangle will also work fine), staying out of melee range while attacking her with magic, and praying Protect from Missiles to prevent damage from Scorpia's offspring. Once her guardians spawn, players should wait until Scorpia is about to become unfrozen, then quickly freeze both guardians and lure Scorpia far away from them. This should cause the guardians to despawn, allowing Scorpia to be easily finished off.

Equipment:
The setup primarily consists of only taking 3 or 4 expensive items as this boss resides in a multi-combat area in level 50+ Wilderness, meaning player killers may quickly kill off-guard players.

Scorpia is not immune to venom and poison; therefore, using a trident of the swamp will do some additional damage over the course of the kill. Due to her low magic defence, a minimally geared player will rarely miss, therefore magic damage and prayer bonus should be prioritised over magic accuracy to reduce risk and prolong trips.

If bringing a powered staff, a magic boost such as a Magic potion, forgotten brew, or saturated/imbued heart will provide additional magic damage.

Thermonuclear Smoke Devil.title: Thermonuclear smoke devil
Thermonuclear Smoke Devil.intro:
The thermonuclear smoke devil, often referred to as thermy, is the boss version of the smoke devil. It requires a minimum of 93 Slayer to damage. Located at the Smoke Devil Dungeon south of Castle Wars, the Thermonuclear smoke devil can only be attacked on a smoke devil task, with the exception of one kill for the Western Provinces Diary (provided that the player has 93 Slayer without boosting).

It is the only monster to drop the smoke battlestaff, jar of smoke, and the pet smoke devil. It drops the occult necklace at a higher rate than smoke devils.

Unlike most NPCs, the Thermonuclear smoke devil is always able to walk through other monsters/players. This is to prevent players from safespotting the boss using the smoke devils found in its lair.

A dwarf multicannon cannot be used inside the boss room. If it is set up, the cannon will be destroyed.

Vardorvis.transport:
The quickest methods of reaching the Stranglewood Ritual Site, where Vardorvis resides, are:
• Using the ring of shadows to teleport to the Stranglewood Temple entrance. This requires having used the strangled tablet on it, which is a 1/25 drop from Vardorvis.
• Using fairy ring code fairy ring BLS and run west to the rowboat. From there, run all the way west to the entryway leading to the Ritual Site.
• Using Xeric's talisman to teleport to Xeric's Honour, running east to the Mountain Guide and travelling to the base of Mount Quidamortem, then running west to the rowboat.
• Using Rada's blessing to teleport to the Kourend Woodland. From there, run north-east to Buneir and ride the Lovakengj Minecart Network to Mount Quidamortem. Run north-east to the Mountain Guide and travel to the base of Mount Quidamortem, then run west to the rowboat.

During the quest, the player should have unlocked the shortcut from the temple grounds to the ritual site; this will save a significant amount of time. If the shortcut is not accessible after the quest, the player must unlock it by running the long way to the ritual site and unlocking by using the shortcut at the other end.

Note: All routes will require player to traverse the Stranglewood, and players will be running past several Strangled and a Strangled Boar while reaching the boss, even with the shortcut unlocked. The strangled will deal 1-3 damage, while the boar can deal 2-4 damage if they attack the player. Make sure to click on…
Vardorvis.requirements: • Completion of Quest Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire
Vardorvis.intro:
Carnifex Maximus Vardorvis was a Ghrazi vampyre whose corpse is found in the Stranglewood Ritual Site, animated by the Strangler parasite. A high-ranking member of the Zarosian Empire, Vardorvis succumbed to the Strangler and has remained under its control ever since, where the player encounters it during Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire. A stronger variant of him can be fought again after the completion of the quest.

An ancient tablet by the rocks leading to the Ritual Site shows statistics related to Vardorvis.
Vardorvis.strategy:
