After the completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire, players can fight a stronger variant of Vardorvis. An even stronger awakened variant can be fought by climbing the rocks with an awakener's orb in the player's inventory and selecting "Yes" when prompted.

If the player dies while fighting Vardorvis, their grave will appear by the rocks leading to the Stranglewood Ritual Site. Players will have their reclamation fee reduced by 75% until they have five kills, after which the standard death cost will apply. Note: If you have an active gravestone prior to dying at Vardorvis, the full death cost applies without reduction.

Fight overview:
Vardorvis has 700 hitpoints. He has an Attack level of 280 and attack bonus of +190, meaning he is very accurate regardless of the armour players use. He starts off with a Strength level of 270 and Defence level of 215. He is weakest to slashing attacks, with +65 slash, +85 crush and +215 stab defence bonus. Vardorvis is highly resistant to ranged and magic, with a Magic level of 215, +580 magic and ranged defence. Vardorvis only attacks with melee, but he is able to chase after players with routefinding. If Vardorvis is somehow unable to reach his target, he may either dart to them to catch up (without creating cracks in the ground) or may instead launch a crack under the player which can be avoided.

The melee attack has a max hit of 32, but will increase to 43 when his health is critically low. Both his normal and special attacks will also heal him for 50% of the damage inflicted, rounded down. Using Protect from Melee will reduce the potency of his auto-attacks by 75%, turning his max hit to 8-10.

Vardorvis, much like Duke Sucellus and The Whisperer, is not aggressive if fighting him after the quest, and the fight only begins when he is attacked. Once attacked, tendrils will burst from the ground and surround the arena. If the player did not bring a teleport, the tendrils can be used to quickly escape the arena, as the rock will have its options disabled. These tendrils will disappear after Vardorvis is killed, and the rock can be used once again to leave. Unlike the other bosses who use their special attacks at predictable intervals, Vardorvis uses them at random. This can be problematic during the enrage phase; learners are likely to be killed due to the large number of overlapping threats to manage.

Vardorvis has a unique mechanic in which his Strength and Defence levels scale linearly with his remaining hitpoints; as his health falls, his Defence level will lower, making him easier to hit, but his Strength level will increase, increasing his max hit. Due to this, defence-draining weapons are useless (zero Defence reduction), and players should opt for damage or sustain-type special weapons.

Upon reaching 33% of his health (~231 health), Vardorvis will enter an enrage phase after his next non-enraged attack. Similarly to Duke Sucellus, there is no visual indicator when enrage starts. During the enrage phase, Vardorvis' axes will appear more frequently, with a new set of axes appearing after the previous set have been thrown off the arena. The head will also appear at a more frequent rate, which when combined with spikes can deal a lot of damage or even kill the player if they are not prepared for it. If there is a lull in the axes, then the strangle mechanic is coming up, which can give players a brief moment of respite.

Equipment:
Vardorvis is weakest to slash attacks, followed by crush. The difference between the two is significant enough that crush is not recommended, however. Despite being an undead vampyre, Vardorvis is not susceptible to the effects of silver weaponry, Crumble Undead, or the Salve amulet.

The soulreaper axe is the best weapon to use against Vardorvis, as his 2x2 size and high defence inhibits the scythe of Vitur. Alternatively, the noxious halberd or blade of Saeldor work well, and lower tier slash weapons are also viable. However, due to Vardorvis healing on damage dealt to the player and having high defence, several equipment downgrades can compound and make the fight significantly longer.

Oathplate armour is extremely effective against Vardorvis due to its high slash defence and additional slash accuracy. Alternatively, a full set of justiciar armour can be used, which prevents Vardorvis from healing as often at the cost of lower melee strength. Echo boots can be used to provide defence and reflect damage; a ring of suffering serves the same purpose, but the DPS loss from not using an offensive ring is much greater. An amulet of blood fury can also provide longer trips, but the high upkeep cost and lower damage compared to the amulet of rancour can make it less desirable. The ancient godsword can instead be used to provide additional sustain if desired due to its guaranteed heal.

Players should be on the Arceuus spellbook to utilise thralls and Death Charge. Burning claws, dragon claws, and Voidwaker are all also effective options against Vardorvis in particular, with lower tier special attack weapons providing much less utility. If a player is confident in their ability to defeat the enrage phase, it is better to use these special attacks early in the fight due to their high accuracy. Otherwise, they are very useful at quickly ending the chaotic enrage phase towards the end of the kill.

In Awakened mode, an amulet of rancour is strongly recommended, as the player will generally be overhealing constantly to avoid dying to mistakes and as such rarely be capable of receiving the blood fury's healing effect.

When learning the Vardorvis fight, players are recommended to maximize slash defence. This can include opting to use a weaker 1-handed weapon (such as an abyssal tentacle) and a defender over stronger 2-handed weapons which provide little to no defence bonuses.

All weapons that have a Slashing combat style should be set to it, including Burning Claws if they are the special attack weapon u

Venenatis is a large spider that resides in the Silk Chasm, at level 35 Wilderness.

According to Phabelle Bile, Venenatis is the last of her kind, who were hunted to extinction by dwarves.

A dwarf multicannon cannot be set up in the Silk Chasm; if attempted, you will receive the message:

Venenatis.strategy:
• Venenatis resides in a multi-way area in moderately high-level Wilderness. You may be attacked at any time during the fight, and this is always a possibility in any deep wilderness multicombat area. Do not bring any items that you are not willing to lose. Items like the Dragon defender become broken if not protected on death.

Venenatis is a level 464 spider boss that is found in the Silk Chasm. Completion of the medium Wilderness Diary is required to fight Venenatis. Spindel is the level 302 lesser variant of Venenatis found in the Web Chasm, requiring the hard Wilderness Diary to access, but otherwise her mechanics are identical. Being on a Venenatis slayer task bypasses the diary requirement for both bosses.

Overview:

Venenatis can attack with all three forms of combat. While she will only use one combat style at a time, players in melee distance will instead only be attacked by melee. Like Vet'ion, she is weakest to crush.

She will begin the fight using 8 range attacks, followed by 8 magic attacks, all while moving position every 4 attacks. She will spawn spiderlings on the 1st range attack in cycle, and deploy her web attack on the 3rd mage attack in the cycle. This pattern will repeat until Venenatis is defeated.

All players who enter the arena will appear to the north, so it is recommended to hang south as much as possible to escape player killers, as she is no longer under level 30 Wilderness following the Wilderness boss rework. This does not apply to the weaker variant of the boss, Spindel, as her lair is still below level 30 Wilderness and can be teleported out of directly.

Players should avoid the webs at all costs, as their ability to drain run energy will prevent them from escaping from player killers.

The web can be positioned safely by standing on the outskirt of the arena on the 3rd magic attack to help prevent accidentally walking into the web.

The spiderlings should be killed as soon as they spawn to prevent them from empowering her too much; fortunately, they only have 5 health and can be killed in one hit by any combat style.

• Darts or Throwing knives can quickly eliminate individual spiderlings.
• Any tier of Chinchompa can eliminate multiple spiderlings with a well-placed shot (Ensure PK Skull prevention is activated).
• Players with 70+ Magic and Ancient Magicks can use a burst spell with Blighted ancient ice sacks to eliminate multiple spiderlings at once.

For Venenatis, her location in deep wild in multicombat should warrant extra precautions. Bring defensive armour, especially against magic attacks from other players, as even with a scout and perfect reactions you can be caught inside the cave. Reduce risk accordingly.

For Spindel, her location below 30 wilderness means escaping other players is much easier. However, players may bring more powerful equipment that can deal more damage. Spindel also has a lower defence level compared to Venenatis, so your equipment and setup can focus more on strength bonus and longevity.

The Twisted bow and Bow of Faerdhinen are also both strong alternatives to some melee setups, although are generally not advised due the significant risk of being smited in multi-combat and from Venenatis' webs. Vet'ion.intro:
Vet'ion (pronounced ) is a Zamorakian skeletal champion that resides in Vet'ion's Rest, at level 35 Wilderness. Like other bosses in the Wilderness, he can also drop the dragon pickaxe.

Vet'ion has two forms: the (purple) regular form and the (orange) enraged form. After he is defeated in his first form, he will go to his second form, which has a faster attack speed and stronger max hit. After changing forms he will reset any stat reductions applied in the first form. If he is not killed within five minutes in his second form, he will revert to his first form with the same Hitpoints. If he reverts after his hellhounds have been killed, the player(s) will not have to kill them a second time.

According to Andros Mai and as evidenced by the Desecrated Tomb, Vet'ion's power comes from his resting place.

Ironmen are eligible for drops from Vet'ion when defeating it alongside other players.

In order to enter Vet'ion's lair, the player must have completed the medium Wilderness Diary tasks, OR they must have a Vet'ion boss Slayer task (a skeleton Slayer task does not bypass the diary requirement).
Vet'ion.strategy:
• Vet'ion resides in a multi-way area in moderately high-level Wilderness. Completion of the medium Wilderness Diary is required to fight Vet'ion.

You may be attacked at any time during the fight, and death is all but guaranteed in any deep wilderness multicombat area. Do not bring any items that you are not willing to lose. Some untradeable items like the Dragon defender will become broken or mangled, requiring you to pay to repair them if they are not protected on death or protected with a trouver parchment.

Strategies:
While Vet'ion's stats were not changed following the 25 January 2023 rework, Vet'ion has the highest defensive capabilities of the three bosses. However, his negative crush defence of -10 makes him fairly easy to hit.

Since all of Vet'ion's attacks are AoE it is possible to avoid all damage from his attacks - meaning it is possible to logout or hop worlds during the fight to avoid player killers if you haven't taken any damage 10 seconds prior. This will eject the player outside his arena into the Escape Caves. The shield bash is the only major concern due to its larger AoE, but is still otherwise easy to dodge as the attack is signalled by a slight delay from his regular attacks.

When Vet'ion reaches 50% of his health in either form he will summon Skeletal Hellhounds during his first and Greater Skeletal Hellhounds in his second phase to assist him in battle. The hellhounds will channel immunity to Vet'ion until they are killed. While they deal powerful melee hits, they are not durable, with both the normal and greater versions only having 30 health. Vet'ion will gain 90% damage resistance after falling below half health, so it is not possible to skip the hellhounds.

Upon reaching 0 health in his standard form, he will charge up lightning around him as he yells that the player has to defeat him a second time. This can be avoided by being far enough from him or standing under him in his middle tiles. Vet'ion will restore his health to full, restore any drained stats, increase his max hit and attack speed from a 6 tick cycle to 5 ticks.

As Vet'ion will move towards a player between his attacks, the player can draw him towards the exit to his arena and keep him there for the majority of the time. This is fairly easy to set up in small teams and for solo players and enables a faster escape, as getting frozen in the middle of the room will likely result in death from both player killers and Vet'ion's attacks.

Unlike his lesser counterpart Calvar'ion, Vet'ion resides in a Multicombat area and in level 35 Wilderness, so teleports cannot be used to directly escape player killers. The only chance a player has to escape is by running out the exit, which will take them into the Escape Caves where they must navigate their way to an exit. The Escape Caves are full of aggressive monsters, such as Grizzly bears and poison spiders, so antipoison is recommended. It is recommended to leave a "scout" outside, giving the player an early warning and can sometimes cause other players to ignore whoever is inside.

In the event you are targeted by player killers and are leaving via the escape caves, the fastest exit to level 30 Wilderness for a teleport is the southern exit from the caves. However, the north-eastern exit is preferrable for players confident in their ability to tank a single PKer to level 30 wilderness or for the duration of a Tele Block, as teams may wait at the southern entrance to attack players.

Equipment:
Always keep risk to a minimum in the Wilderness! - Whenever gearing, check your Items Kept on Death and enable "Wilderness beyond level 20" to make sure important items will not be lost.

The most effective equipment to fight Vet'ion involves a large amount of risk by using items that can be protected with Trouver parchments, but most players should opt for cheaper setups until they are confident in their ability to handle PKers. The Ursine chainmace is by far the most effective weapon against Vet'ion, but comes with additional risk as it must be charged with Revenant ether. Players should choose three (or four, with Protect item if you are confident you can mitigate the risk of being Smited) valuable with the most strength bonus possible compared to cheaper alternatives.

Note: The benefit from Salve amulet (e) does not stack with a Slayer helmet. As Salve amulets are free and kept on death below Level 20 Wilderness they should always be prioritised.

Vorkath.intro:
Vorkath (roughly translated as pathetic failure/weakling/runt in the dragonkin's language) is a draconic boss-monster first encountered during the Dragon Slayer II quest as the penultimate boss. Created by Zorgoth during the Fourth Age's Dragonkin Conflicts, the blue dragon is one of his subjects that has survived his experiments in the laboratory beneath the dragonkin fortress on Ungael. Despite its phenomenal strength, Zorgoth abandoned Vorkath due to its lack of aggression, leaving it as a 'distraction' for any humans that would stumble onto the island.

Vorkath is considered a blue dragon and zombie for the purpose of a Slayer task. As Vorkath is also undead, the Salve amulet and its variants will work on him. However, it does not stack with the Slayer helmet. Vorkath is also immune to recoil damage.

After completing Dragon Slayer II, players may fight Vorkath again, with increased stats and rewards.
Vorkath.strategy:
After completion of Dragon Slayer II, a stronger variant of Vorkath can be fought again. To get to Vorkath, talk to Torfinn, located in Rellekka on the 3rd dock to the right. This brings you to Ungael at the entrance of Vorkath. Fight Preparation: It's recommended to turn off run during this fight. It's neccesary to walk during the acid special, and manually turning off run as the attack starts adds complexity and room for error. This leaves one less tick to dodge the bomb standard attack, though this can be mitigated by ctrl-click (which overrides the run setting for that movement). The optimal protection prayer depends on the player's gear: • Protect from Magic if using melee or fighting Vorkath without a dragonfire protection shield (such as with the toxic blowpipe). • Protect from Missiles if using a crossbow with a dragonfire ward, dragonfire shield or anti-dragon shield. Have quick prayers configured to your protection prayer and stat boosting prayer, as Vorkath has an attack that switches off prayer. The Standard spellbook must be used to cast Crumble Undead for one of Vorkath's specials. It's strongly recommended to bring a magic staff that can auto-cast Crumble Undead (such as the slayer's staff), which is much easier than manually casting the spell under time pressure. Bring anti-venom protection, as Vorkath envenoms player with its venom dragonfire. Fight Overview: • Vorkath has multiple attacks that can quickly kill the player if not addressed promptly — the acid barrage, the zombified spawn, and especially the vertical dragonfire bomb. Pay attention to the fight. Vorkath's attack pattern consists of six random standard attacks, one special attack, another six standard attacks, then the other special attack, and so on until defeated. Equipment: Ranged=

: The base salve amulet and salve amulet (e) do not provide bonuses to Ranged. The amulet must be imbued to provide Ranged bonuses; make sure your salve amulet has a blue gem and has an (i) or (ei) in its name. Ascension crossbows are the most effective ranged weapons against Vorkath, followed by the dragon hunter crossbow. The toxic blowpipe is the premier budget option. Elite Void Knight equipment and masori armour are similar at 95+ Ranged. Masori is best-in-slot with ascension crossbows or a toxic blowpipe. Elite Void outcompetes Masori with the more accurate 5-tick crossbows, though it becomes worse at lower Ranged levels as base accuracy decreases. With 5-tick crossbows, ruby dragon bolts (e) or ruby bolts (e) are the most effective ammunition until Vorkath reaches ~250 HP (33% hitpoints), at which point it's best to swap to diamond dragon bolts (e) or diamond bolts (e) (weaker setups can switch bolts at slightly lower HP). Rings of recoil, Vengeance, and thralls do not inflict damage on Vorkath. As such, any spellbook swap setups are not particually useful. With 99 Ranged and a high Defence level, players should expect anywhere from 3-6 kills with crossbows. A reagent pouch can be used to store crushed superior dragon bones and extend trips. |-| Melee= The dragon hunter lance is the most effective melee weapon to use against Vorkath. The lance's passive effect damage and accuracy boosts stack with the salve amulet(ei), so it scales incredibly well with high-tier armour and jewellery. With worse equipment, the Osmumten's fang is sometimes a superior option. Players use Protect from Magic and wear the best melee armour possible to maximise their ranged defence. Players should stay in melee range when not dealing with specials, as despite taking the occasional melee, being out of melee range increases the rate of ranged attacks and results in more damage taken overall. If your gear has -64 magic attack bonus or lower, your Crumble Undead will not hit.

Below Bandos equipment, prioritise defensive bonuses over strength bonus if you find your trips cut short by Vorkath's normal melee and ranged attacks. With regard to profit, consistently higher kills per trip are more valuable than marginal damage gains. Additionally, if sacrificing defensive bonuses for melee strength in a given slot, ensure that you are actually gaining a max hit (check with the DPS Calculator) and that you are not reducing your kills per trip. For example, depending on your other equips and Strength level, it is possible that the +2 melee strength bonus of Bandos tassets does not improve your max hit and instead increases the likelihood that your trips are cut short compared to using Justiciar legguards, which has higher melee and ranged defences. Inventory setups: In all setups, chaos runes must be brought in order to cast Crumble Undead, along with dust runes (or air and earth runes). A rune pouch (or its divine variant) can be used to significantly reduce the number of inventory slots needed. As air and earth runes will already be brought, law runes can be brought to cast Teleport to House as a cheap teleport option. Fire and nature runes can also be brought to cast High Level Alchemy on Vorkath's valuable drops, but will take up additional inventory space. With a divine rune pouch, nature runes can be brought without taking up an extra inventory space, and a low quantity of fire runes (20-30) can be brought outside of it, with leftovers being dropped at the site to free up the space for more loot. Much of the value of Vorkath's drops is in its guaranteed drop of superior dragon bones. To save space in your inventory you can bring the Heavy bonesack if you have completed Rag and Bone Man III. For players without said quest completed, a pestle and mortar and reagent pouch can be brought to convert the bones to crushed superior dragon bones, which can be stored in the pouch. Be aware that crushed bones will not sell as quickly as the original version, but the profit loss overall will not be significant. Whisperer.requirements: • Completion of Quest Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire
Whisperer.intro: The Whisperer is a siren found in the sunken cathedral of the Lassar Undercity, who is encountered during Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire. A high-ranking assassin in the Zarosian Empire whose real name was classified, the Whisperer succumbed to the darkness of the blackstone and was transformed into her current state. A stronger variant of her can be fought again after the completion of the quest.
Whisperer.strategy:
After the completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire, players can fight a stronger variant of the Whisperer than the one fought during the quest. An even stronger, awakened variant can be fought by disturbing the Odd Figure with an awakener's orb in the player's inventory and selecting "Yes" when prompted in a fresh instance - having obtained an orb in the instance will not cause the prompt to appear.

If the player dies while fighting the Whisperer, their grave will appear in the Ruins of Camdozaal, by the rope leading to the Lassar Undercity. Players will have their reclamation fee reduced by 75% until they have five kills, after which the standard death cost will apply.

Fight overview:
The player must bring the blackstone fragment to initiate the fight, as parts of the fight will require the player to enter the Shadow Realm. The player will refuse to fight the Whisperer without it.

The sanity mechanic is present throughout the fight. When outside the Shadow Realm, the player will slowly restore 1% sanity every 4 ticks; inside, the player will lose 3% sanity along with 3 prayer points. Sanity can be further decreased (regardless of realm) by tentacle hits or by unavoided special attacks. If the sanity bar fully depletes, the player will go insane and will quickly die within 10 ticks; teleport out if this occurs.

The fight begins by disturbing the Odd Figure, who will then knock the player back and begin attacking as the Whisperer.

The Whisperer's regular attack involves shooting three projectiles per attack in either Ranged or Magic. The ranged attacks consist of grey barbs, while the magic attacks consist of a cluster of three blue orbs; the Whisperer's chest will additionally emit a blue aura. Protection prayers fully block the projectiles' damage if activated before the projectile hits the player; if not blocked, they can deal up to 40 and 36 damage respectively. The pattern of these projectiles changes depending on how far into the fight the player is.
• Upon beginning the fight, she will only use Magic (M) or Ranged (R) for all three projectiles.
• After one or two special attacks have been used, she will use M-M-R or R-R-M.
• After all three special attacks have been used, she will use M-R-M or R-M-R.
• During her enrage phase, she will start with ranged, and switch styles every two attacks.

After each regular attack, four shadow tentacles will surface four tiles from the player, converging on the tile they were on when they first appeared. If the player is struck by a tentacle, they will deal 20 damage and drain sanity by 20% (only one tentacle can hit the player at a time). These initially converge in an "X" formation, and a "+" formation can be used after two special attacks. Both formations can be dodged by performing an L movement (two tiles forward/backward, then one tile left/right - analogous to a knight move in chess).

The tentacles will only spawn on a valid empty tile; if they would spawn on the arena edge, or if the Whisperer herself is on top of the tile, they will not spawn on that tile. This can be manipulated into creating safe tiles.

The Whisperer will melee the player if they stand next to her, dealing two heavy hits in two ticks. This melee attack hits through prayer, always hits and has the second hit mirror the first (e.g if the first hit deals 40 damage, the second also deals 40). The Whisperer actively checks if the player is in melee distance; if the player runs into melee distance in the middle of a volley, she will immediately cancel it for a melee attack, which is extremely dangerous. Players should stay at least five tiles away from the Whisperer to avoid misclicks and accidentally wandering into melee range.

Perfect kills are disqualified on a tentacle hit or on damage from a projectile (the player is still eligible if the projectile misses off prayer).

Enrage phase:

Upon reaching 0 health, the Whisperer will heal 140 hitpoints, restore any drained stats, and pull the player into the Shadow Realm. She will alternate between ranged and magic every two attacks and increase her attack speed to 2 ticks (1.2 seconds). A single tentacle is launched alongside every attack, rather than a cluster of four.

Players should restore their health and prayer before triggering her enrage phase, as it's difficult to heal during the phase itself.

The tentacles still drain sanity and are a serious threat, so the focus should always be on movement. There are two general movement strategies:

• Basic movement (recommended for beginners). Players can dodge most of the tentacles just by running in a straight line; even running directly into a tentacle usually won't cause damage as long as the player is moving. To take advantage of this, run in a large square around the Whisperer (stay out of melee range) or back-and-forth in a line in front of her, taking care not to stop for more than a few ticks. When the second auto-attack of the same style (ranged or magic) is just about to hit the player, click to move and then switch prayers. Fit in your own attacks where possible, then immediately keep moving. Do not panic if you're hit, simply click a a good distance away and ensure your prayers are correct.
• Advanced movement. Utilises L-movement to dodge all tentacle attacks. See the video to the right for an example.

Once the Whisperer dies, the player's sanity is instantly restored to 100% and any attacks launched in transition will not cause damage. She will respawn as the Odd Figure in roughly 18 seconds.

Tips for mobile:
The sanity interface, chat menu, and world map all take up extremely valuable space on the screen, and this can especially be a problem during the enrage phase. Long tap the world map icon to collapse the world map before the fight begins, and collapse the chat menu after the Whisperer’s specials to help you focus more on the direction of the tentacles during enrage.

Magic is the most effective way to defeat the Whisperer,

Zulrah.intro:
Zulrah is a level 725 solo-only snake boss. Before the player can fight Zulrah, players must have completed Regicide to the point of reaching Port Tyras, as well as having spoken with High Priestess Zul-Harcinqa to offer themselves as the sacrifice in place of the gnome child, as Zul-Gwenwynig will prevent the player from boarding the boat until Zul-Harcinqa allows them to be the sacrifice.

Killing Zulrah is a required task for the hard Western Provinces Achievement Diary, which in turn is a requirement for upgrading to the Elite Void set.
Zulrah.strategy:
Zulrah is a level 725 solo-only snake boss found at a shrine east of Zul-Andra, accessible by boat. Zulrah's shrine can be exited through victory, death, logout/hopping worlds, or teleportation.

Equipment:

Magic=
Magic can be used on all phases, but performs much worse than even simple ranged switches for the tanzanite phase. Zulrah possesses a 50% elemental weakness to fire spells, but the Standard spellbook loses out on additional damage and utility of thralls or Vengeance, so it usually is less effective at higher levels.

|-|
Ranged=
The Twisted bow and Bow of Faerdhinen are both powerful enough to be used on all 3 phases to reduce switches, if desired. Otherwise, ranged is primarily used on the Tanzanite phase in addition to magic. If hybriding, ranged helmet and boot switches provide fairly minimal dps increases while also having negative magic accuracy. Consider swapping them for supplies instead.

|-|
Melee=
The Noxious halberd is powerful enough to be used on all 3 phases to great effect. The Crystal halberd special attack is very effective during the last hit of each phase, as the double hitsplats get around the 50 damage cap on Zulrah. Attacking primarily with the crystal halberd is possible, but significantly less effective than simply using other styles, due to its slow attack speed. A small Ranged switch is recommended to bring as some phases cannot be attacked with melee due to poison clouds obstructing the area, and to fit in extra hits with a faster weapon. The Eclipse atlatl is best suited to this, as it scales very well from the already worn melee gear, although other options from the ranged gear tab can work in its place with one or two additional switches.
Note: No other halberd besides the Noxious halberd (and the Crystal halberd for the special attack) is worth using to melee Zulrah due to the slow 7 tick attack speed of other halberds. If other styles are particularly poor for your available gear, the crystal halberd can still be worth using however.

|-|
Magic (Diary kill) =
Due to Zulrah's elemental weakness to fire spells, they perform particularly well against Zulrah, especially at a lower magic level when powered staves are less effective.

With slower kill times, it may be beneficial to hide behind a pillar for Zulrah's tanzanite phase to maximise damage output and minimise damage taken.

Alchemical Hydra.intro:
The Alchemical Hydra is a boss version of hydra, found in the lower level of the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon in Mount Karuulm, requiring level 95 Slayer to kill. The Alchemical Hydra was the creation of a Dragonkin named Karuulm. While Karuulm saw promise in his creation, he nevertheless saw it as a failure because he could not replicate its traits, and abandoned it along with his other creations: the Wyrms, Drakes, and Hydras.

Unlike normal hydras, the Alchemical Hydra can only be killed while on a hydra Slayer task, which are only assigned by Konar quo Maten and Mortimer. Likewise, it can be assigned for boss slayer, but only by Konar.

In addition, as it is found within the volcano, players who have not completed the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary must wear boots of stone, boots of brimstone, or granite boots to protect themselves from the extreme heat of the dungeon floor. This also applies to attempting to use the Item Retrieval Service, where the rapid damage will interrupt actions and dying a second time will wipe the storage.

Along with all the unique drops obtainable from hydras, it can also drop hydra leather, which is used on the machinery south-west of the pool in the Lithkren Vault to create ferocious gloves, as well as the hydra claw, which is combined with a Zamorakian hasta to create the dragon hunter lance.
Alchemical Hydra.strategy:
The Alchemical Hydra is a level 95 Slayer boss encountered in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. In order to fight it, players must be assigned a Hydra task.

To reach the boss, players must run north past the Tasakaal, then east past the Hydras. They will then reach the entrance to the lair by Orrvor quo Maten. Alternatively, players with level 88 Agility can reach it safely by using the mysterious pipe just behind Kaal-Ket-Jor.

Fight overview:
The fight is instanced; if players die while fighting the Hydra, then they may reclaim their items from Orrvor quo Maten outside for 100,000 coins each time. Dying elsewhere with items still held by him will result in them being lost forever.

While the Hydra is in the room, players cannot leave through the doors, as they are jammed when this occurs. Teleports will still work, however. The Hydra has a respawn time of 20 seconds.

The Hydra has four phases, each one beginning upon each 25% health threshold (~275 health). A head will fall off each time this occurs, as the Hydra roars and changes colour. At the start of each phase, the Hydra will perform three auto-attacks before performing a special attack.

The Hydra attacks with both Magic and Ranged. The Hydra will begin the fight with either combat style. For the first three phases, after every three basic attacks, the Hydra will sway its heads backwards as an indicator that it is changing combat styles.

During the first three phases, the Hydra reduces incoming damage by 75% until it is lured over and sprayed by the appropriate chemical vent. The Hydra will when hit by the correct vent. If Hydra is sprayed by an incorrect vent, the damage of its attacks increase, although protection prayers continue to block all damage regardless.

In the final phase, the Hydra attacks alternately with Magic and Ranged, choosing to start with the opposite of what it attacked with last. On the fourth attack, the Hydra instead throws poison splatters as in the first phase.

Equipment:
The Alchemical Hydra has a Defence level of 100. It is weakest to ranged attacks, possessing +45 global ranged resistance.

As it is considered draconic, Dragonbane weapons are effective against it. If using melee, use a dragon hunter lance on stab. The Hydra's stab defence is slightly higher than its ranged but still provides acceptable accuracy due to its lower Defence level. Magic is not recommended due to its Magic level of 260.

Ranged=

Prayer bonus is prioritised over ranged accuracy because of the boss's relatively low defensive stats and the minimal damage taken when dealing with the mechanics correctly. Alternatively, players may use gear that maximises ranged accuracy if they are confident with prayer flicking, as it greatly reduces the need for prayer potions. With sufficient experience, barely any damage should be taken most kills; the only unavoidable damage players may take is the first hit at the start of kill, and self-inflicted damage from Divine potions or the special attack of Ruby bolts (e).

Maggot King.transport:
Use Drakan's medallion to get to Castle Drakan, enter Vampyrium, and then run east. Before fighting the boss, players should unlock a quick-travel method by rescuing an aranei scout south-east of Sangvesti.

This scout will initially be attacked by sanguidae; kill all three of them, then talk to the scout again, who will then be found south of the bank chest by the map icon and will take players just east of Sangvesti. Two agility shortcuts can be used to traverse the woods more quickly, both requiring level 64 Agility; It is recommended to only use the shortcut furthest away from the scout, as the closer shortcut is a longer path to the boss and the player is likely to be attacked by an Ancient feral vyre.

Lastly, to use the bank chest, it must first be built with level 70 Construction (boosts can be used) using a hammer and saw, 1 magic stone, 2 cupronickel bars, 2 adamantite bars, and 4 ironwood planks. If the player is not using this chest to bank, they may rebank at their desired location, then utilise a shortcut south of Safalaan to quickly reach the scout.

Regardless, both routes will usually result in the player running into the nearby dire bat which is the only nuisance on the way to the scout.

Maggot King.intro:
The Maggot King is a boss in Vampyrium that requires completion of The Blood Moon Rises to kill. The entrance to its lair can be found in the forest east of Sangvesti, near the Ruined Village.

Players may only fight the boss by themselves, and the fight takes place inside an instance. Additionally, a mix of melee and either magic or ranged is required to fight the Maggot King, as it cannot be attacked with melee until it falls below ~980 hitpoints (65%).

The Maggot King is the most mature and strongest form of the ur-maggot, a parasitic entity that kills its host and later possesses its body. This ur-maggot seems to have killed and then taken over the body of a powerful venator.

A scoreboard can be found outside of the entrance leading into the boss area, recording the player's and global records against the boss.
Maggot King.strategy:
After completion of The Blood Moon Rises, players can fight the Maggot King in its lair, in which the entrance is accessed via some darkwood trees in the forest between Sangvesti and the Ruined Village.

If the player dies while fighting the Maggot King, they will respawn in Vampyrium by the portal back to Gielinor, with their grave appearing outside of the boss lair entrance. Players will have their reclamation fee reduced by 75% until they have five kills, after which the standard death cost will apply.

Should players not wish to make the trek from the portal to the boss lair, the aranei scout near the portal can be paid with one of three items to move the gravestone near them:

Fight overview:
The Maggot King is initially fought at a distance, requiring players to attack with either ranged or magic attacks from their side of the arena; heavy ranged attacks and fire spells work best, with fire spells dealing an additional (stacking) 5 burn damage to the boss and reducing its magic defence by 20 per burn stack.

The Maggot King's basic attacks cover all three combat styles. Both the magic and ranged attacks can deal up to 46 damage, and are fully blocked by prayer. The melee attack is slightly stronger, dealing up to 55 damage, and prayer does not fully protect against these attacks, instead reducing them by ~40%.
• Ranged - Green spit is launched at the player, leaving poisonous bile behind on the tile the player stood on when the attack lands, as well as on two adjacent tiles. The attack will also poison the player starting at 8 damage.
• Standing on the poisonous bile will deal minor damage, as well as drain poison immunity by 45 seconds. It will remain there until it is covered over with carrion or when stepped on.
• Using both the serpentine helm and anti-venom+ will provide immunity to poisonous bile.
• Magic - Yellow spit is launched at the player, leaving sticky bile behind on the tile the player stood on when the attack lands, as well as on two adjacent tiles.
• Standing on the sticky bile will deal minor damage, drain Attack, Strength, or Defence, and delay the player's next attack by one tick (0.6s). The amount drained is based on the damage dealt by the bile. It will remain there until it is covered over with carrion or when stepped on.
• An inoculation bracelet will provide immunity to sticky bile.
• Melee - The Maggot King walks up close and slams its head in a 3x4 Area-of-Effect.

Equipment:
The Maggot King is weakest to crush and heavy ranged attacks. Although it possesses a relatively high Magic level and defence (200 Magic and +150 magic defence), it also possesses an 80% susceptibility to fire spells, which can be feasible for maging players utilising a harmonised Nightmare staff, tome of fire and confliction gauntlets. Furthermore, successful attacks with fire spells deal an additional (stacking) 5 burn damage to the boss. It is recommended to use fire spells with either the harmonised Nightmare staff or the twinflame staff, as not only does the boss's magic defence get reduced by 20 per burn stack, but failed casts will also benefit from confliction gauntlets, whereas Tumeken's shadow gains none of these benefits. The harmonised nightmare and twinflame staffs also output fire hits at a higher rate than standard autocast staffs such as the Purging staff, ensuring the boss gets to full burn stacks more quickly and stays there more reliably.

Perfect kills will require minimal sustain, as the boss deals very little chip damage when walking onto acid/bile pools and being hit by small carrion bits. While not necessary, an amulet of blood fury switch can also be used to heal off of any damage taken during the fight. The boss frequently drops a dull ancient medal and 2-4 stymphike tartares, which help restore prayer, has a 3/7 chance to provide combat stats and heal a good amount of health, which often adds an extra kill into trips.

Magic=

Fire spells are especially powerful, causing both a damage-over-time effect and lowering the boss's magic defence. A harmonised Nightmare staff casting fire surge with a fragment of burning fire, tome of fire and searing pages will significantly outperform the Tumeken's shadow, despite lacking access to thralls and Death Charge. Magic special attacks should generally be performed when the boss has 5 burn stacks, to increase their chance of hitting.

|-|
Ranged=

Heavy ranged weapons are a very competitive alternative to magic, with a cheaper resource cost due to requiring bolts instead of runes. The potential damage output of ascension crossbows is surpassed only by harmonised Nightmare staff, but you will need to time your movement correctly to take advantage of their increased attack speed. Some players may find it simpler to continuously "blowpipe walk" (alternating between moving 1-2 tiles and attacking each tick), rather than time their dodges correctly in response to the Maggot King attacks. Ascension crossbows will be much less effective if you delay your attacks every time the Maggot King spits.

Other crossbows will usually result in longer kills and shorter trips, as damage leading up to the melee phase is heavily reliant on enchanted ruby bolts, which forces the player to keep health low to avoid as much self-damage as possible. A hunters' sunlight crossbow can serve as a budget option, as it is better than a twisted bow here with enough components of max range gear.

Additionally, a standard ranged weapon is required to deal with ur-maggots. Dizana's quiver allows bringing both ammo types without using extra switches or inventory slots but caution is advised if the player brings a melee cape switch, as failing to switch back to quiver can result in failing to fire. A charged bow such as a Bow of Faerdhinen, Crystal bow or Webweaver bow is a good way to get around this problem while also providing a nine to ten tile range to hit larvae. A venator bow is another option for killing larvae as the shots can bounce to the boss f

Shellbane Gryphon.intro:
The shellbane gryphon is the boss version of gryphons found in a cave in the centre of the Great Conch, requiring level 51 Slayer and completion of Troubled Tortugans to kill. As a Slayer boss, it may only be killed while on a gryphons Slayer task. Gryphons can be assigned as a slayer task by Vannaka, Chaeldar and Mortimer. Additionally, Nieve/Steve or Duradel/Kuradal can assign them if the player purchases the 'Wings Spread' reward from a Slayer master for 80 Slayer Points, though this unlock is not required for the shellbane gryphon to be assigned as a boss task from those Slayer masters. Konar quo Maten can also assign the shellbane gryphon specifically when she assigns a boss task.

A shellbane gryphon must also be fought and killed on the Little Pearl during the Troubled Tortugans quest. It does not drop anything when killed during the quest.

The shellbane gryphon can also be killed off-task only if the player has the elite clue step to kill the gryphon. Dropping the elite clue scroll while in the cave will delete the item. Combat Achievements can still be completed when killing the gryphon via this method, though not all are possible due to some requiring several kills without leaving the cave. The gryphon will also not drop anything if the clue is not in your inventory when it dies.

Elder Nama at the cave entrance enforces these rules, and also acts as a scoreboard for the boss, displaying the player's statistics for the fight as well as global statistics.

Shellbane Gryphon.strategy:
After completion of Troubled Tortugans, the Shellbane Gryphon can be fought again, but requires the player to be assigned a gryphon slayer task, or to have an elite clue directing them to kill the Shellbane Gryphon (in which case the player will be only be able to kill the boss once).

Fight overview:
Like normal gryphons, the shellbane gryphon is primarily weak to melee, but magic can also be effective due to its elemental weakness to wind spells; however, due to one of its special attacks, this is not entirely practical. Additionally, a tortugan shield is recommended for the encounter with the shellbane gryphon, otherwise the player will take heavy damage from gryphon's melee attacks even through Protect from Melee, and receive a game message stating Using Protect from Melee whilst having the tortugan shield equipped will fully negate all melee damage dealt.

The shellbane gryphon primarily attacks with melee, but also uses a ranged attack occasionally. It also has three special attacks:

• Knockback - The boss will throw the player backwards, dealing up to 30 unavoidable damage. Despite the audio from this attack, the player is not stunned and can immediately resume attacking. The knockback is countered by having the player's equipped weight be ≥40kg, which stuns the boss and momentarily gives the player a chance for their own counter attack. Having an equipped weight ≥ 40 kg also causes the boss to prioritise using its other two special attacks, though this special can still happen regardless of a player’s equipped weight.
• Negating the knockback by having an equipped weight ≥ 40 kg stuns the boss for . During this short window, the player can quickly click to attack the boss to knock it back one tile and grants player one additional attack free of attack delay. However, if the player does not click to attack the boss while it is stunned, they will be knocked back regardless of equipped weight, indicated by the game message
• Players may not be able to perform the knockback in time if their attack is delayed by eating food.
• Corrosive spit - An orange blob is launched, which corrodes the player's worn equipment if they do not move one tile away from where they stood. This causes a player to take 3-12 damage 6 times (18-72 damage total) over the course of 32 ticks (19.2s), which can be interrupted by quickly unequipping all of the player's items.

• Whirlwind - Whirlwinds begin to form at the player's current position, indicated by the game message
• The boss will form a whirlwind every 3 ticks (1.8s), up to a maximum of 5. If a whirlwind would have formed on top of an existing whirlwind, that whirlwind instead grows more powerful. 6 ticks (3.6s) after the last whirlwind forms, all whirlwinds will begin damaging every tick the player stands on them.
• 15 seconds after that, all summoned whirlwinds will burst and deal large amounts of damage, indicated by the game message As such, its recommended to move one tile every attack in order to avoid whirlwinds stacking and increasing their size, resulting in less damage received.
• When countering the knockback attack, players should be cautious on where they move to, as a whirlwind may inadvertently end up in range of damaging the player upon shoving the boss.

Melee=
Since the Shellbane Gryphon's knockback is effective against players with less than 40 kg of worn equipment, some of the best options do not necessarily provide the highest damage, but rather a balance between strength bonus and heavy weight.

A 40kg+ setup can be easily achieved with most melee armour coupled with both a tortugan and dragonfire shield, even when using a slayer helmet. If a black mask is used, its higher weight over the slayer helmet means that the player can slot in an avernic defender for better DPS. If not being used, the dragonfire shield is recommended to meet this requirement.

If using low-level gear, adamant armour may be preferred to rune as it is heavier.

Artio.intro:
Artio is a weaker variant of Callisto who is fought in the Hunter's End, a singles-plus combat area in level 21 Wilderness. To enter Artio's lair, players must have completed the hard Wilderness diary, OR they must have a Callisto boss Slayer task (a bear Slayer task does not bypass the diary requirement).

Compared to Callisto, the fight is safer and easier in return for lower drop quantities and rates. Artio's melee attack has a minimum hit of 15, which can only be partially blocked with Protect from Melee.

Killing Artio counts as a Callisto alternative for a slayer Boss task, the elite Wilderness diary task, and the combat achievements.

Upon any player entering the den, all players inside will be unable to teleport for 3 ticks. This delay no longer occurs after completion of the hard Wilderness diary.

If Artio is not already frozen, and the attacking player has equipment with a total Magic accuracy greater than 0, then the first attack that would freeze the boss (Entangle, Ice Barrage) is guaranteed to hit.
Artio.strategy:
Artio is a level 320 bear that can be found inside Hunter's End. She is killed for the valuable Voidwaker hilt, though she can also drop the claws of Callisto, tyrannical ring, Callisto cub, the dragon 2h sword and dragon pickaxe. The hard Wilderness diary is required to fight Artio.

• Artio resides in a singles-plus area and in mid-level Wilderness. You may be attacked at any time during the kill. Do not bring any items that you are not willing to lose.

Strategy:
Artio will spawn to the south of the den, right in front of the exit. If you wish to avoid player killers, it is recommended to place a secondary account waiting outside the entrance to scout potential threats. All players who enter the den will spawn to the north, similar to Callisto's lair.

Artio uses highly damaging melee attacks and is weakest to magic and ranged attacks. Ice spells will land often even with minimal magic gear, binding her temporarily. If she cannot attack with melee, she will begin using a much weaker ranged attack until she can reach her target. Artio will occasionally launch a white orb at her target, which should be protected against by switching on Protect from Magic or risk taking up to 50 damage from the attack.

Upon reaching 66% and 33% of her health, Artio will roar, launching bear traps all across the arena. Stepping on one will deal up to 15 damage and bind the player for a few seconds. The traps will linger around for a short duration before expiring, but will immediately be replaced with a fresh set of traps. While roaring, she will also glow red, breaking free of binds in the process and requiring a player to refreeze her.

Deranged Archaeologist.intro:
The Deranged archaeologist is a relatively simple boss that resides at the southern end of the Tar Swamp on Fossil Island. His special attack mechanic is similar to that of the Crazy archaeologist and the Chaos Fanatic.

The deranged archaeologist is notable for his unique steel ring drop, the best-in-slot melee defensive ring. Compared to his crazed counterpart, his common drops are slightly more valuable, though the steel ring is his only unique drop.

The deranged archaeologist may be killed as an alternative on a crazy archaeologist boss Slayer task, unless the Wilderness is specified as the task location when given by Krystilia or Konar quo Maten.

Spindel is a level 302 spider boss that is found in the Web Chasm. The fight with her is nearly identical to Venenatis, although with reduced stats and in a singles-plus combat area. Completion of the hard Wilderness diary is required to fight Spindel.

Overview:

Spindel can attack with all three forms of combat. While she will only use one combat style at a time, players in melee distance will instead only be attacked by melee. Like Calvar'ion, she is weakest to crush.

She will begin the fight using 8 ranged attacks, followed by 8 magic attacks, all while moving position every 4 attacks. She will spawn spiderlings on the 1st ranged attack in cycle, and deploy her web attack on the 3rd mage attack in the cycle. This pattern will repeat until Spindel is defeated.

Players who enter the arena will appear to the north, so always keep an eye out for PKers and teleport or run to the exit if needed.

Players should avoid the webs at all costs, as their ability to drain run energy will prevent them from escaping from player killers. The web can be positioned safely by standing on the outskirt of the arena on the 3rd magic attack to help prevent accidentally walking into the web.

The spiderlings should be killed as soon as they spawn to prevent them from empowering her too much; fortunately, they only have 5 health and can be killed in one hit by any combat style.

• Any tier of chinchompa can eliminate multiple spiderlings with a well-placed shot as well as damage Spindel's south-west tile, (Ensure PK Skull prevention is activated).
• Blisterwood stakes, darts, or throwing knives can quickly eliminate individual spiderlings. Blisterwood stakes have longer range than darts and knives, and can be reclaimed from a gravestone for free on PvP death due to being untradeable.
• Players with 70+ Magic and Ancient Magicks can use a burst spell with blighted ancient ice sacks to eliminate multiple spiderlings at once.

Equipment:
Spindel's location in the Wilderness should warrant extra precautions. Bring defensive armour, especially against magic attacks from other players, as even with a scout and perfect reactions you can be caught inside the cave. Reduce risk accordingly.

Spindel has a lower defence level compared to her stronger counterpart, Venenatis.
Melee=
The ursine chainmace is the strongest weapon against Spindel, costing . The four strongest items to bring are generally the chainmace, your strongest defender, the amulet of rancour, and your best strength ring (ultor ring or berserker ring (i)). A fourth valuable item should only be brought if you are confident in not getting Smited by player killers. Further upgrades are generally very expensive and add little additional damage for their risk and cost. Trouver parchments can be used on certain gear, such as an infernal cape or fighter torso, to gain additional strength bonus for additional risk of 500000+ each.

Inventory:

Inventory setup will vary greatly depending on your gear and team. When deciding what supplies to bring, keep in mind that Spindel frequently drops large quantities of un-noted blighted food or potions that replace supplies used during the fight. Make sure to have the following:
• Grey chinchompas, blisterwood stakes, darts/throwing knives, or blighted ancient ice sacks for killing the spiderlings quickly, ordered from fastest to slowest
• Looting bag
• Stamina potion
• (Divine) super combat potion
• Anti-venom/Sanfew serum(s) — cures/prevents venom from player killers.
• Blighted super restores
• Blighted manta ray or blighted anglerfish (if the player is 93 or higher hitpoints) for the rest, and multiple blighted karambwan
Optional:
• Phoenix necklace — emergency healing whilst tanking
• Saradomin brews — more expensive outlast healing, combo eating with hard food is invaluable
• Royal seed pod — if not bringing a charged amulet of glory or ring of wealth
• Games necklace or revenant cave teleport to reach the Web Chasm faster.
• Runes for thralls and/or Death Charge
• Death charge can be cast off cooldown with frequent spiderling spawns.
• Divine rune pouch locked with a trouver parchment — if using Arceeus spellbook, allows for more supplies.

|-|
Ranged=
Both the webweaver bow and Craw's bow offer very competitive damage against Spindel despite her higher ranged defences. Ranged also has the luxury of staying closer to the exit in case of player killers, although you will need to monitor and change your overhead prayers depending on the attack cycle. The twisted bow and bow of Faerdhinen are also both strong alternatives to some melee setups, but the former is generally not recommended due to the higher likelihood of being smited from PKers and Spindel's webs. Crossbows generally perform worse than most melee weapons, but offer some relative safety by being able to stay south of the entrance.

Inventory:

• Royal seed pod acts as a one-click emergency teleport from up to level 30 Wilderness
• Super restore potions can be used in place of blighted super restores
• Blighted manta ray or blighted anglerfish (if the player is 93 or higher hitpoints) for the rest, and multiple blighted karambwan

Calvar'ion.transport:
Calvar'ion resides in the Skeletal Tomb, the entrance of which is located north-east of Ferox Enclave in the Graveyard of Shadows. There is a small tombstone where the player may drop into his chambers, requiring a fee of 50,000 coins to enter which can be taken from the bank. This fee decreases by 10,000 for every kill for the player who deals the most damage. The fee is not required again on subsequent trips unless the fee is lost to another player.

To get there quickly, you can:

• Teleport to Graveyard of Shadows with the Carrallanger Teleport or using a teleport tablet.
• Teleport to the Ferox Enclave with the minigame teleport or a ring of dueling.
• Teleport to Corporeal Beast's Lair with a games necklace (Beware this exits into multi-wilderness).
Calvar'ion.requirements:
• 70+ Attack
• 70+ Strength
• 70+ Defence
• 75+ Hitpoints
• 70+ Prayer (for Piety)
Calvar'ion.intro:
Calvar'ion is a weaker variant of Vet'ion who is fought in the Skeletal Tomb, a singles-plus combat area in level 21 Wilderness. To enter Calvar'ion's lair, players must have completed the hard Wilderness diary, OR they must have a Vet'ion boss Slayer task (a skeleton Slayer task does not bypass the diary requirement).

Compared to Vet'ion, the fight is quicker and safer at the cost of an overall lower loot value.

Killing Calvar'ion counts as a Vet'ion alternative for a slayer Boss task, the elite Wilderness diary task, and the combat achievements.

Upon any player entering the tomb, all players inside will be unable to teleport for 3 ticks. This delay no longer occurs after completion of the hard Wilderness diary.
Calvar'ion.strategy:
• Calvar'ion resides in level 21 Wilderness where you may be attacked at any time during the fight. Do not bring any items that you are not willing to lose. Items like the Fighter torso and Infernal Cape are permanently lost if not protected beyond level 20 Wilderness unless a Trouver Parchment has been applied to them.

Calvar'ion is a level 264 skeleton boss. It is the weaker variant of Vet'ion, sharing similar mechanics and drops, but with reduced stats and in a singles-plus area. The hard wilderness diary is required to fight Calvar'ion.

Strategies:
Calvar'ion has the highest defensive capabilities of the three wilderness demi-bosses. However, his negative crush defence of -10 makes him fairly easy to hit.

All of Calvar'ion's attacks are AoE, meaning that if the player avoids them, they can essentially take no damage from his attacks. Calvar'ion will yell quotes whenever he attacks as a fairly easy and simple way to dodge the attacks. The shield bash is the only major concern due to its larger AoE, but is still otherwise easy to dodge since it is only used in melee distance.

When Calvar'ion reaches 50% of his health, he will summon skeletal hellhounds to assist him in battle. The hellhounds will channel immunity to Calvar'ion until they are killed. While they deal powerful melee hits, they are not durable, with both the normal and greater versions only having 30 health. Calvar'ion will yell a quote about their demise as an indicator that the immunity has been lifted.

When Calvar'ion reaches 0 health in his standard form, he will charge up lightning around him as he yells that the player defeat him a second time. The player can simply stand underneath him to avoid the reach of the lightning as normal. Calvar'ion will restore his health to full and increase his max hit and attack speed and any drained Defence levels will be restored.

Calvar'ion will move towards a player between attacks, so the player can manipulate him into walking towards the exit to his arena and keeping him there for the majority of the time. This is useful for players not relying on a "scout" outside the entrance to his tomb, as it ensures a fast escape, as getting teleblocked and frozen in the middle of the room will likely result in certain death from both the player killer's and Calvar'ion's attacks. It is still recommended to leave a secondary account if possible outside, as players cannot hop inside the tomb; and leaving one outside can sometimes cause other players to ignore whoever is inside.

Escaping in the event of a player killer should not be too much of a problem, as the exit leads players back to the Graveyard of Shadows, where there are plenty of escape opportunities with a well-timed bind or gap between them.

Equipment:
Always keep risk to a minimum in the Wilderness! - Whenever gearing, check your Items Kept on Death and enable "Wilderness beyond level 20" to make sure important items will not be lost.

Thanks to the powerful Salve (e) effect, as long as you bring a strong weapon and 2-3 other high-bonus items, your DPS will be very good with little risk. For a low-risk setup, a Neitiznot, myth cape, and d'hide/proselyte are perfect, risking less than one average boss kill's-worth. From there, Barrows gloves then Dragon boots make great upgrades to the Rune gloves and Climbing boots budget setup.

That being said however, due to the incredible passive effect of the Ursine/Viggora's chainmace stacking multiplicatively with the Salve's bonus, every extra bit of strength and accuracy bonus from equipment will noticeably increase DPS, provided you are willing to risk more. Some untradeables, such as a Fire cape, provide notable strength bonus for only some additional cost on death. However, some untradeables require a Trouver parchment, such as the Fighter torso, for the same strength bonus. These highly multiplied bonuses, coupled with the fact that it is possible to log out mid-fight here, make Calvar'ion the most feasible and rewarding of all the wilderness bosses to bring additional risk to. However, expensive armour slots are only worth bringing IF players are confident in their ability to escape PKers or teleport out in time.

Lastly, when figuring out your setup, keep in mind that some of these equipment recommendations, such as the Avernic defender and Infernal cape, are meant to maximize 4-item protection. These can easily be downgraded if they would be risked, or if the player is not using PK Skull Prevention. Due to the hazard of being smited and having the Protect Item prayer disabled in combat, untradeable items locked with Trouver parchments are particularly effective as the 4th item kept on death, in order. Again, whenever in doubt, "Items kept on death" will show exactly how items are kept, degraded, or lost.

Note: Due to the Salve bonus not stacking, fighting on a skeleton (or hellhound!) Slayer task with a Slayer helmet will not provide as high of an offensive bonus as the Salve amulet (e) will, and is not free to reclaim like the amulet.

Brimhaven Dungeon.title: Brimhaven Dungeon
Brimhaven Dungeon.transport:
The dungeon can be reached by sailing from East Ardougne to Brimhaven, for a fee of 30 coins or for free when using the Ring of Charos. Another sea route can be taken from Port Sarim to Musa Point, again requiring 30 coins or the Ring of Charos for a free trip. However, it is a much longer walk to the dungeon entrance from Musa Point than from Brimhaven. Alternatively, one can charter a ship to get to Brimhaven (the Port Sarim-Brimhaven charter ship ride costs 1,600 coins).

The nearest bank, although completion of the quest Shilo Village and 10 extra coins are required, is Shilo Village bank which can be reached by using Hajedy's cart. The Tzhaar City is also an option.

Teleportation is also practical:
• Teleport to House if the player-owned house is in Brimhaven or if using a scroll of redirection. This is by far the quickest way to get to the dungeon, and best to get items lost on death back if the player dies.
• Using a Tai bwo wannai teleport scroll and running west to the alternate entrance. This requires paying Banisoch a one-time fee of 5,000 trading sticks (GE: *5000), and takes players to the bronze dragon area.
• Spirit tree if the player has a fully grown spirit tree behind the Brimhaven Agility Arena.
• Amulet of glory to Karamja, then run west then south.
• Fairy ring code fairy ring CKR and then north to the dungeon.
• Ardougne Teleport, take Captain Barnaby's ship to Brimhaven (costs 30 coins). Walk south to the dungeon.

Catacombs of Kourend.title: Catacombs of Kourend
Catacombs of Kourend.transport:
The fastest way to the main entrance is through Xeric's talisman with the "Xeric's Heart" function, which teleports the player outside the statue of King Rada I, the Kourend Castle Teleport spell, which requires completion of Client of Kourend, or using a Ring of returning having set your respawn point to Kourend Castle, which can only be done after completion of A Kingdom Divided.

Alternate forms of transport include:

• Achievement diary cape to the Kourend & Kebos option, which puts the player next to Elise.
• A portal in the portal chamber or portal nexus of a player-owned house attuned to Kourend Castle.
• Using the Hosidius page(Lunch by the Lancalliums) in the Kharedst's memoirs; or using the Hosidius page in the Book of the Dead, after completion of A Kingdom Divided
• Fairy ring: fairy ring DJR.
• Fairy ring: fairy ring CIS.
• Games necklace to Wintertodt, then Lovakengj Minecart Network to Kingstown
• Rada's blessing to Kourend Woodland, then Lovakengj Minecart Network to Kingstown

Isle of Souls Dungeon.title: Isle of Souls Dungeon
Isle of Souls Dungeon.transport:
The dungeon can be reached by teleporting to fairy ring code fairy ring BJP on the northern coast of the isle, then running south-east.

Otherwise, players can use a Minigame Teleport to Soul Wars and run north-east. A dose of stamina potion drunk at the bank in the Soul Wars lobby will expire on reaching the deepest part of the dungeon.

Ancient Cavern.title: Ancient Cavern
Ancient Cavern.transport:
The whirlpool entrance to the Ancient Cavern is south of the Barbarian Outpost near Baxtorian Falls. Players can get there by walking west from Seers' Village, north from East Ardougne, or east from the Tree Gnome Stronghold. (From the stronghold, players with level 37 Agility can take the shortcut north-east of the Grand Tree; otherwise, the more round-about route through the stronghold's southern gate is necessary.)

Some teleports can be used to get near the whirlpool:

• A games necklace can teleport to the Barbarian Outpost. This is the quickest way to get to the whirlpool, as it is just south of the Outpost. Minigame Teleport to Barbarian Assault can also be used, requiring having gone through the tutorial for Barbarian Assault, and it can only be cast once every 20 minutes.
• Barbarian Teleport from the Lunar Spellbook. Teleporting between the Barbarian Outpost and Lunar Isle provides quick banking during Slayer tasks.
• Players with level 37 Agility can use the gnome gliders or spirit trees to travel to the Tree Gnome Stronghold and then use the shortcut north of the Grand Tree to get to the Baxtorian Falls lake. Additionally, players who have completed Monkey Madness II may use the royal seed pod to teleport to the Grand Tree.
• Players with level 99 Fishing can use the Fishing cape to teleport to Otto's Grotto and run to the whirlpool from there.

Lithkren Vault.title: Lithkren Vault
Lithkren Vault.transport:
Prior to unlocking the digsite pendant teleport after Dragon Slayer II:
• Use the digsite pendant to teleport to Fossil Island
• Mushtree transport to Mushroom Meadow
• Use the rowboat found south-west of the mushtree
• Climb up the stairs in the middle of island
• Climb down the south trapdoor
• Climb down the north stairs
• Keep going north until you are in the vault!

After Dragon Slayer II has been completed:
• Use a digsite pendant on the strange machine in Lithkren Vault (north of the rune dragons) to unlock the teleport.
• Afterwards, a digsite pendant can be used to immediately teleport outside the vault.

Abyssal Area.title: Abyssal Area
Abyssal Area.transport:
The Abyssal Area can be accessed by using the code fairy ring ALR in the fairy rings network (must have started Fairytale II - Cure a Queen). It is one of several areas in Abyssal Space, and as such is inhabited by the Abyss' denizens. Abyssal demons can also be found in this section of the Abyss; however, the demons here are rarely killed unless part of Konar quo Maten's Slayer assignment due to them being spread out and the other monsters being aggressive.

Since the Abyssal Area is the whole plane itself, players assigned abyssal demons in the Abyss may alternatively kill the Abyssal Sire.

Slayer Tower.title: Slayer Tower
Slayer Tower.transport:
• The Slayer ring can be used to teleport to the main entrance of the tower.
• Fairy ring code fairy ring CKS lands you in the west of Canifis, just south of the tower.
• The Salve Graveyard Teleport (requires Arceuus spellbook) will take you to the graveyard just south of the tower.
• The Kharyrll teleport (requires completion of Desert Treasure I) (spell, tablet, POH portal) will take the player to Canifis, where it is a short run north-west.
• Go west after casting Fenkenstrain's Castle Teleport or using the tablet.
• The player can use the Ectophial to teleport to Port Phasmatys, and walk from there.
• You can walk from Varrock or the digsite through Paterdomus, though this is by far the longest route.

Wilderness Slayer Cave.title: Wilderness Slayer Cave
Wilderness Slayer Cave.transport:
Entrances to the Wilderness Slayer Cave:
• Level 18 Wilderness — west of Larran's small chest
• Level 29 Wilderness — south-west of the Silk Chasm

Teleports near the cave's entrances:
• Games necklace offers a teleport to the Corporeal Beast — players can then run east to the level 18 entrance. This is usually the most convenient location for the southern entrance, as the Corporeal Beast cave is not classed as the Wilderness despite leading directly to it giving the player added security.
• Teleporting to Ferox Enclave and running east to the level 18 entrance. This is preferred by many players, as here they are able to bank and it is not a PvP area. It's also possible to restore health, prayer, and run energy here with the Pool of Refreshment. Be aware of others players, you may be more likely to be scouted if running from the Ferox Enclave.
• Teleporting to the Wilderness obelisk in level 19 wilderness by using an obelisk built in a player's Superior garden and running east to the level 18 entrance. This is more dangerous as it takes the player directly into the wilderness rather than a safe location.
• Using either the Carrallanger teleport or Carrallanger teleport tablet, leading to the Graveyard of Shadows and again running east to the level 18 entrance.
• Breaking a Wilderness crabs teleport tablet and running west to the level 29 entrance — This is not recommended not only due to the high cost of this teleport, but also because it teleports the player to level 33…

Iorwerth Dungeon.title: Iorwerth Dungeon
Iorwerth Dungeon.transport:
The Iorwerth Dungeon is a dungeon found in Prifddinas' Iorwerth district in the south-west part of the city, used by the Iorwerth Clan for training (). Players have access to the dungeon after the completion of Song of the Elves quest; Konar quo Maten will also begin to be able to assign them to slay monsters in the dungeon.

The dungeon consists of numerous rooms which contain a variety of Slayer monsters, as well as some traitorous Iorwerth Warriors camping out. The monsters in the dungeon do not require players to be on a Slayer task to be killed. A dwarf multicannon can be used in the dung

Mourner Tunnels.title: Mourner Tunnels
Mourner Tunnels.transport:
The Mourner Tunnels are located outside the basement of the Mourner Headquarters in the north-eastern part of West Ardougne. During Mourning's End Part II, the Head Mourner gives the player the new key, which can be used to enter the tunnels from the basement. Note that if the player is not wearing full mourner gear, the mourners in the basement will be aggressive.

After the completion of Mourning's End Part II, the slayer ring can be used to teleport directly into the tunnels, skipping the need to wear mourner gear or have the new key. After the completion of Song of the Elves, the mourners

Buccaneers' Laboratory.title: Buccaneers' Laboratory
Buccaneers' Laboratory.transport:
Buccaneers' Laboratory is located on Buccaneers' Haven, therefore requiring 76 Sailing to access.

The entire laboratory is a multicombat area, and a dwarven multicannon can be used here. There are a total of:

• 8 mutated bloodvelds to the north-east
• 5 hellhounds in the centre
• 11 shadow spiders to the south-east
• 2 skeletons to the west

The small key (Buccaneers' Haven) can be dug up by digging on the red ball in the second-most westward prison cell in the north-west of the laboratory.

Charred Dungeon.title: Charred Dungeon
Charred Dungeon.transport:
The Charred Dungeon is a dungeon containing several Slayer monsters and other resources, including lava strykewyrms. It is accessible by climbing down the dark hole on Charred Island, which requires level 60 Sailing to dock at. Rope is required when entering the dungeon the first time. However, there is a rope item spawn on the island so one doesn't need to be brought to the island.

If you teleport out of the dungeon, you will need to retrieve your boat via a Shipwright, use one of the boat teleportation spells, or be brought to the island by another player, as there is no other way to get to

God Wars Dungeon.title: God Wars Dungeon
God Wars Dungeon.transport:
God Wars Dungeon is located north of Trollheim. Accessing it requires partial completion of Troll Stronghold (defeating Dad) or full completion of the Easy Combat Achievements (in order to use the teleport on Ghommal's hilt 1) and either 60 Strength or 60 Agility. A rope is also required the first time. Without 61 Magic and the completion of Eadgar's Ruse (to be able to use the Trollheim Teleport), climbing boots are required each time. Strength potions may be used to boost past the boulder blocking the entrance, but cannot be used to reach the Bandos area. Before entering, items aligned to the gods should be equipped; otherwise, all the followers of those gods will be aggressive, which can quickly kill any player, as there are numerous monsters residing in the dungeon.

• If you have completed Eadgar's Ruse and have level 61 Magic, you may use the Trollheim Teleport (or the equivalent teleport tablet) to land on top of the mountain east of the Troll Stronghold. From there, make your way down to the base of the mountain and go north. There are Agility shortcuts from level 41 to 47 along the mountain that can be used to shorten the walk. If Making Friends with My Arm has been completed, a stony basalt can also be used as it teleports you to the Troll Stronghold, but this is a slightly longer run.
• Players can reach Trollheim without losing additional inventory slots for teleports. This requires using two scrolls of redirection on two house teletabs, creating two Trollheim…

Karuulm Slayer Dungeon.title: Karuulm Slayer Dungeon
Karuulm Slayer Dungeon.transport:
• Players can get there via the fairy ring fairy ring CIR. The mountain is a short walk north of this fairy ring.
• The skills necklace (The Farming Guild) will take you just south-west of Mount Karuulm.
• The Battlefront Teleport will take you just south-east of Mount Karuulm.
• Players may use Rada's blessing 3 or higher, which is unlocked after completing the Kourend & Kebos Hard Diary, to teleport straight to the dungeon using "Mount Karuulm" option. Rada's blessing 3 offers three daily teleports, while Rada's blessing 4 provides unlimited teleports.

Stronghold Slayer Dungeon.title: Stronghold Slayer Cave
Stronghold Slayer Dungeon.transport:
The entrance to the Stronghold Slayer Cave is located in the Gnome Stronghold near Nieve, who is located just south-west of the spirit tree. ()

There are various ways to get there:
• Use a Slayer ring to teleport directly to the entrance by Nieve.
• Use the gnome glider to Ta Quir Priw, which will take you to the Grand Tree. Exit the Grand Tree and run south-west to the entrance.
• Use the spirit tree to the Gnome Stronghold and run south-west.
• Use the necklace of passage to Teleport to 'Outpost' and then run north-east.
• Use the royal seed pod to Teleport to the Grand Tree, then run south-west.
• Use the Achievement diary cape to Teleport to Elder Gnome child, then run south-west.

Taverley Dungeon.title: Taverley Dungeon
Taverley Dungeon.transport:
The entrance to the dungeon is found south of Taverley and west of Falador. Ways of getting there include:

• Teleport to House if your house is in Taverley, or Taverley teleport tablet.
• Falador Teleport spell or tablet.
• Balloon transport system to Taverley.
• The south portal in the Wizards' Guild (requires 66 Magic) of Yanille brings the player to the Dark Wizards' Tower located just south.
• Skills necklace teleport to Crafting Guild, then run north.
• Burthorpe Games Room Minigame Teleport or games necklace to Burthorpe, then run south.
• Portal to the Heroes' Guild in the Myths' Guild, then run south.

Witchaven Dungeon.title: Witchaven Dungeon
Witchaven Dungeon.transport:
• Ardougne Teleport or the tablet then head east.
• Fairy ring code fairy ring BLR and head south.

Shayziens' Wall.title: Shayziens' Wall
Shayziens' Wall.transport:
Shayziens' Wall, also known as the Shayzien Outpost, is a wall located west of Shayzien. Immediately to the west of the wall, on the other side of the river, are two outposts that serve as a first line of defence against the lizardmen. Fires can be found at both of the outposts.

West of this wall is the Lizardman Settlement, home to hostile lizardmen, including brutes and shamans, who can poison unprepared players.

Lizardman Settlement.title: Lizardman Settlement
Lizardman Settlement.transport:
The Lizardman Settlement can be reached by various methods:
